title: Puck world projection (puck.world.projection.v1)
description: puck.world.projection.v1 — what an authority hands a peer holding the Presentation tier. A separate versioned document rather than a WorldDefinition with sections nulled out: a partial definition either refuses at WorldDefinitionValidator or misreports what it carries. This type's member list is the disclosure decision: a section that must not leave an authority below the replica tier has no member here. Absent by construction: rules, grants, state, admission, generation, generators, groups, properties, addons, storage, host, authoring, identity, inputHold, targetRegisters, bodyMotionPrograms, portals, every kit's producers/actions (see WorldProjectedKit), and every machine's memory, contentFolders and preferFolderDefault (see WorldProjectedMachine). Adjacencies, Destinations, References, and Interactions cross because TryDeriveOverlap reads them from both sides of a seam and must derive the same depth on each; withholding one side's inputs desymmetrizes it silently. Metadata crosses in reduced form: WorldProjectedMetadata carries title/description only — a world's authored name and blurb are harmless to a presentation-tier peer. authors, tags, and custom never cross; custom in particular is an unbounded author scratch bag that may hold notes never meant to leave the authority.

provenance.description: Who composed this, from what, at which revision and tier.

authority.description: The composing authority's own addressable namespace (a host.authority endpoint, or the process-local boot namespace for an in-process authority).

documentId.description: The source document's stable id, when it carries one.

revision.description: The source document's revision at composition.

tier.description: The tier this projection was composed at — always Presentation today, since Replica sends the definition verbatim and Frames sends no document at all.
tier.title: WorldDisclosureTier

x-enumDescriptions.Presentation: A puck.world.projection.v1 document — what a visitor's client needs to render and be embodied. The wire default: a peer whose admission entry authors no tier receives this.
x-enumDescriptions.Replica: The whole puck.world.definition.v1 document, verbatim — the sanctioned download. Authored explicitly, never defaulted into.

moveSpeed.description: Locomotion speed in world units per second — the profileless fallback a stand-in advances on (a seated player whose identity CLAIMS a rate reads that claim instead, live, so identity.motion stays real-time; an identity claiming none rides the kit's own rate).

turnSpeed.description: Turn speed in radians per second (the profileless fallback counterpart to MoveSpeed).

maxSmoothError.description: The largest server-correction position error, in world units, that presentation may ease instead of snapping.

items.description: One named spawn pose available to seats and population policies.

id.description: The stable spawn name, unique within the definition.

yawDegrees.description: The spawn yaw about +Y, in degrees.

items.title: WorldSpawnPoint

renderScale.description: The scalar boot render-scale ceiling in [0.125, 1].

upscaleSharpness.description: The boot reconstruction sharpness: the spatial resolve's blend (0 bilinear .. 1 Catmull-Rom) and the strength of the sharpen a temporally resolved view gets at its rect's own extent.

temporal.description: Whether the world's own views boot reconstructing over time (world.temporal): each jitters its samples and resolves them over its history, native or reduced. The world's own views include every layout slot that names a camera; the camera views screens film and session views never do.

dynamicResolution.description: Whether views boot adapting their grids (world.render-scale auto). Saved per-view quality and tier rows supply their floors. A native ceiling is lowered to three-quarter while adaptation is enabled, since a native view reconstructs nothing.

lighting.description: The scene's direct lights and curvature shading. Optional, and every field within it is optional individually — an absent section, or an absent field within it, resolves to SdfFrame's pinned default for that field, so a world renders unchanged until it authors one.

lights.description: The lights, at most SdfLights.MaxLights, in authored order; each view shades only those that can reach what it shows (SdfLightSelection). Shadow-capable directionals compete for the quality row's shadow slots by mode and tick-resolved luminance.

curvature.description: The stylized curvature enrichment — cavity darkening, curvature rim light, and an ink outline. Optional; absent (and all-zero) shades exactly as a world that declares none.

clock.description: The clock the section's keys read, by name in the timeline section. Required with Keys and refused without them.

keys.description: The section's keys, ascending in time. A field a key states is keyed on Clock through the keys that state it, blended by the field's type and eased by each key's ease; a field no key states keeps its authored value.

items.description: One key of Keys: a partial record of the section at one time.

at.description: Where on the section's clock the key sits, in the clock's span units, in [0, span).

ease.description: How time eases from this key to the next key that states each field. Absent is Linear.

lights.description: The lights this key moves, by name: each the same kind as the light of that name, stating only the fields it moves. A light's name and shadowing are structure, which a key never states.

curvature.description: The curvature fields this key moves.

items.title: WorldRenderLightingKey

lighting.title: WorldRenderLighting

sky.description: The repeatable sky-layer stack. Optional; an absent section renders the default look, the two-stop gradient SdfSky starts from, as data the kernels read like any authored sky.

clock.description: The clock the section's keys read, by name in the timeline section. Required with Keys and refused without them.

keys.description: The section's keys, ascending in time. A field a key states is keyed on Clock through the keys that state it; a field no key states keeps its authored value.

items.description: One key of Keys: a partial record of the sky at one time.

at.description: Where on the section's clock the key sits, in the clock's span units, in [0, span).

ease.description: How time eases from this key to the next key that states each field. Absent is Linear.

layers.description: The layers this key moves, by name: each the same kind as the layer of that name, stating only the fields it moves. A gradient states every stop the layer has, in order. Counts, seeds, kinds, a layer's name, blend, mask, visibility, tier and clock and the sun disc's light are structure, which a key never states.

items.title: WorldRenderSkyKey

frame.description: Which way is up for the sky. Absent is world +y.

up.description: The sky's up direction in world space, any nonzero length. Absent is world +y.

frame.title: WorldRenderSkyFrame

sky.title: WorldRenderSky

environment.description: The sky's bindable ambient and reflection gains, each defaulting to one. Zero disables that lighting contribution.

ambient.description: The diffuse irradiance gain. Absent is one; zero disables harmonic lighting.

reflection.description: The reflection gain. Absent is one; zero disables reflection lookups.

environment.title: WorldRenderEnvironment

atmosphere.description: Fog, height fog, haze and a medium between the camera and what it sees. An absent section renders the default fog; an authored section contains exactly the kinds it states.

fog.description: The fog: an exponential medium, level or thinning with height. Absent is no fog.

density.description: The density per world unit, at the base when Height is authored. Absent is the default look's density.

color.description: BindableColor's grammar: the colour the fog in-scatters. Absent is the sky in the pixel's direction, so a distant surface fades into the horizon behind it.

height.description: The height fog's profile. Absent is a fog alike at every height.

luminance.description: The luminance, in nits, an authored Color of one in-scatters at. Absent is SdfSky.DefaultLuminance; a fog that reads the sky takes the sky's own.

fog.title: WorldRenderFog

haze.description: The haze: aerial perspective that scatters the sky and the light of the bodies that cast light, brightest toward them. Absent is no haze.

amount.description: The share of the light the haze takes over the far distance, in [0, 0.99]. Absent is zero, which draws none.

anisotropy.description: The Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy of its scattering toward the bodies, in [0, 0.9]: zero scatters alike in every direction. Absent is SdfAtmosphere.DefaultHazeAnisotropy.

height.description: The haze's height profile, the amount taken at its base. Absent is a haze alike at every height.

haze.title: WorldRenderHaze

medium.description: The medium: water below a level surface, with its own extinction and colour. Absent is no medium.

surface.description: The surface's height. Absent is zero.

extinction.description: The extinction per world unit below the surface. Absent is SdfAtmosphere.DefaultMediumExtinction.

color.description: BindableColor's grammar: the colour the medium in-scatters, which a deep view through it reaches. Absent is SdfAtmosphere.DefaultMediumColor.

luminance.description: The luminance, in nits, a Color of one in-scatters at. Absent is SdfSky.DefaultLuminance.

medium.title: WorldRenderMedium

atmosphere.title: WorldRenderAtmosphere

tone.description: The display transform every view of the world puts its exposed scene light through before the view's display pass encodes it for the display (WorldToneCurve). The letterbox color, every pane (display-referred) and the HUD are never toned. Optional; absent applies no curve.

peak.description: The value the shoulder rolls into.

linearStart.description: The exposed value where the toe gives way to the linear section.

linearLength.description: The share of the range above LinearStart the linear section spans.

toe.description: The toe's power: above one it darkens the shadows, below one it lifts them.

tone.title: WorldToneCurve

farDistance.description: The far distance in world units: the depth at which every view's geometry ends — the mesh raster's far plane, the reach of the bake and the indirect volume, and the depth the fog and depth ramps are measured against. Geometry beyond it is never drawn, so an infinite plane ends on a visible horizon curve at this depth unless the atmosphere absorbs it (render.atmosphere). Optional; absent resolves to the engine's pinned 40. Must lie within [MinFarDistance, MaxFarDistance]. Re-read on every definition revision (a world.row.set render lands on the next frame); world.budget echoes it with its derived costs.

shadowLights.description: The boot number of held shadow slots, from 0 through 4; one keeps the pinned sun selected.

shadowFadeSlots.description: The boot number of additional shadow handoff slots, from 0 through 2.

shadowFadeTicks.description: The boot length of a shadow handoff in delivered ticks; zero selects instant changes.

shadowOverflow.description: How a crossing proceeds when its handoff capacity is occupied.
shadowOverflow.title: WorldShadowOverflow

skyQuality.description: The sky's boot quality tier (world.sky-quality): a layer below it writes no entry, and below High each kind draws its reduced form.
skyQuality.title: WorldSkyTier

indirect.description: The world's diffuse indirect-light tier, sources and application.

sources.description: Bindable source gains in [0, 1]; absent gains are one.

sky.description: Physical sky radiance at world exits.

feedback.description: Reflected preceding-sweep radiance gain, once per bounce.

sources.title: WorldRenderIndirectSources

bounces.description: Feedback sweeps after the direct sweep, capped by the selected tier. Absent uses that tier's limit.

apply.description: Bindable receiver-only controls. They do not change the traced radiance.

contact.description: How much existing ambient occlusion dims indirect diffuse, zero disabling that attenuation.

apply.title: WorldRenderIndirectApply

tier.description: The boot tier, Medium by default. The live session lever and selected quality preset override it.
tier.title: SdfIndirectTier

x-enumDescriptions.Off: No indirect light: the coarse volume occludes, and none of its light is applied.

budget.description: The irradiance work each second grants the volume and the lighting age it reports past; absent bounds nothing.

lightingGrid.description: Fixed angular and radiometric grids for indirect captures; absent leaves them continuous.

directionDegrees.description: Directional azimuth and elevation step in degrees, from zero through 180.

radiance.description: Fractional radiance step per power-of-two range, from zero through one.

lightingGrid.title: WorldRenderIndirectLightingGrid

indirect.title: WorldRenderIndirect

skyFieldScale.description: The boot sky field grid fraction, one or one half, independent of view render scale.

exposure.description: The camera exposure each view maps the luminance it shades to the display by, before the tone curve. Absent is a manual exposure at SdfExposure.DefaultEv100, a sunlit day's.

mode.description: Manual or automatic. Absent is manual.
mode.title: SdfExposureMode

x-enumDescriptions.Auto: The EV100 the view's own image meters (Meter), less the compensation, held within the bounds, and eased toward over the adaptation time once its target leaves the dead band.

ev100.description: The manual exposure value at ISO 100, in [−6, 20]: about 15 for a sunlit day, 7 for a lit room, 3 for a dim one. An automatic exposure starts there and holds it while its meter has no reading. Absent is SdfExposure.DefaultEv100, or with automatic exposure the middle of its bounds.

minimum.description: The lowest EV100 an automatic exposure adapts to: the darkest scene it brightens. In [−6, 20]; absent is −6.

maximum.description: The highest EV100 an automatic exposure adapts to, at or above Minimum. In [−6, 20]; absent is 20.

compensation.description: The stops an automatic exposure brightens the metered image by, in [−10, 10]. Absent is zero.

adaptation.description: The time constant an automatic exposure eases toward its meter with, in seconds, in [0, 60]; zero follows the meter at once. Absent is SdfExposure.DefaultAdaptation.

local.description: The share of the local adaptation, in [0, 1]: how far each surface's exposure moves from the view's toward what its own illumination would meter against the view's image meter, within six stops either way, so a dim ceiling beside a sunlit window lifts and the sunlit ground seen through the window compresses, as the eye adapts across a scene. Zero exposes the whole view alike; absent is zero. Read only with an automatic exposure.

hold.description: A bindable EV100 that pins the exposure while it is above zero, in [0, 20]: every view then renders manual at that value with no local adaptation, whatever Mode and the bounds say, and zero (the value of an unbound or released hold) leaves the authored exposure exactly as it was. The bounds still size each point and spot light's range, so a hold never changes the lights the volume traces. Absent is no hold.

band.description: The automatic exposure's dead band, in stops, in [0, 4]: the exposure holds while the meter reads within this far of the reading it last settled on, and follows the meter once a reading leaves the band. Absent is zero, which follows every change.

low.description: The percentile, in [0, 1), below which the image meter leaves the darkest pixels out. Bindable, so a world keys it on a view clock of the viewer's height: a camera climbing into a black sky leaves the void out of its meter and exposes what the sun lights. Absent is zero.

high.description: The percentile, above Low and at most one, above which the image meter leaves the brightest pixels out. Absent is one.

center.description: How far the image meter weights the image toward its centre, in [0, 1]: a pixel counts 1 − Center · r², r its distance from the centre over the half diagonal. Absent is zero, every pixel alike.

exposure.title: WorldRenderExposure

toon.description: The world's default cel style (ToonStyleDocument), which every material that authors no style of its own takes: its ink, and the styled mark the live world.toon off suppresses with the Shade default it inks. On unless it says enabled: false; absent is off.

bloom.description: Optional camera scatter. Absent is off.

shadowCoverage.description: How far the key light's shadow cascades reach (WorldRenderShadowCoverage). Absent keeps the engine's 16 m near, 120 m far and 200 m caster reach; world.budget prints the coverage with each cascade's texel.

near.description: The depth from the eye the near cascade covers, positive and below the far reach (16 when absent).

far.description: The depth from the eye the far cascade covers, at most the far distance it is clipped to (120 when absent).

casters.description: How far past a cascade toward the light a caster may stand and still shadow it (200 when absent).

shadowCoverage.title: WorldRenderShadowCoverage

lanes.description: The world's render lanes: up to four bindable scalars (a literal, a state.<row> binding, or keys on a clock), resolved at each frame's presented tick and read by every surface and volume as render lanes 4 to 7 (SdfLanes), so a static placement sharing one baked mesh follows world state without a slot. Absent or a missing entry reads zero; world.lighting echoes them as authored.

shade.description: The default shading program inherited by materials without their own.

devices.description: The world's device profiles (WorldDeviceProfile): for each graphics device, the quality table it runs and the memory it may use. The engine selects one by the adapter it runs on and by name (world.device-profile). Absent authors none, and no cap applies.

items.description: One graphics device's profile: the quality table it runs and the memory it may use. A profile is data a world (the standard package, for the shipped devices) authors in render.devices; the engine selects one by the adapter it runs on (Select) or by name, applies its table through the same levers world.quality writes, and admits memory against its bars. No device name or figure is engine code.

name.description: The profile's name, unique within the world, which world.device-profile and a benchmark run select by.

match.description: The text the driver's adapter name must contain, ignoring case, for the engine to select the profile on that adapter.

quality.description: The quality tier the profile runs as (Names): the world's render preset of that tier is its table unless Table authors the device's own, and the tier's indirect default applies where the table names none.
quality.title: QualityTier

deviceMemoryMiB.description: The most device memory the process admits on a discrete adapter, in mebibytes, where that is below the adapter's own budget less a tenth; absent leaves the device pool at the adapter's reading.

hostMemoryMiB.description: The most host memory the process admits, in mebibytes, where that is below the machine's budget; absent leaves it. A unified-memory device states its one bar here, since its device segments lie in the host pool.

table.description: The device's own quality table: the levers it runs in place of the world's render preset of Quality, so each device meets its bar by the path it enables (its render scale, its distant shadow map's texels, its indirect tier, which sizes the irradiance volume and its caches). Absent runs the tier's preset.

frameBar.description: The device's frame bar: the window size its frame time is judged at and the rate it must hold there. A host started with --frame-bar opens its window at this size, and a benchmark run judges its iterations against this rate's period. Absent where the world states no bar for the device.

width.description: The window's client width in pixels.

height.description: The window's client height in pixels.

hertz.description: The presented frames a second the device must hold at that size.

frameBar.title: WorldFrameBar

items.title: WorldDeviceProfile

nested.description: What a nested view gives up at each presented size (WorldNestedViewQuality). Absent gives up nothing.

rayQueries.description: Whether the indirect volume's background rays (its probe trace, the relight's shadow rays and the camera sample) boot taking the device's ray hardware where it has it, through the scene's acceleration structures (world.rays). The software walk answers the same hits wherever it is off or the device has none. Absent is off.

distantShadows.description: The distant shadow map the world boots drawing past the far cascade (WorldDistantShadows); a quality preset's row replaces it. Absent draws none.

farShadows.description: How often the world boots refreshing the far shadow cascade (WorldFarShadows); a quality preset's row replaces it. Absent refreshes it every frame.

viewsRate.description: The maximum shared shading footprint and classification tile size. Absent shades every pixel.

items.description: One diegetic screen in the world — a screen slab emitted by SdfProgramBuilder whose lit face samples a bound source (or shades as dark glass when unbound). The frame (Origin/Right/ Up + HalfWidth/HalfHeight) is the sampled surface frame and must match the slab's placement; the frame source bakes the geometry translate from it.

index.description: The engine screen-surface index (0..MaxScreenSurfaces−1) this slab declares — the key the source/light providers bind under.

origin.description: The front face's world-space center (the sampled surface origin); the geometry center sits one HalfDepth behind it along the face normal.

right.description: The unit world axis the sampled U increases along (the slab's local +X in world space). Must be orthogonal to Up: the client derives the slab's orientation and UV frame from the pair while the server's collider projects the half-extents onto it, so a skewed pair would render and collide as different solids.

up.description: The unit world axis the sampled V increases against — V = 0 at the top (the slab's local +Y in world space).

halfWidth.description: The face half-width (the slab's local X half-extent).

halfHeight.description: The face half-height (the slab's local Y half-extent).

halfDepth.description: The slab's local Z half-extent (its thickness behind the face).

source.description: The signal the lit face carries.

engageable.description: Whether a player may engage this screen.

engageRadius.description: The world-unit radius a player must be inside to engage (meaningful only when Engageable). Validated finite and non-negative.

autoInsert.description: When set, engaging the screen first boots the selected magazine entry (the "walk over, press the button, the screen lights" gesture), so the interaction is one act rather than an insert then an engage.

engageChannel.description: The world-event channel whose arrival on a body engages this screen, or null (the default) for a route that does not answer gestures. The author chooses this name freely; the engine never special-cases a spelling. Omitted from the wire when null.

cycleChannel.description: Same, for advancing the magazine selector. Omitted from the wire when null.

channels.description: The declared channel names an application onto this screen reaches — a masked-out channel keeps flowing to the source body's own pose (when the own-body application is retained) but never reaches this screen. null (the default) reaches every declared channel. Omitted from the wire when null.

kit.description: The Name whose Pad map an application onto this screen wears, or null for the engine's default pad map. The named kit must carry a pad map — refused by name otherwise. Omitted from the wire when null.

input.description: Where a pointer hit on the screen's source goes: Presentation for hover and highlight, or Simulation for a pointer ray mapped in fixed point from this row, which a $pointer: rule read sees and which aims the screen machine's light gun for a seat applied to the screen (WorldScreenMappings). Passthrough is refused by name: host passthrough exists only for a source the local user opened on their own machine, and a world document can never create one or send it input. null (the default) is Presentation. Omitted from the wire when null.
input.title: SourceDestination

port.description: The machine input port, by the provider's port name (controls-2), that a seat engaged on this screen drives; the machine's other ports hold neutral input unless another screen routes to them. null (the default) resolves only a machine with a sole input port, and a screen showing a machine with several is refused by name until its route names one. Omitted from the wire when null.

display.description: How the window shows this screen to a seat engaged on it once its camera has framed the picture: what surrounds the matte (WorldScreenDisplay). null (the default) is Neutral: a black matte. Omitted from the wire when null.

fill.description: The matte colour around the framed picture, as #RRGGBB, or null for black.

display.title: WorldScreenDisplay

padPointer.description: How a local pad's sticks drive the pointer over this screen's framed picture while a seat engaged on it frames a window capture (WorldScreenPadPointer). Only an engageable screen showing a window capture may author it. null (the default) moves and scrolls nothing from a stick; a pad's buttons still click and press keys. Omitted from the wire when null.

speed.description: The pointer's speed at full deflection before any boost, in heights of the framed picture per second. Positive.

curve.description: The exponent the deflection's length is raised to; 1 is a linear response. At least 1.

boost.description: The speed's multiplier once a deflection has been held for RampSeconds, rising linearly from 1 while it is held and back to 1 once the stick rests. At least 1.

rampSeconds.description: How long a held deflection takes to reach Boost; 0 applies it at once. Non-negative.

scrollSpeed.description: The wheel's speed at full deflection of the scrolling stick, in wheel notches per second, its deflection raised to Curve too. Non-negative; 0 scrolls nothing.

padPointer.title: WorldScreenPadPointer

solid.description: The screen slab's solidity facet (a box collider derived from the slab's oriented frame + Margin by Server.WorldColliderSet), or null for a decorative screen. Omitted from the wire when null.

magazine.description: The per-screen source magazine (the cycle primitive), or null for a screen with no magazine — nothing to cycle. Omitted from the wire when null — the whole-row UpsertScreen carries it for free, so no new mutation kind is needed.

entries.description: The ordered source list (at least one entry).

items.description: The signal carried by a WorldScreen's lit face. A source declares which provider feeds a slot; the engine resolves and samples it. The $type string is the JSON discriminator; a new source kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.
items.title: WorldScreenSource

selected.description: The 0-based entry the selector starts on (what screen.select advances from), not what the screen boots showing — a screen always wakes on its declared Source (the one-live-console ceiling depends on this). Live selection drifts from this and is folded back by world.save (see Puck.World.Server.WorldSessionCapture).

wrap.description: Whether advancing past the last entry returns to the first (the arcade cabinet's wrapping cycle); when false the selector clamps at both ends.

magazine.title: WorldScreenMagazine

filter.description: How the face samples its source's image: Nearest, the default, keeps each source pixel crisp, as an emulator or a pixel-art source wants; Linear blends between source pixels, as a camera or a desktop capture wants. The screen's mapping carries it, and a hit maps to the same source pixel under either. Omitted from the wire when Nearest.
filter.title: GpuSamplerFilter

luminance.description: The display's peak luminance, in nits: a white picture shows at it, and the light the picture casts into the room scales with it. A CRT television shows about 100 to 200, a handheld's unlit panel far less, a desktop monitor about 250. In (0, SdfScreenEmission.MaxLuminance]; absent is SdfScreenEmission.DefaultLuminance. A screen whose source is a window onto another world shows that world's own luminance whatever this says.

carry.description: The body that carries the screen's picture while it holds the device (see WorldScreenCarry), or null for a screen that stays where it is authored. Omitted from the wire when null.

look.description: The look row whose wearer carries the picture; a creation look.

pose.description: The look's Poses frame that holds while the body carries it.

shape.description: The name of the ungrouped box in the look's creation that shows the picture.

camera.description: The name of a Cameras row whose rig frames the body holding the device, or null for none (a seat engaged on the carried screen then starts on the framed picture, as at any device). The rig runs against an anchor at the picture's front face whose axes are the picture's: +X its right, +Y its up and +Z its normal, toward the body looking at it (offset and lookAt without worldAxes read in those axes).

carry.title: WorldScreenCarry

material.description: The id of the screen material (WorldScreenMaterial, the document's screenMaterials) the face draws its picture through, or null for none: the picture as its source made it, filling the face. Refused on a window, which is an opening rather than a display. Omitted from the wire when null.

items.title: WorldScreen

screenMaterials.description: The screen materials the screens and the placements' creation faces name by id, so a presentation peer draws each display through the treatment its authority authored.

items.description: An authored screen material: how a display's face draws its picture through the screen shading's display treatment, a row of the document's screenMaterials that screens and creation faces name by Id. The treatment models a display's own pixel structure over the picture, which always fills the face: a darkening between source rows, coloured stripes across each source column, a radial vignette, a glint at grazing angles, and the face's rounded, softened edge. Every term is the author's (the standard package authors a cathode-ray tube, worlds/standard/skin.puck); zero turns a term off, and a view's screen fidelity fades the whole treatment out as a seat frames the screen. Presentation only: a material never moves the mapping a pointer hit takes.

id.description: The id screens and faces name the material by; unique among the document's materials.

scanlines.description: How dark the gap between source rows draws, in [0, 1]: one source row a cosine period.

subpixelStripes.description: How strong the red, green and blue stripes across each source column draw, in [0, 1].

vignette.description: How much the face darkens toward its corners, in [0, 1].

glint.description: How bright the glass's rim glint at grazing view angles adds, in [0, 1].

glintPower.description: How tightly the glint hugs grazing angles: the exponent of one minus the view cosine, positive.

cornerRadius.description: The face's corner rounding, as a fraction of the face, in [0, 0.5).

edgeSoftness.description: The width over which the face's edge fades to black, as a fraction of the face, in [0, 0.5).

items.title: WorldScreenMaterial

items.description: One placeable camera composed from a reference frame, local motion, framing policy, lens, and render target.

name.description: The camera's stable name — the handle a View screen / layout slot samples by.

rig.description: The independent local motion, aim, and lens axes.

name.description: The stable name a Blend op selects this program by.

operations.description: The selected ops, in authored evaluation order.

bloom.description: The camera's optical scatter override; absent inherits the world.

rig.title: WorldCameraProgram

renderWidth.description: The offscreen render width in pixels.

renderHeight.description: The offscreen render height in pixels.

anchor.description: What the camera rides, or null for the world reference frame (or for Anchors to decide).

anchors.description: Ranked anchor candidates, first holding wins each frame — a portrait camera that rides the speaking character while they speak and the seat's own avatar otherwise. Refused beside Anchor; a single unconditional anchor is Anchor.

items.description: One ranked anchor candidate of a WorldCamera: the anchor the camera rides while When holds. Candidates are walked in authored order every frame and the first holding one wins; a null predicate always holds, so the last row is the default.

anchor.description: What the camera rides while this candidate wins.

when.description: The condition, evaluated for the seat the view is resolved for.

items.title: WorldCameraAnchorCandidate
WorldCamera

population.description: The population defaults — capacity, distribution, seat activation.

items.description: Whether a local seat activates automatically at boot (Eager) or waits for a claim (OnDemand) — the per-seat authored policy SeatActivation declares. Both doors converge on the identical Server.WorldPopulation.ActivateSeat call through the same SessionRequest.Join/WorldServer.ApplySession session-join seam regardless of which policy admitted the seat — a seat activated on demand (player.join, or a controller's own hot-plug first touch via Client.PlayerRoster.ResolveDeviceSlot) is indistinguishable from one activated at boot the instant it is active.
items.title: SeatActivationPolicy

x-enumDescriptions.Eager: The seat's body is minted at boot, mirroring a session join for it immediately — the only policy seat 0 (player 1) may declare, since a session always needs a first player.
x-enumDescriptions.OnDemand: The seat stays empty at boot; its body is minted the first time something claims it.

mode.description: Which bodies an observer is delivered.
mode.title: WorldObserverDisclosureMode

x-enumDescriptions.All: Every active body. The default, and what every world authoring no policy delivers.
x-enumDescriptions.Radius: Only bodies within Radius metres of the observer's own body, plus that body itself. An observer with no body of its own is delivered nothing.
x-enumDescriptions.SelfOnly: Only the observer's own body. An observer with no body of its own is delivered nothing.

radius.description: The disclosure radius in metres for Radius; authored only for that mode.

updateSeconds.description: The minimum interval between remote projection snapshots. Zero requests every authority tick; the default is 0.03 seconds (30 Hz on the standard 240 Hz authority after whole-step quantization). Local in-process sinks are unaffected.

population.title: WorldBodiesDefaults

items.description: One authored identity used to seed an owned world.

name.description: The display name.

items.title: WorldIdentitySeed

yawSensitivity.description: The yaw response in radians per pixel of raw pointer motion along the X axis.

pitchSensitivity.description: The pitch response in radians per pixel of raw pointer motion along the Y axis.

invertYaw.description: Whether the final semantic yaw response (pointer, stick, and gyro) is inverted.

invertPitch.description: Whether the final semantic pitch response (pointer, stick, and gyro) is inverted.

stickLookRate.description: The look stick's yaw/pitch rate in radians per second at full deflection.

gyro.description: The optional full-axis gyro projection. Absent resolves to None.

scale.description: The dimensionless multiplier applied after projection.

deadZone.description: Gets the independent X/Y/Z dead zones in radians per second; zero where none is authored.

invertX.description: Whether the physical X angular-velocity axis is inverted before projection.

invertY.description: Whether the physical Y angular-velocity axis is inverted before projection.

invertZ.description: Whether the physical Z angular-velocity axis is inverted before projection.

yaw.description: Gets the X/Y/Z projection weights producing semantic look-right angular velocity; zero where none is authored.

pitch.description: Gets the X/Y/Z projection weights producing semantic look-up angular velocity; zero where none is authored.

gyro.title: WorldSeatGyro

autoFirstPerson.description: The player's automatic pull-in choice; null inherits the author's default.

channels.description: The channel table — the ordinal vocabulary an intent image is addressed in.

items.description: One row of the world's channel table — the intent vector's declared vocabulary (see PlayerIntent). The consumer is exactly one of Role (an engine motion channel, claimable by at most one channel) or Composition (a kit composition trigger, bound — or left inert — per kit via Actions).

name.description: The channel's unique, non-empty name — the vocabulary key every binding, body.press, kit Actions entry, and the addon wire resolve against.

shape.description: The declared value shape: bipolar [-1, 1], unipolar [0, 1], or binary.
shape.title: ChannelShape

x-enumDescriptions.Binary: A bit: exactly {0, 1} once quantized. Edges derive from the value crossing the channel's threshold against the previous sub-step (see Puck.World.Server.WorldBody's per-channel edge tracking) — never carried.
x-enumDescriptions.Relative: A Q32.32 displacement accumulated since the preceding input submission, consumed once.
x-enumDescriptions.Text: Ordered Unicode scalar events with no held value or numeric/button storage.

role.description: The engine motion role this channel claims, or null for a composition channel.
role.title: ChannelRole

x-enumDescriptions.MoveStrafe: Motion along the body's right, +1 right / -1 left.
x-enumDescriptions.Turn: The heading turn rate, +1 left (counter-clockwise about the body's up) / -1 right. The grounded program integrates it into the heading scalar the attitude derives from; the free program reads it as the yaw rate beside Pitch/Roll.
x-enumDescriptions.MoveUp: Motion along the body's up, +1 up / -1 down.
x-enumDescriptions.Pitch: Pitch rate about the body's right, +1 nose-up / -1 nose-down.
x-enumDescriptions.Roll: Roll rate about the body's forward axis, +1 banks left (the body's right rises) / -1 right.
x-enumDescriptions.FaceX: The world +X component of a commanded facing direction — with FaceY and FaceZ a world-frame vector; nonzero, it is the direction the body faces this tick, ahead of movement-facing. All zero commands nothing.
x-enumDescriptions.FaceY: The world +Y (up) component of a commanded facing direction. Carried so the commanded facing rides as a whole vector; no motion op reads it yet — the yaw snap takes its angle from the planar pair alone.
x-enumDescriptions.FaceZ: The world +Z component of a commanded facing direction (see FaceX).
x-enumDescriptions.MoveX: The world +X component of a commanded movement direction — with MoveY and MoveZ a full world-frame vector. Claimed, it supersedes the MoveAdvance/MoveStrafe pair whenever it is nonzero.
x-enumDescriptions.MoveY: The world +Y component of a commanded movement direction (see MoveX).
x-enumDescriptions.MoveZ: The world +Z component of a commanded movement direction (see MoveX).

composition.description: Whether this channel is a kit-composition trigger. Exactly one of Role or this must be set.

threshold.description: The binary crossing threshold in [0, 1] raw units (binary channels only); null takes DefaultBinaryThreshold (One/2).

frame.description: What the MoveAdvance/MoveStrafe pair is relative to when a binding row folds into it (see ChannelFrame); the two roles must declare the same frame, and every other channel leaves it at World. Omitted from a saved document at that default.
frame.title: ChannelFrame

x-enumDescriptions.World: Raw world axes — what the sim reads; the kit's own MoveFrame/FacingSnap decide the rest.
x-enumDescriptions.Camera: Relative to the seat's camera yaw — latched the tick movement begins, so the camera may orbit mid-run without steering — and the body's HEADING turns to the way it moves (the seat composes the direction into the FaceX/FaceZ roles) — the third-person scheme.
x-enumDescriptions.Heading: Relative to the body's own heading, which the Turn role steers and movement never turns — the keyboard scheme: strafe sidesteps (the drawn attitude angling toward the travel under the kit's facing snap, the heading intact), turn turns, the camera is its own control.

relative.description: Required units, sensitivity and limit for Relative channels; absent on levels.

unit.description: An authored unit name shared by producers and consumers.

sensitivity.description: Units per device sample, applied before host quantization.

maximumPerStep.description: The positive absolute displacement limit in authored units.

relative.title: WorldRelativeChannel

items.title: WorldChannel

items.description: One kit as a visitor's client sees it — the embodiment facts (which motion tuning a body wears, what shape it occupies, whether it depenetrates). The projection document's own row type, not a WorldKit with holes: it carries no member for the kit's producers/actions, which are the world's game logic and are read only by the authority that runs them.

name.description: The kit's name — the identity a placement/assignment row addresses.

bodyMotionProgram.description: The program name the destination advances this kit on. A name only; the bodyMotionPrograms section itself never crosses below the replica tier.

motion.description: The kit's motion tuning, which is what decides how a client interpolates and frames a body wearing it.

value.description: Locomotion speed in world units per second — the profileless fallback a stand-in advances on (a seated player reads its live profile's speed instead, so identity.motion stays real-time).

envelope.description: The inclusive bound a seated player's live profile speed (and the profileless Value fallback) is clamped to at seat time, or null (the default) for no bound — a feel-pinned world authors this to keep a seat's speed inside its own kit's envelope regardless of what the player's identity requests. null reproduces an unclamped resolve exactly; Min == Max pins the effective speed outright; a narrower-than-wide-open range still admits a bounded profile override.

max.description: The greatest admitted value (inclusive) — WorldDefinitionValidator refuses Max < Min by name. Equal to Min pins the scalar outright regardless of what a profile requests.

envelope.title: MotionScalarEnvelope

held.description: The held-multiplier channel (a "boost"/"sprint"), or null for a kit with no held speed multiplier. The multiplier applies AFTER Envelope clamps the resolved value: the envelope pins the base rate, the multiplier rides on top.

channel.description: The declared composition channel name read while held.

multiplier.description: The speed multiplier while the channel reads held. Required positive.

held.title: WorldSpeedHeld

rate.description: Turn speed in radians per second at full authority (the profileless fallback counterpart to Value).

referenceSpeed.description: The longitudinal (drive) or local (grounded/free) speed, world units per second, at which steering authority peaks — authority rises linearly from zero at standstill and falls linearly past it toward Falloff at the kit's resolved move speed. Omitted (the default): full authority at every speed, the behavior every kit authoring no curve keeps.

falloff.description: The fraction of full steering authority remaining at the kit's resolved move speed, in [0, 1]. Unread while ReferenceSpeed is omitted.

pitchRate.description: The pitch rate (rad/s) a drive kit's Pitch channel commands; 0 (the default) locks the drive frame planar (the ground and hover variants). Positive selects the flying variant's pitched facing, clamped inside the integrator so the frame can never flip past vertical.

maxPitch.description: The drive pitch clamp (radians): how far the flying variant's facing may climb or dive before the integrator holds it, so it can never flip past vertical and invert the yaw frame mid-flight. Unread while PitchRate is zero.

shaping.description: The ordered velocity-shaping table (see WorldShaping) the ShapeVelocity operation reads — the first row whose when gate opens governs. Required (non-empty) for a kit whose program selects ShapeVelocity; null for a kit whose program never shapes planar velocity through it (a free-flight kit that owns its whole velocity channel directly).

items.description: One row of a kit's ordered shaping table: how velocity converges on the commanded intent while When holds. Rows evaluate in order, first match wins; the table may carry one unconditional (When omitted) row, and when present it must be last. Exactly one of Along or Dynamics is authored per row; Across is legitimate only beside Along. A drift/boost row is authored as an ordinary row gated on a held predicate: the FIRST open row governs, so a drift row belongs ahead of the kit's ordinary anisotropic row.

when.description: The gate that must hold for this row to win, or null for the unconditional row (permitted only as the final row). The gate reuses the action-lane predicate vocabulary, admitting body-fact kinds (now/recently/all/any/not) and held (a composition channel's own live read) — never a per-body action-state predicate.
when.title: ActionPredicate

along.description: The along facet — see WorldShapingAlong — or null for a Dynamics row.

engage.description: The whole-vector engage rate (u/s²) while the commanded target exceeds the body's current magnitude, or — paired with Across — the drive's longitudinal accel rate while throttle commands more speed. null means converge immediately.

reversalRate.description: The drive's sign-reversal rate (u/s²) while back-throttle opposes forward travel. null means reverse sign immediately. Refused without a paired Across.

release.description: The whole-vector release rate (u/s²) while the target does not exceed the current magnitude, or — paired with Across — the drive's coast rate toward rest with throttle centered, and the decay rate while over the commanded speed. null means converge immediately.

backwardSpeed.description: The backward speed (u/s) full back-throttle converges on from rest; absence forbids travelling backward. Refused whenever authored without a paired Across.

along.title: WorldShapingAlong

across.description: The across facet — see WorldShapingAcross — selecting the drive decomposition, or null for a row that shapes the whole vector. Refused paired with Dynamics or without Along.

lateral.description: The lateral convergence rate (u/s²) toward zero slip while this row governs, or null to remove slip immediately.

across.title: WorldShapingAcross

dynamics.description: The dynamics row a second-order follower shapes velocity through instead of Along, or null (the default) for the response/drive law. Exactly one of the two is authored per row.

turnScale.description: The steering-authority multiplier while this row governs — the tightened drift arc's spelling, and the neutral default for every ordinary row.

items.title: WorldShaping

moveFrame.description: Which frame MoveAdvance/MoveStrafe resolve in. Heading explicitly rotates the commanded planar target by the body's own integrated heading. World (the default) takes the two channels as axes already in world frame — the seat's client composes the camera yaw into the submitted intent before it ever reaches the wire, so the sim never reads a camera pose (determinism: no camera state enters simulation).
moveFrame.title: MotionMoveFrame

facingSnap.description: Under World only: whether the body's drawn ATTITUDE snaps to Atan2 of the commanded planar direction every tick that carries input (no turn-rate ramp, no skid) — the body angles toward its travel, a strafe included — while its HEADING (the Turn role's integral, WorldBody.FixedYaw, the frame a Heading pair moves in) holds, and the attitude returns to the heading the tick movement stops. Only the Face roles turn the heading itself. Ignored under Heading, where attitude is the integrated heading by construction. true is the default.

holds.description: The ordered list of what may hold this body — see WorldHold — read by the ResolveHold/ApplyHold operations. A Motion-kind kit authoring none refuses validation by name: the hold list is the only spelling of a vertical channel, so a kit with no vertical law of its own still authors one row of kind None.

items.description: One authored hold row of a kit's ordered Holds list — what may hold this body, in preference order. ResolveHold keeps the hold it has while its surface is still there and the same face, and otherwise takes the first row the world offers; ApplyHold applies Hold.

name.description: The row's name, unique within the list — the body.hold read-back token.

bond.description: Whether this row needs a surface (Surface) or holds the body where it is (Free).
bond.title: BodyHoldBond

hold.description: What holds the body once the row is taken.
hold.title: BodyHoldKind

cone.description: The inclusive angle band, in degrees, between an admitted surface normal and gravity-up: [0, 60] is floors, [60, 120] walls, [0, 180] everything. Required for Surface, refused for Free.

pull.description: The inward pull, world units per second, under Pull. Applied as a positional standoff, so it closes a gap the surface opens without ever pushing the body through it.

lift.description: The fraction of gravity cancelled under Lift: 1 hovers, 0.5 halves the fall.

speed.description: The travel speed along the hold's tangent plane, world units per second, or null to ride the kit's own resolved move speed.

reach.description: How far a surface row's probes search, world units. Required positive for Surface.

upLean.description: How far the body's up axis blends from gravity-up toward the surface normal, in [0, 1].

forward.description: Where the hold's frame takes its forward direction when the surface leaves it free.
forward.title: BodyHoldForward

onDrive.description: Whether driving into an admitted face takes this row with no channel press.

driveAlignment.description: The least alignment, in [0, 1], between the commanded direction and the face's inward normal before OnDrive takes it. Inert without it.

release.description: The declared channel name whose held read drops this row, or null for a row no channel can drop.

spend.description: What the row spends while held, or null for a row that spends nothing.

ratePerSecond.description: The positive rate the slot drains at, per second.

spend.title: WorldHoldSpend

medium.description: The medium's own displacement law. Required for Medium and refused on every other bond.

idleDrift.description: The idle vertical drift velocity below the equilibrium band, signed (u/s).

equilibriumOffset.description: The equilibrium line's depth below the medium surface, and the band's half-width (u).

settleRate.description: The proportional gain (1/s) the equilibrium error scales by to reach a target velocity inside the band or while recovering a breach above the surface.

medium.title: WorldHoldMedium

gravity.description: The vertical arc this row falls under. Required for Gravity and Lift; refused for Pull, None, and every Medium row.

rise.description: The downward acceleration while rising (u/s²) — the floaty top of the arc.

fall.description: The downward acceleration while falling (u/s²) — the snappy descent (heavier than the rise). The world's own solved gravity field, where one is authored, overrides the MAGNITUDE but keeps this row's rise-to-fall ratio as the arc's asymmetry.

gravity.title: WorldHoldGravity

envelope.description: The vertical-channel envelope Gravity's terminal fall speed and Medium's terminal rise/sink speeds share. Required for a Medium bond and for a Gravity/Lift hold short of full lift; refused otherwise.

riseSpeed.description: The terminal upward speed (u/s). Required for a Medium bond; refused (the arc never clamps a rise) for Gravity/Lift.

sinkSpeed.description: The terminal downward speed (u/s) — a Gravity/Lift row's own terminal fall speed, or a Medium row's terminal sink speed.

envelope.title: WorldHoldEnvelope

thrust.description: The fraction of the kit's resolved move speed the MoveUp role commands vertically while this row holds, in every bond — 0 (the default) is no vertical thrust at all, 1 is fully isotropic. A non-Medium row commanding thrust takes the vertical channel outright for the tick, clearing the ballistic carry; a medium row folds it into the medium's own displacement before that law's convergence runs.

items.title: WorldHold

upTurn.description: How fast a solved gravity field and a measured contact normal may each turn the body's up axis — see WorldUpTurnRates. Omitted (null) reproduces the engine's own steering rates exactly; read the effective rates from UpTurn.

field.description: The ceiling on how fast a solved gravity field may turn the up axis. Crossing this rate lets an attractor's pull replace the world's own as one continuous roll rather than a single-tick inversion; every ordinary reorientation turns far slower and is untouched.

contact.description: The ceiling on how fast a measured ground-contact normal may turn the up axis — a discontinuity filter, not a smoothing rate: it should sit an order of magnitude above the fastest curvature this kit's own top speed can walk, so ordinary running adopts the surface exactly and only a collider crease is spread across a few ticks. Both rates must remain positive after Q48.16 compilation.

upTurn.title: WorldUpTurnRates

obstruction.description: The non-walkable contact witness's latch tuning — see WorldObstructionLatch. Omitted (null) reproduces the engine's own latch exactly; read the effective latch from Obstruction.

displacement.description: World units a body must move from where the witness last (re)latched before it is considered to have genuinely moved on. Its squared comparison threshold must remain positive after Q48.16 compilation.

idleThreshold.description: The raw MoveAdvance/MoveStrafe role-channel magnitude (each reads in [-1, 1]) below which the body counts as not actively driving.

graceSeconds.description: How long, in real time, an un-refreshed latch survives a solver pass reporting no push at all — absorbs ordinary query noise near a surface (a gradient/quantization boundary, or a body settled into a wall/ground corner under blended contact geometry). Must convert to a positive exact whole engine-tick count.

obstruction.title: WorldObstructionLatch

groundSnap.description: The greatest downward distance a grounded walker follows a surface across a crest, down a slope or off a small edge. Scaled with the body. Jumping and deliberate upward launches release support. Zero disables snapping; must be finite and non-negative.

stepHeight.description: The tallest riser, in world units scaled with the body, a grounded body walks up onto rather than stopping against (see FixedStepUp). A step the ordinary contact solve finds blocked is retried raised by this height, moved, and lowered back, and is kept only when it lands grounded on a walkable surface no higher than this above where it started. Read only by a program that owns the vertical contact channel, and never while the body is airborne or held by a pull. Zero, the default, never steps. Must be finite and non-negative, and a positive value must remain positive after Q48.16 compilation.

motion.title: WorldMotion

collider.description: The kit's collider, when it authors one.

anyOf.description: A sphere resting on the body root.
anyOf.title: WorldColliderSphere

anyOf.description: A capsule whose lower sphere rests on the body root.

endpoint.description: The body-local vector from the lower sphere center to the upper sphere center.

anyOf.title: WorldColliderCapsule

anyOf.description: An oriented box resting on the body root before its local rotation is applied.
anyOf.title: WorldColliderBox

anyOf.description: The finite primitives emitted by a creation, composed into one compound body collider. Spheres and ellipsoids retain their exact surfaces; other primitives currently use their local boxes.
anyOf.title: WorldColliderFromCreation

collider.title: WorldCollider

bodyContact.description: Whether two bodies wearing this kit physically depenetrate.
bodyContact.title: WorldBodyContactMode

x-enumDescriptions.Overlap: Bodies may overlap. This is the default; the engine never introduces crowd shoving implicitly.
x-enumDescriptions.Solid: Two bodies physically depenetrate only when both of their kits select this mode.

items.title: WorldProjectedKit

bindingOverlays.description: The world's binding layers — a visitor's seat composes over them.

items.description: One per-world binding overlay — a whole BindingProfileDocument layered over the engine default beneath every seat's profile bindings, so a world can contextualize the controls (a kart world remapping a lane, an RTS world adding a chorded command page) as data, never a client fork. Merged in order; the composed result (default ⊕ every overlay whose When currently holds) is what the validator compiles.

id.description: The overlay's stable id — its mutation address (unique within the definition; carries no meaning beyond identity).

document.description: The overlay binding document merged into the composed mapping.
document.title: BindingProfileDocument

bindingBar.description: The on-screen bar policy carried with this binding layer; null carries no policy on this layer, so bar resolution falls through to the world-authored policy, and to Absent (no bar drawn) when neither an identity nor the world authors one.

slotSet.description: The physical controls this bar shows, by input source id (gamepad.buttonSouth, mouse.button1, …) — the same vocabulary a binding entry's sources speak, every id validated against the engine's input-source catalog, unique, at most MaxSlots. A layout's bank places these; one it does not place is not shown on that bank.

banks.description: The stacked banks — at least one, at most MaxBanks, unique ids, each naming a page the composed binding profile actually declares. List order is draw order.

items.description: One stacked binding-bar bank: what it is — the page it renders and its opacities. Several banks of the same slot set render simultaneously, each showing what that bank's OWN page binds. Where a bank sits, and which plates it shows, is each layout's banks table's to say; draw order is this list's order (later draws on top).

id.description: The bank's stable id — its mutation address and its key in every layout's bank table.

pageId.description: The BindingPageDefinition.Id this bank renders — validated to exist somewhere in the composed binding profile. A context overlay (a board's) replaces only the pages it declares, so a page no bank names can be active: it renders in the first bank whose page the same held modifiers select. The board's resting page takes the resting page's bank, the pages it leaves to the player stay in their own banks, and the bar's layout and model stay as the seat set them.

alpha.description: This bank's opacity when it is NOT the seat's currently active page.

activeAlpha.description: This bank's opacity when it IS the seat's currently active page; null draws fully opaque (1.0) while active.

items.title: WorldBindingBarBank

enabled.description: Whether the bar is shown when no live override hides it.

text.description: Whether the bar draws the atlas text it composes — a badge whose icon row carries a Label (LB/RB, LT/RT, LS/RS, the menu trio, the exotics), the active page's name under the modifier indicators, and a chord hint's label. false drops every label-content badge outright and leaves a purely pictographic bar: every plate, the glyph-content badges (the d-pad arrows and the face-position marks), the bound actions' icons, and the modifier indicators all still draw.

modifiers.description: Whether the bar draws the modifier indicator row on its anchor line — one plate per modifier the composed profile carries (declared rows plus every chord/held token the compiler synthesizes), lit while held. false drops the row and leaves the slot clusters alone. While the row draws, it places every chord member, so every command chord can show as a hint; without it a hint shows only for a chord whose members are all in SlotSet.

declaredModifiersOnly.description: Whether the modifier row (and the chord hints it places) keeps to the modifiers the binding document DECLARES in its modifiers section — the page-holding triggers an author named — and leaves out the implicit modifier the compiler mints for every raw source a chord or held row names (a bare key, a mouse button, a shoulder). false draws every one. It shapes only what Modifiers draws, so it does nothing while that is off.

pageLabel.description: Whether the bar names the active page under its anchor while Text is on; false keeps every badge label and chord hint and drops only the page's name.

hideUnbound.description: Whether a slot with no bound act on its bank's page should not render at all, rather than drawing the disabled tier-0 plate. A player's own BindingBarPreferences.HideUnbound overrides this.

multiSeatAlpha.description: The opacity every joined seat's bar renders at while two or more seats are joined — the split-screen quieting lever, multiplied into each bank's own alpha; 1 keeps multi-seat bars fully opaque.

iconRow.description: The state row a slot's icon resolves through, spelled state.<row> — the row's CELL KEY is the bound row's id when it authors one, else its action (command or channel; a dotted command name therefore needs an id, since a cell key holds no dot), and its value is an icons name. The engine holds no action-to-icon vocabulary of its own: the association is ordinary authored state, so it is written, read, and MUTATED like any other state (world.state.cell.set) — a spell minted at runtime gets its icon by writing a cell, never by reshaping the document. null resolves no slot icons at all; a key the row does not carry simply draws no icon.

layouts.description: The bar's layouts by name — a crossbar, a strip, whatever an author adds next — each a whole WorldBindingBarLayout.

additionalProperties.description: The authored layout of one on-screen binding bar: its tables, its banks, and its size tuning. Every tuning field is an optional override of the engine's resolved default (the Default* constants below): lengths are fractions of the seat viewport's height, every *Ratio is a multiple of the button size, and every *MinPx is a device-pixel floor.

tables.description: The plate tables by name — a cross, a strip, a column — each authored once and placed by the banks' pieces as many times as the layout needs.

items.description: One physical control's plate on a bank, in button pitches from the bank's anchor — x right, y UP.

source.description: The physical control's input source id (a slotSet member).

x.description: Pitches right of the anchor (negative = left).

badge.description: Where the plate's physical-button badge sits, [x, y] as signed multiples of the layout's glyph offset: +1 right / up, −1 left / down, 0 centered. A plate in a cluster points its badge outward — a d-pad's up button badges up, its left button left — so the badge never lands on a neighbour. null is the up-right corner, [1, 1].

items.title: WorldBindingBarSlotPlacement

banks.description: Where each bank sits and what it shows, by bank id. A bank with no row here is not drawn in this layout.

additionalProperties.description: One bank's place on a layout — a bank is a bar: where it hangs and the pieces it is made of. A control in the slot set that no piece places is not shown on this bank; a source placed by two pieces takes the later one.

items.description: One placed table: a named table of the layout, moved by At.

table.description: The key of a table in the layout's tables.

at.description: The displacement, [x, y] in button pitches (x right, y up); null is none.

badge.description: A badge direction for every plate of this piece, overriding the table rows'; see Badge. null keeps each row's own.

items.title: WorldBindingBarPiece

anchor.description: Where this bank hangs, or null to share the layout's anchor (and so its frame: the pieces then nest against the other banks there).

additionalProperties.title: WorldBindingBarBankPlacement

anchor.description: Where the bar's own anchor (the modifier row, page label, chord hints) hangs, and the anchor every bank without its own shares.

buttonSize.description: The slot-plate size at most: the writer shrinks it so every anchor group fits its seat region, and a seat's stored bar scale multiplies it.

glyphOffsetRatio.description: The badge's offset as a fraction of ButtonSize — each plate's badge takes its own signed multiples of it (Badge).

glyphSizeRatio.description: The badge's size as a fraction of ButtonSize.

modifierHalfRatio.description: The modifier indicator's plate half-extent, in button sizes.

modifierSpacingRatio.description: The modifier indicators' pitch, in button sizes.

modifierGlyphRatio.description: The modifier badge's half-extent, as a fraction of the modifier plate half.

labelCellRatio.description: The page label's glyph-cell height, as a fraction of the modifier plate half.

labelCellMinPx.description: The page label's glyph-cell floor, px.

labelGapRatio.description: The page label's drop below the anchor, as a fraction of the modifier plate half.

hintCellRatio.description: A chord-hint line's glyph-cell height, as a fraction of the modifier plate half.

hintCellMinPx.description: A chord-hint line's glyph-cell floor, px.

hintLineStepRatio.description: The chord-hint line pitch, as a fraction of the hint cell height.

hintBaseGapRatio.description: The hint stack's lift above the anchor, as a fraction of the modifier plate half.

additionalProperties.title: WorldBindingBarLayout

layout.description: The name of the layout drawn when LayoutCell is absent or names none.

layoutCell.description: A text state cell, state.<row>.<key>, whose value names the live entry of Layouts; a value naming none falls back to Layout. Ordinary state: a chord, a wheel sector, or the console switches the bar's whole shape by writing the cell.

modelCell.description: A text state cell, state.<row>.<key>, whose value picks the bar's model: single draws one bar — the active page, in the first authored bank's place, swapping in place as a chord is held or released or a context group switches the page; any other value (or no cell) draws every bank the live layout places, the active one at full alpha and the rest as wings. The active page never changes the model. Ordinary state, flipped the same way LayoutCell is.

visible.description: The bar's visibility condition over presentation facts, or null for always.

bindingBar.title: WorldBindingBarAuthoring

when.description: The condition this layer composes under; null always composes it (today's behavior). Reuses StateCondition's field convention rather than a second reading of "compare a state cell" — the same state/key/comparison/value shape a placement's own response facet speaks. Re-evaluated whenever the routed definition changes, never per frame.

state.description: The state row compared — any declared state.world row of a numeric kind (never Text).

value.description: The literal comparand, or null when ComparandState spells the comparand instead.

key.description: The cell inside State, or null for its slot cell. Refused when State is keyed and this is absent, or unkeyed and this is present.

comparandState.description: Another declared state.world row, read live and compared instead of Value. Must share State's cell kind (refused by name otherwise).

comparandKey.description: The cell inside ComparandState, on the same terms as Key. Refused when ComparandState is absent.

items.title: WorldBindingOverlay

prototypes.description: The content references rendering resolves prototype bodies from.

items.description: A prototype's local name and the full content pin of its disclosed body.

id.description: The name placements address in this projection.
id.title: DocumentIdentifier

content.description: The SHA-256 pin of the canonical document and mesh.

items.title: WorldPrototypeReference

placements.description: The placement rows, as the recipient's state disclosure deals them (Disclose).

items.description: One placement instance row — a creation asset stamped into the world by reference: transform + facets as data, addressed by its stable Id. A placement whose creation carries timeline frames is animated: it replays client-side on the render clock through the reserved dynamic-transform pool (distribution/mirror facets are static-stamp-only and reject on an animated row). A placement carrying an Inhabit facet is a live population body rather than furniture (see WorldPlacementInhabit); its declared creation eyes derive WorldCamera feeds and its declared faces derive screens (both at the delivery boundary, never written to the document).

id.description: The row's stable string id (its mutation address). It may not carry : or be exactly $each (TryValidateId).

prototypeId.description: The referenced Id (must resolve; removal of a referenced creation rejects loudly).

position.description: The opaque stored translation — a local offset when Parent is null, or relative to Parent's composed frame otherwise (see Parent). A dealt child's is its displacement from its DealSlot's offset in its template's region (LocalFrame). Exact runtime writes retain Q48.16 through serialization; geometric readers require a resolved frame. Inert (still validated and stored, but read by nothing — neither the resolve nor the renderer) when Attach is set: the row's live position is the resolved attachment, never this authored one.

yawDegrees.description: The stamp yaw about +Y, degrees — world-space when Parent is null, added to the parent's own composed yaw otherwise. Same attach caveat as Position.

scale.description: The uniform stamp scale (clamped to the placement policy envelope by validation).

distribution.description: The placement distribution, or null for a single copy. Static placements accept a Lattice, Noise, or Scatter region, each with a none fill — Lattice materializes a regular two-axis grid (PatternFor); Noise and Scatter materialize a deterministic hash-sampled instance set instead (SampledFixedOffsetsFor), the placement twin of the field lattice's own Noise/Scatter fills. Refused together with Attach.

mirror.description: The authored local reflection plane, or null for no reflected copy. Refused together with Attach.

emission.description: The placement's emission facet (a synth voice the stamp itself makes — see WorldEmission), or null for silent. Under Distribution the emission binds to the placement root only. Omitted from the wire when null. Composes with Attach: an attached row's source point rides the resolved live pose (Client.WorldAnchorPoses) instead of the row's static position, and an inactive carrier silences the emitter rather than leaving it at a stale point.

solid.description: The placement's solidity facet (see WorldSolid). Both contact providers compile the creation's emitted shapes; analytic collision uses per-primitive colliders, including exact half-spaces for planes. Omitted from the wire when null. Composes with Attach under the analytic provider only (WorldColliderSet.RefreshAttached recomputes an attached row's colliders every tick from the resolved live pose); still refused together under the field provider, which compiles every solid row's geometry once into one SDF program and never rebuilds it per tick.

inhabit.description: The inhabit facet (null = decoration), binding the row to live population bodies. Omitted from the wire when null. Refused together with Attach — a row cannot both spawn its own driven bodies and ride another body's pose.

faceSources.description: Per-instance overrides of the creation's declared faces (null = every face shows its declared default). Omitted from the wire when null. Orthogonal to Attach (a content selector, not a transform) — composes freely, like every other facet that now tracks the dynamic pose.

region.description: The placement's region facet (see WorldPlacementRegion) — a named volume the world-events feed watches for body enter/exit, or null for none. Omitted from the wire when null. Composes with Attach: an attached row's sensing sphere centers on the resolved live pose (Server.WorldEventFeed.CollectRegions) instead of the row's static position — see WorldPlacementRegion's own remarks.

attach.description: The placement's attach facet (see WorldPlacementAttach) — binds the row's resolved world pose to a live population body, or null for a static/authored transform (the default, unchanged behavior). Omitted from the wire when null.

contribution.description: The placement's contribution facet (see WorldPlacementContribution) — marks the row a host-authored slot a federation partner fills, or null for an ordinary placement. Omitted from the wire when null. Composes with every other facet: the facet governs which creation the row shows and for how long, never its transform.

respond.description: The placement's response facet (see WorldPlacementResponse) — the ordered prototype swaps a lattice-field or state-cell condition fires, or null for an ordinary placement that always shows PrototypeId. Omitted from the wire when null. Refused together with Attach, Inhabit, and FaceSources.

grip.description: The placement's grip facet (see WorldPlacementGrip) — overrides the world's default hold policy for this row's compiled surface(s), or null to inherit the world default. Omitted from the wire when null. Requires Solid (validated).

board.description: The placement's board facet (see WorldPlacementBoard) — the tabletop primitive, or null for no anchored topology. Omitted from the wire when null.

parent.description: Another placement's Id this row's frame composes over, or null for a world-space row (today's behavior, unchanged). Position/YawDegrees become this row's own LOCAL offset/heading in the parent's composed frame: the parent's resolved yaw rotates the offset before adding the parent's resolved position (the same local-offset-rotated-by-orientation convention WorldPlacementAttach already uses), and yaw adds. Resolved by WorldPlacementFrameCompilation into PlacementFrames, with cached frames only for immutable inputs and fresh frames for state-bound translations or lattice steps, which every consumer of a placement's WORLD transform reads instead of this row's own Position/YawDegrees. Validated: must name a declared placement other than itself, must not close a cycle, and that placement must carry neither a Distribution nor a Mirror (an expanded row has no single frame to compose against). Parent scale multiplies the child's local offset and resolved scale.

deal.description: The placement's deal facet (see WorldPlacementDeal) — the row is a template whose instances are dealt from a keyed state row as child placements over its own Distribution region, or null for an ordinary placement. A template renders nothing and collides with nothing itself. Omitted from the wire when null. Requires Distribution; refused together with Inhabit, Attach, Respond, Mirror, and FaceSources.

dealSlot.description: A dealt child's reserved distribution slot, independent of its editable transform. Absent on ordinary placements and templates.

spatial.description: Named occupation, clearance, and influence volumes in this placement's local frame. The compiled static-query eligibility is exposed by Unsupported; ordinary inhabit/attach/distribution facets remain legal and are reported there when they have no single static frame.

holding.description: Which of Respond's entries held at the last response sweep, one bit per entry in authored order (bit i for entry i); 0 while none holds, and always 0 on a row without Respond. The response sweep writes it, and a booting document's state entries are settled into it before admission (SettleResponses); the row shows the lowest set bit's entry, else its own authored PrototypeId (ShownPrototypeId). Refused on a row without Respond and with a bit at or past its entry count. A reader whose disclosure withholds a cell an entry reads is handed the mask without that entry's bit (Disclosed). Omitted from the wire when 0.

surface.description: Optional one-time projection of each static occurrence onto explicitly named contact surfaces.
