items.description: One placeable speaker in the world — the camera family's sibling: abstract, name-keyed, $type-discriminated, whole-row UpsertSpeaker/RemoveSpeaker. Routing chiasmus: screens consume cameras; speakers consume audio sources. Omni-only v1 (no cones — stereo separation is already the feed model). A new speaker kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.

anyOf.description: A speaker posed directly in world space.

name.description: The speaker's stable name — its mutation address.

feed.description: The feed it plays (source + channel + gain).

attenuation.description: The point-attenuation policy, or null to coalesce to the WorldAudioDefaults section. Beds carry their own radii instead and leave this null.

anyOf.title: WorldSpeakerFixed

anyOf.description: A speaker anchored to a WorldAnchor — the entity/part/placement pose it rides supplies the live position; Offset is the exact attachment point in the anchor's local axes on top of that. Unlike cameras, speakers resolve every anchor kind, placements included (the placement's stamped transform is reachable client-side from the definition plus the animator state).

offset.description: The attachment point relative to the anchor's resolved pose, in anchor-local axes.

name.description: The speaker's stable name — its mutation address.

feed.description: The feed it plays (source + channel + gain).

attenuation.description: The point-attenuation policy, or null to coalesce to the WorldAudioDefaults section. Beds carry their own radii instead and leave this null.

anyOf.title: WorldSpeakerAnchored

anyOf.description: An ambient bed — a region presence, not a position: center-panned, its gain an envelope of the listener's distance from Center — full inside InnerRadius, zero at Radius — with its presence slew bounded by FadeSeconds. Box extents become a later $type only if a sphere proves dishonest.

center.description: The region's extent center, world space.

radius.description: The region's outer radius — the envelope's zero and the cull edge.

innerRadius.description: The full-presence inner radius; 0 shoulders the envelope from the center.

fadeSeconds.description: The presence slew bound in seconds (null = the audio defaults' DefaultBedFadeSeconds).

name.description: The speaker's stable name — its mutation address.

feed.description: The feed it plays (source + channel + gain).

attenuation.description: The point-attenuation policy, or null to coalesce to the WorldAudioDefaults section. Beds carry their own radii instead and leave this null.

anyOf.title: WorldSpeakerBed

items.title: WorldSpeaker

items.description: One tune asset reference row — a puck.tune.v1 document's stable name, its file path (resolved beside the document that authors the row, the same rule WorldMusicRow follows), and the SHA-256 hex64 pin of the referenced document's own canonical bytes. Never embedded: the document is loaded, canonicalized, and hash-verified where it is compiled, the same load-then-pin discipline WorldMusicRow already applies. The hash doubles as the runtime restart discriminator: a content change restarts the tune's headless host, a rename does not.

name.description: The row's stable name — its mutation address and the handle a speaker's Tune references.

hash.description: The SHA-256 hex64 of the referenced document's canonical bytes.

items.title: WorldTune

items.description: One synth-patch asset reference row — the puck.synthesizer-patch.v1 twin of WorldTune, same name/source/hash shape and load-then-pin discipline.

name.description: The row's stable name — its mutation address; referenced by Synth and by PatchId facets.

hash.description: The SHA-256 hex64 of the referenced document's canonical bytes.

items.title: WorldPatch

masterGain.description: The master gain the mix path applies over every emitter (1 = unity), bounded by MaxLevel.

defaultSpeakerRadius.description: The audible support radius a point emitter coalesces to when its row declares no attenuation/radius.

defaultCurve.description: The falloff curve a point emitter coalesces to: CurveSmoothstep or CurveLinear.

defaultBedFadeSeconds.description: The presence slew bound a bed coalesces to when it declares none.

listener.description: The listener policy: ListenerFocus (the active view camera's pose listens), seat<n> (that seat's view camera), or a declared camera name — so a stage or museum world can pin its listener without touching the runtime.

cues.description: Gets the cue table. The absence-coalesce lives in the accessor for the same reason Elements's does.

items.description: One world-event → sound binding — a row of the Audio section's cue table: when the named engine event fires, the referenced patch voices through a short-lived transient emitter placed per Placement. Event tokens are either a published engine mechanism (EventTokens) or a cue name emitted by one of the same world's rules. A genre can therefore bind authored rule events without widening the engine vocabulary.

event.description: The published engine token or rule-emitted cue name.

patchId.description: The referenced Name the cue voices (must resolve).

placement.description: Where the cue sounds: PlacementAtSite (spatial, at the event's world position — the shimmer's audio twin; events with no derivable site fall back to the listener), PlacementListener (UI feedback — rides the listener pose, so distance 0 renders full gain and the mixer's on-top-of-listener pan hold centers it), or emitter:<name> (sounds from the named speaker's resolved pose and support radius).

gainThousandths.description: The cue's voice gain in thousandths (1000 = unity), or null for unity. Bounded by MaxLevel × 1000 — the shared audio gain ceiling in the cue table's integer unit.

items.title: WorldAudioCue

collision.description: The contact tuning — a client reads body radius/height from it to frame and interpolate.

requirements.description: The contact qualities the world requires. An empty list permits analytic primitive contact; any declared requirement selects the SDF field.

items.description: A contact quality authored by the world, independent of the engine implementation that supplies it.
items.title: WorldContactRequirement

x-enumDescriptions.SmoothUnionContact: Blended creation surfaces remain solid across their smooth-union seams.
x-enumDescriptions.GradientDerivedUp: A body's up direction follows the contacted field gradient rather than world +Y.

contactSkin.description: The signed skin the solver keeps between a body and every surface (world units).

maxIterations.description: The relaxation iteration count per tick (above 8 is a solver pathology, not a choice).

maxSlopeDegrees.description: The steepest surface a body still counts as standing on. A contact whose normal leans further from the body's up axis than this pushes the body but never grounds it — the walkable-slope limit.

gradientProbe.description: The finite-difference step field contact samples the surface normal with, in world units; 0 takes the evaluator's own default. Meaningful only when a requirement selects field contact.

defaultHold.description: Whether a body's surface hold may take any solid surface by default. A placement's own WorldPlacementGrip overrides this for the colliders it compiles; the field lattice's own terrain, which no placement row owns, has only this. false (the default) holds nothing.

events.description: The bounded body-overlap event policy. ABSENT takes Default; author maxPairsPerBody: 0 to disable body-pair events while retaining ordinary world contact.

candidateBudget.description: The most box-overlapping sweep candidates inspected for one body while discovering new overlaps; a body whose bounding box misses the searching body's is never charged. Must be at least MaxPairsPerBody.

maxPairsPerBody.description: The maximum retained overlap-event degree of one body; zero disables collision begin/end sensing.

beginBudget.description: The maximum collision-begin relationships admitted in one authority tick. Existing relationships and their ends are not delayed.

events.title: WorldCollisionEvents

bodyContacts.description: The bounded dynamic-body depenetration policy. ABSENT takes Default. This is independent of overlap events.

candidateBudget.description: The most sweep candidates inspected for one solid body. Must be at least MaxPairsPerBody.

maxPairsPerBody.description: The most body contacts incident to one body in a tick. It also sizes the rigid contact registry: a rigid body carries at most this many body contacts plus its surface contact, so no admitted contact is ever dropped for want of room.

rigidSubstepCeiling.description: The rigid solver's substeps per tick: each runs a velocity integration, a biased solve, a position integration and an unbiased relax over every contact, and the contact softness is formed at the substep width.

rigidRestSpeed.description: Below this speed (world units/second) of its fastest point, the centre's linear speed plus its angular speed times its bounding radius, a supported rigid body counts toward the resting hold window (RigidRestHoldSeconds). It scales with each body's live scale, so a long piece turning slowly about its centre stays awake while its ends still move. Non-negative.

rigidRestHoldSeconds.description: How long a rigid body must stay under the rest speed while supported before the resting latch actually closes — long enough that crossing a contact skin's noise band for one tick never freezes a body mid-roll. Non-negative.

rigidSubstepTravelFraction.description: The fraction of a rigid body's own bounding radius its solved motion may depart from the motion its contact probe certified before a guard sweep re-certifies it against the static field: a smaller fraction guards more often. Strictly positive.

rigidSubstepMinimumTravel.description: The floor (world units) under that departure bound, independent of RigidSubstepTravelFraction — guards a body whose collider is small enough that the fraction alone would derive a near-zero bound. It is also the travel of the support a sleeping body is woken within. Strictly positive.

rigidPairRestitutionSpeed.description: Below this closing speed (world units/second), a rigid contact restitutes at zero rather than its pair's coefficient, so two bodies at rest never micro-bounce. Non-negative; small enough that a real strike is unaffected.

contactHertz.description: The contact spring frequency in hertz, clamped by the solver to one eighth of the substep rate. Non-negative; zero authors no soft push.

contactDampingRatio.description: The contact spring's damping ratio, dimensionless and non-negative.

contactSpeed.description: The maximum penetration push-out speed, in metres per second. Non-negative; zero authors no push-out bias.

bodyContacts.title: WorldBodyContactPolicy

gridCellSize.description: The world-space cell edge of the distance grid the solid field bakes its program into, so a query far from every surface reads a corner bound instead of marching the program; 0 (the default) bakes no grid and every query reads the exact program. A smaller cell tightens the bound and enlarges the grid. Meaningful only when a requirement selects field contact.

collision.title: WorldCollision

views.description: The authored window composition (slots, layouts, seat framing), or null when the document authors none — a seatless world composes no seat view.

seatRig.description: The authored chase framing, or null for a document that seats no body; SeatRig is what a reader resolves through.

seatControl.description: The authored constraints for live seat camera input, or null for a document that seats no body; SeatControl is what a reader resolves through.

yawReference.description: What the camera yaw is relative to.
yawReference.title: WorldSeatYawReference

minPitch.description: The minimum live pitch offset in radians.

maxPitch.description: The maximum live pitch offset in radians.

follow.description: The follow camera: with no look input the camera yaw eases in behind the body's heading; any look input (a deflected look stick, a held orbit/steer) is free-look and the follow yields for as long as it lasts. Optional; absent is a still camera that goes only where look input sends it. Needs World — a body-relative yaw already rides the body.

rate.description: The exponential rate (per second) the camera yaw closes on the heading — about 63% of the remaining angle per 1/rate seconds; larger is a stiffer follow.

whileIdle.description: Whether the follow also runs while the body has no movement input. false (the default) is the classic feel: after a free-look the camera stays where you left it until you move.

follow.title: WorldSeatFollow

autoFirstPerson.description: The automatic pull-in policy; absent, automatic pull-in is unavailable whatever a player or session asks.

enabled.description: Whether automatic pull-in is the author's default.

exitDistance.description: Minimum open room for exit, greater than entry.

autoFirstPerson.title: WorldCameraAutoFirstPerson

boom.description: Optional authored distance limits and input step for the interactive orbit.

step.description: Distance removed by one positive input unit.

boom.title: WorldCameraBoom

seatControl.title: WorldSeatViewControl

cameraRig.description: The program a seat's view resolves through while its published mode state targets CameraTarget — null for a world that authors no camera-targeting mode state. Resolved through the ordinary Puck.World.Client.WorldCameraRigCompiler pipeline against whichever body the seat currently perceives from (the possessed camera body — see Puck.World.Server.WorldEngagement), exactly like SeatRig resolves against the seat's own avatar; no bespoke per-frame integrator reads this field.

shaderToolchain.description: The directory holding the graph compiler's dxc, or null to resolve it by bare name through the ordinary executable search path — never an environment variable.

graphs.description: The authored views.graphs frame-graph instances (empty = none declared).

items.description: One named instance of a frame graph: a view rendered by a puck.render.graph.v1 document, such as a pane, a game camera shown on a screen, or a nested world, or an engine package's producer such as the SDF world. A Instance shows it in a layout, and the pipeline.* console verbs address it by name. The row carries authored intent; planning, scheduling, compilation and resources belong to the renderer.

name.description: The instance's stable name (a SafeName, unique within the section), which another row's input, a layout slot and a capture name.

source.description: Where the instance's graph comes from, or null for a row that names a Package: a puck.render.graph.v1 graph document, a one-off shader source file, which reads as a one-pass graph, or a puck.shader.package.v1 package directory, which loads with its source tree gone. It resolves beside the document that authors it (WorldDocumentPaths), like every relative path a document authors.

package.description: The engine package whose producer renders the instance, such as sdf.world, or an uploaded producer's source package, source.<producer id>, opened from Settings and converted once a frame at most however many instances read it, or null for a row that names a Source. A package instance reads no input and takes no time scale, output or override.

refresh.description: How often it refreshes, or null for every frame something visible reads it.

divisor.description: The instance renders at most once every this many presented frames, or null when Hertz states the rate.

hertz.description: The most renders a second, or null when Divisor states the rate.

refresh.title: WorldViewGraphRefresh

inputs.description: The external versions of its graph bound to other instances' outputs, or null for none.

items.description: One external version of a graph instance's document bound to another instance's output.

resource.description: The external version of the instance's graph document the binding fills.

instance.description: The views.graphs row whose output fills it. Naming the row's own instance reads its previous frame.

previousFrame.description: Whether the read takes the producer's previous completed frame, which lets two instances show each other. Default false: the producer renders first in the same frame.

items.title: WorldViewGraphInput

timeScale.description: The instance clock's rate multiplier — presentation only, never simulation state. Default 1; 0 freezes the clock.

output.description: The image version the instance shows, or null for the source's first declared output.

overrides.description: This instance's parameter overrides, keyed by pass name; each value is that pass's config object keyed by field. A field absent here keeps the default the shared source declares, so two instances of one source differ only in what they override. The source's config schema binds them when a boot, a world.load or world.reload, a commit, or an upsert names them (the server reads the source, and refuses a value by name), and again when a graph installs (the host binds them into its passes). null overrides nothing.

additionalProperties.$comment: Open payload: this member's shape is decided by an id named elsewhere in the document, never by this generator.

settings.description: A source package row's producer settings, which its producer opens the image with and its shape validates, as a screen's producer source's settings are, or null for the producer's defaults. Only a row naming a source package (source.<producer id>) takes settings.

additionalProperties.$comment: Open payload: this member's shape is decided by an id named elsewhere in the document, never by this generator.

parameters.description: This instance's bound parameters, keyed by pass name and then by config field: a number, or a state.<row>[.<key>][.$target] token naming a Fixed or Int cell whose value the pass reads through its state mirror slot, eased by default. A field a row names both here and in Overrides is refused by name, and a binding that does not resolve leaves the field at its source's default. null binds nothing.

tier.description: The quality tier the instance renders at, from the authored quality vocabulary: the variant of its source's package it loads, or the tier its source compiles for where no package holds it. A tier selects how the passes compute and never what they read, so two documents differing only in a row's tier present the same state. null loads the variant no tier names.

fit.description: How a layout slot showing the instance fits its image: Stretch fills the slot whatever the two aspect ratios, and Contain shows the whole image at its own aspect ratio, centred, with letterbox bars where it does not reach the slot's edges, which a pointer passes through to the game. A window capture's aspect ratio is the captured window's, whatever its profile extent. A pane is never cropped, so Cover is refused. null stretches.
fit.title: SourceFit

items.title: WorldViewGraph

graphBudget.description: The graph scheduler's price ceiling, or null for none.

passPixelsPerFrame.description: The pass-pixels (passes times rendered pixels) those instances may spend in one presented frame; the stalest due instance is admitted first and the rest read their latest completed output. 0 sets no ceiling.

bytesPerTick.description: The bytes every bound parameter together may owe its pass on a tick that moves its row, or 0 for no ceiling. A document whose bindings exceed it is refused, naming the graph and the binding that crosses it.

bytesPerFrame.description: The bytes every bound parameter together may owe its pass on each presented frame between ticks, or 0 for no ceiling, refused the same way.

graphBudget.title: WorldViewGraphBudget

root.description: The views.graphs row the display shows and captures read, or null for the render graph composition synthesizes from the document around WorldViewGraphs.WorldInstance and WorldViewGraphs.MainInstance. A world that names its root authors its whole render graph, the sdf.world package row included.

post.description: The post-process passes the synthesized root graph runs over the composed frame, in order, before the overlay, or null for none. A world that names Root authors its whole graph and names none.

items.description: One pass the render graph composition synthesizes runs over the composed frame: a post-process package pass of the root graph (WorldViewGraphs.MainInstance), written as a puck.render.graph.v1 document's packages row is, less its ports. The rows run in order after every view and pane is placed and before the overlay, each reading the frame the pass before it wrote and writing the frame the next reads, so a row names no input or output. Presentation only; nothing here reaches simulation state.

name.description: The pass's name in the root graph (a SafeName, unique within the section and distinct from every views.graphs row, whose place pass the root names after the row), which a probe parameter's post target names.

package.description: The post-process package the pass runs, a render graph package id such as sdf.film-grain, checked against the host's catalog at document load.

config.description: The package's config values, each absent field at its default, or null for every default. The graph compiler binds them against the package's schema when the root graph is composed, and a boot refuses a value that does not bind, naming the row.
config.$comment: Open payload: this member's shape is decided by an id named elsewhere in the document, never by this generator.

items.title: WorldViewPostPass

config.description: Film grain: a per-pixel integer-hashed offset added over the input image, keyed on the engine tick.

size.description: The grain cell size, in pixels.

seed.description: Folded into the per-pixel hash; two worlds with different seeds grain differently.

flickerHz.description: How many times per second the grain pattern advances. The pattern is keyed on the engine tick, so a frame carries the grain of the flicker period its tick falls in; a rate that does not divide the tick rate advances every whole number of ticks nearest below its period.

quality.description: Per-view render quality and tier floors; a row named * supplies the defaults.

items.description: A view's durable render quality. A name of * supplies the defaults for the world's own player views (world, world$2 on); a named row overrides only that view, and a camera or session view takes only a row that names it, rendering native otherwise. Pins are session state and have no document member.

name.description: The render view's instance name, or * for the player-view defaults.

renderScale.description: The scalar allocation ceiling, or null to inherit the render defaults.

renderScaleFloor.description: The lowest dynamic grid tier, or null to use the selected tier's floor (Quarter by default).
renderScaleFloor.title: WorldRenderScaleTier

x-enumDescriptions.Native: Native resolution (scale 1): the view renders at its rect's own extent, 1280x800, and a lone whole-display view is not placed at all, so the root shows the world's output itself.
x-enumDescriptions.ThreeQuarter: Scale 221/255 (about 0.867), which the extent quantization rounds up to 0.875: 1120x700, about three quarters of the native pixel work.
x-enumDescriptions.Half: Scale 181/255 (about 0.710), which the extent quantization rounds up to 0.75: 960x600, about 0.56 of the native pixel work.
x-enumDescriptions.Quarter: Scale 128/255 (about 0.502), which the extent quantization rounds up to 0.5625: 720x450, about 0.32 of the native pixel work.
x-enumDescriptions.Eighth: Scale 90/255 (about 0.353), which the extent quantization rounds up to 0.375: 480x300, about 0.14 of the native pixel work; the most aggressive tier.

tier.description: The authored quality preset whose floor this view uses.

items.title: WorldViewQuality

programs.description: The named camera programs no camera or seat resolves through directly: the framings a SelectProgram or Blend names, such as the cases a seat rig selects between. Programs is what a reader resolves through.

builtinTransition.description: The ease into or out of the built-in seat ladder (the composition no authored layout selects), or null for the neutral WorldViewTransition defaults (a cut). An authored layout brings its own envelope.

framings.description: The framings a seat's camera eases to while their conditions hold (WorldSeatFraming), or null for none.

items.description: One row of views.framings: a framing a seat's camera eases to, in place of its chase framing, while a condition holds, such as a seat at a bench, an instrument or a desk. Each frame a seat holds the first row, in document order, whose When reads positive for it; its camera eases onto Program, resolved against the seat's own body pose, and back once no row holds. The ease is timed by the program's own dynamics op, or by the seat rig's where it authors none. Presentation only: the rules that seat a player and the state they write stay the document's.

id.description: The row's stable id, unique within the section; the camera read-back names the held row by it.

It never changes the field or the bake; the views pass draws it crisp at the pixel. A plane stroked at a half-width paints a stripe, an extruded ellipse prism stroked paints a ring projected along its axis, and a thin sweep paints a curved line where it crosses the surface.

type.description: The primitive, read as a shape's type: every primitive but a path profile.

color.description: The paint's color, #RRGGBB or a state binding.

Exact when the offset clears the profile's radial extent (a torus-like solid); a harmless conservative underestimate near the axis when the profile crosses it (offset 0 = a solid of revolution centred on the axis, e.g. a spheroid from an ellipse). Always 1-Lipschitz.
x-enumDescriptions.Extrude: Extrude the 2D profile along the local Z axis (the extrude lift operator) to the given half-height (the shape's liftAmount): a prism/slab whose cross-section is the exact 2D shape. Exact for any exact 2D field, and 1-Lipschitz.

chamfer.description: The cap chamfer radius, as a shape's.

radiusEnd.description: The sweep radius at t = 1; finite and strictly positive.

twist.description: The strand orbit rate, in turns along the curve (null = 0); finite.

strandOffset.description: The strand orbit radius, in creation units (null = 0); non-negative, finite, refused past MaxSweepStrandOffsetRatio times max(RadiusStart, RadiusEnd).

Every kind decides per CELL with integer hashes and Q48.16 arithmetic only, so a fill is bit-identical on every machine and backend -- lattice values are simulation state. The Field member is compile-stamped from the carrying row (see Compile) and omitted in the document.

anyOf.description: Every cell whose XZ centre lies in the rectangle takes Value.

minX.description: The rectangle's least X, world units.

minZ.description: The rectangle's least Z, world units.

anyOf.description: Patchy fill: fixed-point hash-lattice fBm over the CELL INDEX decides each cell. Where the octave sum n (in [0, 1]) reaches Threshold, the cell takes Value · (n − Threshold) / (1 − Threshold) -- a smooth patch interior rising to the full value. The hash folds the fill's Seed with the world seed (the generation section's reroll lever), and every blend runs in Q48.16, so two boots of one document at one seed are bit-identical.

value.description: The peak value written inside a patch.

frequency.description: Lattice cells per noise cell reciprocal -- noise-cell edge in CELLS (e.g. 8 = one noise cell spans 8 lattice cells). At least 1.

threshold.description: The patch admission level in [0, 1); higher = sparser patches.

seed.description: The hash seed, folded with the world seed.

field.description: Gets the filled row's name -- compile-stamped, never authored inside a trait.

anyOf.description: Scattered discs: one jittered point per Spacing-cell block (integer-hash offset), and every cell within Radius cells of a point takes Value -- the CPU boot-fill sibling of the renderer's CellJitter scatter.

value.description: The value written inside each disc.

spacing.description: The scatter block edge in CELLS (at least 2).

radius.description: The disc radius in CELLS (at least 1; must leave the disc inside its block's jitter envelope, refused otherwise).

seed.description: The hash seed, folded with the world seed.

field.description: Gets the filled row's name -- compile-stamped, never authored inside a trait.

anyOf.description: Every cell drawn from a numeric authored-randomness source — the per-cell lattice draw. The fill is one pass of the row's own draw stream (seeded through the same ladder as a state-row site, under the row's state.<row> descriptor): the cells, in cell-index order, each take the next sample the row's stream draws from drawCursor, so a weighted source under an exhausting mode draws its units across the field and restarts as it goes. The pass advances the cursor by the raw words it consumed, a bounded range's rejected words included. The row's DrawCursor/DrawnMasks name the pass currently painted; generate <row> advances them one whole pass and repaints. Draw occupies its authored paint position (overwriting earlier fills and preceding later fills); boot, rebuild, load/reset, and a draw-rewinding undo repaint the pass the document names.

x-enumDescriptions.Markov: The weighted-transition walk over Contexts — reads Start/Bound/Contexts/ Mode, writes text. The only source that deals (see GeneratorMode) and the only one whose emission costs more than one sample.
x-enumDescriptions.UniformRange: One draw over the closed integer range [RangeMin, RangeMax] — reads only those two fields, writes an int or fixed value. The shared Maths rejection sampler makes every accepted value equally likely. The cursor counts all raw words, including rejected words. A result attempts at most MaxBoundedAttempts words, then refuses without a biased fallback.
x-enumDescriptions.WeightedNumeric: One alias-table draw over Weighted's numeric outcomes — reads that field and Mode, writes an int or fixed value. Each outcome's probability is exactly its weight over the total. A draw takes two advances, plus the raw words of one exact wide draw on the one word in 2³² that lands on a column's threshold; the result reports the advances consumed, and the Markov walk pays the same per token. Under an exhausting mode the outcomes are drawn through the site's one DrawnMasks mask, which is the numeric shuffle bag.
x-enumDescriptions.StreamDraw: One raw, unshaped 32-bit draw off the site's own stream — no range, no weights — widened into the target's raw value as-is. One fixed-cost advance per draw. The unshaped-entropy primitive: no distribution is applied.
x-enumDescriptions.SymmetryOrbit: One uniform draw over an orbit of the symmetry lattice: the thirty nodes of Ring, or the nodes Node visits under Word (the lattice's own cycle when none is authored, so the node's ring) — reads those fields and Mode, writes the node index in the site's displayed unit (a fixed site stores node.0, the phase a cycle trait reads). The units are the orbit's nodes in walk order, equally weighted, drawn under an exhausting mode through the site's one DrawnMasks mask exactly as a weighted numeric source is; two advances per draw, plus the rare exact wide draw a weighted numeric source takes.

start.description: Markov only: the context every emission begins from. Must name a declared context.

bound.description: Markov only: the maximum tokens one emission may draw before refusing by name, 1..MaxEmissionBound. Left at DefaultBound by a numeric source.

contexts.description: Markov only: the declared contexts, at least one, uniquely keyed.

items.description: One named context of a StateGenerator — the state the walk may be sitting in and the weighted alternatives it may pick while there. A context declaring NO alternatives is TERMINAL: reaching it ends the emission.

key.description: The stable context key, unique within the generator.

alternatives.description: The weighted alternatives out of this context, or empty for a terminal context.

items.description: One weighted alternative of a GeneratorContext: the token it emits, its relative weight, and the context the walk moves into after it is picked. The authored Next is what makes this a real Markov process rather than a bag of independent draws — the context key is the process state, so an author folds exactly as much history into it as the chain needs.

token.description: The opaque game-authored token this alternative emits. The engine never interprets it; it is space-joined with the emission's other tokens and written into the target text cell. Bounded by MaxTokenLength.

weight.description: The alternative's positive relative weight. At least one alternative in a context must carry a non-zero weight.

next.description: The context the walk moves into after this alternative is picked. Must name a declared Key; naming a context that declares NO alternatives ends the emission (a terminal is a context with nothing to say, never a reserved token spelling).

multiplicity.description: How many units of this alternative one pass holds, at least one; null is one. Under WithReplacement a multiplicity only scales the weight; under an exhausting mode each unit is drawn once per pass. A context's units total at most MaxEntriesPerSet.

x-enumDescriptions.WithReplacement: Every sample leaves the entry set unchanged — the ordinary weighted draw.
x-enumDescriptions.WithoutReplacement: Each entry may be drawn at most once per pass; a set whose entries are all drawn refuses the whole emission by name (never a silent stall, never a re-draw).
x-enumDescriptions.RestartOnExhaustion: Each entry may be drawn at most once per pass; a set whose entries are all drawn clears its mask and draws again from the full set, deterministically, in the same emission — the shuffle bag.

rangeMin.description: UniformRange only: the closed range's inclusive lower bound — both bounds present or neither. Raw-encoded per the destination site's CellKind (raw FixedQ4816 bits for a fixed site) — unlike a site row's own min/max, which a fixed row authors as decimal text, since a source is not bound to one site and cannot know the kind it will write.

rangeMax.description: UniformRange only: the inclusive upper bound, same encoding as RangeMin.

weighted.description: WeightedNumeric only: the weighted numeric outcomes, at least one, at least one carrying a non-zero weight; under an exhausting Mode each outcome contributes Multiplicity units to the pass.

items.description: One numeric outcome of a WeightedNumeric source: the raw value it writes and its relative weight — the numeric twin of GeneratorAlternative, minus Token (nothing to join into text) and Next (a numeric draw is one terminal pick, never a walk).

value.description: The raw value this outcome writes on selection (a plain integer for Int, raw FixedQ4816 bits for Fixed).

weight.description: The outcome's relative weight, fed straight to Puck.Maths.WeightedSampler's exact ulong overload. At least one outcome must carry a non-zero weight.

multiplicity.description: How many units of this outcome one pass holds, at least one; null is one. Under WithReplacement a multiplicity only scales the weight; under an exhausting mode each unit is drawn once per pass, so an outcome that should come out twice per pass declares 2 rather than being authored twice. A source's units total at most MaxEntriesPerSet.

simulation.description: The authored simulation rate, when the world authors one.

rateHz.description: The simulation rate in Hz. Zero is a legal, distinct rate: a resident, non-stepping world — a static diorama the authoritative server never advances a fixed step for, though it still applies ordered submissions (mutations, session requests, connects/disconnects) through the administrative drain, so a rate-0 world can accept the very write that revives it. At rate 0, a simulation-tick duration authored as a positive value means never — not zero and not "already expired" — since there is no tick mapping for a world that never advances (see CompiledTickDuration, PopulationReconnectGraceTicks). A positive rate must be a divisor of TicksPerSecond (50400) exactly, so Puck.Maths.FixedTickConversion.PerRate always derives a whole engine-tick step width — never truncated, never remainder-carried (WorldDefinitionValidator refuses a non-divisor, naming the nearest valid rates; a negative rate is refused outright, at any magnitude). 45 and 90 Hz — Steam Deck OLED's two refresh rates — both divide 50400 exactly (1120 and 560 engine ticks per step). The engine holds no rate of its own: an authored section states its rate, and a world authoring no simulation section runs at UnauthoredSimulationRateHz — the distinct rate-0 resident world is reached only by authoring rateHz 0 by name. The derived-floor seam. This record is deliberately the one place a follow-on validation pass adds the physics floor (from body size/speed), the interactivity floor (from input latency), and the representable band; these floors are not built yet. The rigid solver already clamps authored contact frequency to RateHz * n / 8 at substep count n, supplied by collision.bodyContacts.rigidSubstepCeiling. It coincides with RateHz / 4 only at n = 2. A derived floor belongs here, beside the rate it constrains, never as a second section.

Evaluated over every carrier pair (or every occupant) each tick with the matched carriers bound as $left/$right, and compiled through the same effect compiler a WorldRule uses, so it rides the same edge/level latch (kept per pair), journal, and undo.

name.description: The interaction's stable name — unique within the section (a separate namespace from Name, so the two may coincide without colliding). A CellName, never $-prefixed — that prefix marks what the engine mints, and nothing mints an interaction.

left.description: A property name, validated against the declared properties registry — every body whose cell in that keyed row reads nonzero is a left carrier.

right.description: For Distance, a second property name, validated the same way as Left. For Region, a placement id carrying a region facet — validated against the declared placements section instead, never against the property registry.

x-enumDescriptions.Distance: Every pair of a body tagged Left and a different body tagged Right within Range of one another — property x property; the pair is bound as $left/$right.
x-enumDescriptions.Region: Every body tagged Left inside the region of the placement Right names — property x region; the occupant is bound as $left.

range.description: The distance threshold, for Distance alone — an exact JSON decimal lowered directly to deterministic fixed point, with no binary32 intermediate. Ignored (and unchecked) under Region.

mode.description: Whether the interaction fires every tick the co-occurrence holds For a distance interaction, at most this many right carriers per left carrier — the nearest first, ties broken by the lower body index — or null for every carrier in range. The work sheet prices the pair count at this budget. (Level) or once per crossing (Edge, the default — an interaction that transforms/spawns/despawns almost always wants Edge, for the same reason a rule that writes a row does: level-firing a spawn is a journal entry every tick the co-occurrence holds).

x-enumDescriptions.Level: Fires every evaluation the condition holds — the default, and the right shape for a continuous effect (a per-tick drain, a standing impulse).
x-enumDescriptions.Edge: Fires once on the condition crossing from not-holding to holding, and re-arms only when it crosses back — the right shape for anything that writes a document row, since a level-triggered write fires once per tick the condition holds rather than once per crossing.

Authored data only: a row asserts nothing about the named world's existence or shape at boot — resolution is a consumer's job, not this section's (no boot-time existence check). Names its target through exactly one of two mutually exclusive spellings — a local document path (Document), or a remote owner-named world (Owner+World together, since worlds ARE users) — never both, never neither; ValidateReferences refuses any other shape. NeighbourKey folds whichever spelling was authored into the one opaque string every IWorldNeighbourResolver call site already passes around.

A WorldReference names a document; a destination decides how an instance of that document is minted and reused. Several destinations may select one reference differently — a fresh group dungeon, a persisted user workshop, and a shared global zone can all point at the same document.

items.description: One intentional adjacency between two authority-owned regions. It is topology, not visible furniture: no placement, screen, or portal is required. The compiler derives the overlap needed for observation, interaction, grounding, and handoff from the two delivered documents.

name.description: This document's stable name for the edge.
name.title: SafeName

destination.description: A global persisted destination naming the neighbouring authority.

counterpart.description: The reciprocal adjacency row in the destination document.

center.description: The boundary rectangle's center in this world's coordinates.

outwardYawDegrees.description: The outward heading, in degrees (0 = +Z, 90 = +X). It also fixes the rectangle's own right axis, which is the yaw's horizontal right whatever the pitch — so on a face lying flat, where the heading contributes nothing to the outward direction, this is the rectangle's roll about the vertical and the arrival turn it gives the seam is still counterpartYaw - thisYaw - 180 (MapVector). An untwisted seam therefore authors its two yaws 180 degrees apart whether it stands as a wall or lies flat as a floor.

width.description: The full span along the boundary's local right axis.

height.description: The full span along the boundary's local up axis.

x-enumDescriptions.Closed: The handoff is refused and the local authority stays authoritative. At a boundary a body walks through, one whose frame is yaw-only, the body is clamped one raw unit inside it, as against closed terrain. At a pitched boundary, a floor or a ceiling, the body keeps its pose and its velocity and goes on moving under the local authority: a clamp there would pin a falling body in mid-air at the plane.

onUnavailable.description: Optional declared channel pressed once on the body after the engine applies the failure treatment. Use a kit action on this channel for authored sound, animation, state, or other feedback; ownership safety never depends on the binding.

capacity.description: The maximum number of live bodies and outstanding reservations admitted through this border at once, or null to use the destination population's remaining capacity — the same policy Capacity gives portal furniture. A full border refuses the current attempt immediately; it never queues.

livenessGraceSeconds.description: How long this edge may go without a delivered neighbour refresh before the world calls the link dropped — the authored threshold behind the linkEstablished/linkDropped world event family and the $link:<name> reserved rule channel (LinkPrefix). Authored in seconds — a physical unit, so a world's SimulationRateHz can change without silently retuning the window — and compiled per document through AdjacencyLivenessGraceTicks, exactly the population.reconnectGraceSeconds idiom. 0 (the default) disables liveness sensing for this edge outright: no link edge is emitted for it and $link: reads 0 forever, so a world authoring none is unchanged. Per row, not per world: each seam carries its own tolerance. A world whose rate is 0 has no tick mapping for a positive value (see CompiledTickDuration), which reads as never dropped.

hysteresis.description: An authored non-negative minimum ownership deadband in world units. The runtime still derives its contact/vertical safety threshold and uses the larger value; authoring this can widen a seam but never weaken its safety floor. Reciprocal rows must agree.

presentation.description: How a presentation of this world shows a seat that crossed the edge. Absent is Joined.
presentation.title: WorldAdjacencyPresentation

x-enumDescriptions.Joined: One place: a seat that crossed stays presented in the frame of the world it left, the neighbour's ground and bodies drawn in the seam's band (a doorway between two rooms of a quilt).
x-enumDescriptions.Apart: Two places: a seat that crossed is presented in the neighbour's own scene, with its sky, its lights and its bodies as they look there, as a traveller through a portal is (a sky seam between a planet and a moon, where the crossing leaves the band far behind).

observations.description: Explicitly disclosed state observations, without draw bookkeeping: each cell as stored, with the value-over-time trait that governs it.

items.description: A presentation observation, without draw seeds, cursors, masks or grants: each cell as it is stored, with the value-over-time trait that governs it (WorldObservedCell). HiddenCount counts the cells the row's Hidden policy withheld from this observer (placeholders included), zero under Omit. Space names a Vector row's vector space, and is absent for every other kind. Min and Max are the row's declared envelope, which an eased read is clamped to and a bound value is read against. Domain carries the disclosed storage shape (slot or keys), without authority-only domain dependencies; Capacity is the authored ceiling, never a live reservation or member count.

x-enumDescriptions.Int: A whole 64-bit signed integer cell (a score, a round counter, an inventory count, or — declaring min zero — a tick-count timer).
x-enumDescriptions.Fixed: A fixed-point cell holding raw FixedQ4816 bits — the deterministic replacement for a float in simulation state. Human-authored surfaces (document JSON, console verb arguments, validator refusal text, read-back echoes) use the decimal representation via FixedQ4816.TryParse/ToString; only the addon ABI channel wire and the per-cell mutation payload carry the raw bit pattern.
x-enumDescriptions.Bool: A boolean cell (a win flag, a toggle). Carries no range — a gauge cannot bind to it.
x-enumDescriptions.Text: A short-text cell (a status label, a player name slot), bounded to MaxTextValueLength UTF-16 code units. Carries no range — a gauge cannot bind to it. The only kind whose value is carried in Text rather than Value.
x-enumDescriptions.Vector: A vector cell holding an admitted, normalized signed 8-bit embedding vector, carried in Vector rather than Value or Text.

items.description: A disclosed cell, or, under Placeholder, an anonymous card back (Hidden true, empty key, zero value, no text, no observation). A cell under a value-over-time trait carries its stored value as Value beside the one trait that governs it (Advance, Cycle or Dynamics) and the Clock that trait reads, exactly as the cell is stored: an advancing cell its base and epoch engine tick, a cycling cell its phase, epoch tick and substep remainder, and an eased cell its target, which a .$target read answers, with the epoch tick and the follower's position and velocity. A reader evaluates the trait at the tick it presents with the engine's own fixed-point computation, so it presents what the authority presents at every tick, and nothing is sent while the value only moves as its trait says.

key.description: The cell's key.

value.description: The stored value: the base an advance or a cycle turns from, or the target an eased cell follows.

text.description: The text of a Text cell.

visible.description: Whether the latest explicit refresh sees this token.

hidden.description: Whether the cell is an anonymous placeholder.

perSecondNumerator.description: The per-second rate's signed numerator, in the row's own displayed unit (see this type's remarks). Negative accumulates downward (decay); zero is declared but inert.

perSecondDenominator.description: The per-second rate's denominator. Refused at zero or below.

cycle.description: The rotation a cycling cell turns by, or null.

word.description: The generator as a word of reflections — mirror nodes, one to eight, applied first to last — or null for the lattice's own cycle. A word that moves no node is refused: it loops nothing.

power.description: How many applications of the generator one step is; nonzero, and smaller in magnitude than the generator's order, since a power reduces modulo the order and a multiple of it would be the identity.

x-enumDescriptions.Turns: The rotation as a fraction of one turn, ⌊step · 2^16 / order⌋ in raw FixedQ4816 bits, so the value wraps once per loop the way a state clock reads its row — a fixed cell.
x-enumDescriptions.Cos: The unit rotation's cosine, the real part of the order's root of unity at the step — a fixed cell.
x-enumDescriptions.Sin: The unit rotation's sine, the imaginary part of that root of unity — a fixed cell.
x-enumDescriptions.Node: The symmetry-lattice node the phase node has been carried to along its orbit under the generator, in [0, 240) — an int cell whose stored value is the node the walk starts from.
x-enumDescriptions.ProjectionX: The current node's projected X coordinate on the plane of eight concentric rings — a fixed cell.
x-enumDescriptions.ProjectionY: The current node's projected Y coordinate on that plane — a fixed cell.
x-enumDescriptions.Ring: The ring, 0..7, the current node lies on — an int cell; constant along the lattice's own cycle, and a value that moves under a word whose orbits cross rings.

epochTick.description: The simulation tick this clock's rotation is measured from — the tick the cell's base value was last explicitly set, or its own behavior last changed. Read by StateCycle. A negative value is refused; in practice this can only be violated by an authored boot document, since every live settle rebases to the applying tick before validation sees it.

epochEngineTick.description: The engine tick (TicksPerSecond per second) this clock's accumulation is measured from — the engine tick the cell's base value was last explicitly set, or its own behavior last changed. Read by StateAdvance alone; never derived from EpochTick at a simulation rate, since a live rate change must move neither. A negative value is refused, for the same reason EpochTick is.

spaces.description: The vector spaces the disclosed vector rows among Observations name, and no other: a space declares only a model, a revision, and a dimension count, and a vector row loads only against its own.

model.description: The model name, non-empty and at most 128 characters.

revision.description: The model revision, non-empty and at most 128 characters.

timeline.description: The world's clocks as a recipient evaluates them from the tick it presents: each tick clock as authored, and each state clock a carried value keys on as an anchored clock holding the anchor of its phase the recipient was last sent (WorldClockAnchorLedger), never the row it reads. A state clock no carried value keys on does not cross.

items.description: One named presentation clock: a tick clock, whose phase advances with the simulation's engine tick through a period; a state clock, whose phase is the fractional part of a state row's presented value (an advancing row wraps once per unit); or a view clock, whose phase is how far the viewer stands from a point (WorldClockView). A projection carries a state clock as an anchored clock instead, whose phase its recipient predicts from the anchor at the tick it presents (WorldClockAnchor); a document never authors one.

name.description: The clock's name, unique within the section.

periodSeconds.description: A tick clock's period, in seconds: a whole number of engine ticks (1/50400 s). Refused beside State.

spanSeconds.description: What one period reads as, in the units a key's time is authored in: a day that passes in twenty minutes and reads as twenty-four hours has a span of 24h. Absent reads as the period for a tick clock, as one for a state clock, and as the distance a view clock covers, so its keys are authored in metres past its near end.

startSeconds.description: How far into its span a tick clock stands at engine tick zero, in SpanSeconds' units, in [0, span). Absent is zero. Refused on a state clock.

state.description: A state clock's Fixed or Int row. Refused beside PeriodSeconds.

anchor.description: An anchored clock's anchor: what a projection carries for a state clock it discloses, in place of the row. Refused in an authored document. An anchored clock carrying none reads no phase, as the state clock it stands for reads none while its row holds no number.

tick.description: The engine tick the anchor stands at.

phase.description: The phase at Tick, a whole turn being 2^64.

rate.description: The phase one authoritative tick adds, wrapping; zero for a clock held still.

step.description: The engine ticks one authoritative tick spans; zero exactly when Rate is.

anchor.title: WorldClockAnchor

view.description: A view clock's measure of where the viewer stands. Refused beside State and PeriodSeconds.

to.description: The distance from Origin at which the phase reaches the end of the span, in metres; greater than From.

from.description: The distance at which the phase leaves zero, in metres. Absent is zero.

origin.description: The point distances are measured from. Absent is the world's origin.

axis.description: The direction distances are measured along, which need not be a unit vector: the viewer's offset from the origin projected on it, so a viewer behind the origin reads zero. Absent measures in every direction, the length of the offset.
