items.title: WorldClock

timeline.title: WorldTimelineSection

items.description: A named puck.music.v1 score and the SHA-256 pin of its canonical bytes. Authoring resolves its file beside the world document. Recipient projections carry the pinned bytes.

name.description: The row's stable name — its mutation address.

source.description: The authored document path or the embedded canonical score in a recipient projection.

hash.description: The SHA-256 hex64 of the referenced document's canonical bytes.

items.title: WorldMusicRow

haptics.description: The world's authored haptic pulse rows driven by delivered state, evaluated per local seat by the haptic director.

items.description: One row of the haptics document section: a world-authored pad pulse driven by presentation state.

id.description: The row's stable id, unique within haptics.

durationSeconds.description: The finite pulse duration, in seconds ((0, MaxDurationSeconds]).

signal.description: The state-driven trigger scalar for Rise and Change modes; omitted in Level mode.

x-enumDescriptions.Level: Continuous motor drive: while Low or High is positive, the pad motors run at those intensities, re-armed within DurationSeconds and stopped when both return to zero.
x-enumDescriptions.Rise: Rising-edge pulse: fires one finite pulse of DurationSeconds at (Low, High) when Signal transitions from non-positive to positive.
x-enumDescriptions.Change: Change-edge pulse: fires one finite pulse of DurationSeconds at (Low, High) whenever Signal changes to a new finite value after initial observation.

seat.description: Optional target seat (seat1..seat4), or null for every local joined seat.

items.title: WorldHapticRow

keyLights.description: The world's authored keyboard lamp section, painted per local seat from delivered state.

idle.description: The color of every key no lit row names.

flash.description: The color a flashing key starts from when its row authors no flash color of its own.

modifier.description: The color of a held chord modifier's key.

unavailableScale.description: The brightness, in [0, 1], a row's color keeps while the row is unavailable.

flashSeconds.description: The seconds a flash takes to fade back to the key's own color. Positive, at most MaxFlashSeconds.

items.description: One row of keyLights: a set of keys and the color they take. The keys are the union of what the row names three ways, each optional: Keys literally, Bound through the seat's active binding page, and Character through the key that types it.

id.description: The row's stable id, unique within the section.

color.description: The color the row's keys take.

bound.description: Binding entry ids: the keyboard sources the seat's active page binds each entry to, so the lamps follow a page change and a player's rebinding.

character.description: A Unicode scalar value, usually a state cell: the key that types it lights, and a letter lights its key whatever its case. A value no key types (zero included) lights nothing.

lit.description: The row paints while this is positive; absent, it always paints.

available.description: The row is dimmed by UnavailableScale while this is not positive; absent, it is never dimmed.

flashSignal.description: The row's keys flash each time this changes to a new value after it is first read.

flashColor.description: The color the row's flash starts from; absent, the section's Flash.

seat.description: The seat whose keyboard the row lights (seat1..seat4), or null for every local seat that holds one.

items.title: WorldKeyLightRow

keyLights.title: WorldKeyLightSection

highlights.description: The world's authored highlight rows, triggered by delivered state.

items.description: One row of the highlights document section: a run of presented frames a world asks the host to keep. Each time Signal changes to a new value after it is first read, the host writes the next Frames presented frames as images under its own capture directory, named for the row. A document names no path: where a player's files go is the host's. Presentation only, and a host that composes no frame capture ignores the section.

id.description: The row's stable id, unique within the section, and the name its files carry.

frames.description: How many presented frames one trigger writes, from 1 to MaxFrames.

delaySeconds.description: The seconds between the trigger and the first written frame, so a still shows what the trigger led to, from 0 to MaxDelaySeconds.

items.title: WorldHighlightRow

shades.description: The shade programs the render defaults and the prototype bodies name by key (WorldShadeTable): a body travels naming its programs, never holding them, so each program crosses once however many bodies use it.

additionalProperties.description: The source-level expression graph serialized in a material. Admission always compiles it afresh.

items.description: A runtime slot's type and initial data. Names bind source references and do not enter program identity.
items.title: SdfShadeParameter

items.description: An output expression; omitted outputs retain the stage's default.
items.title: SdfShadeOutput

items.description: A dependency-ordered value in the canonical document. Reads may name only earlier values of this phase.
items.title: SdfShadeValue

additionalProperties.title: SdfShadeDefinition

text.description: The world's font catalog: each font by name, content pin and generated subset, so a recipient draws the text its screens and creations carry. A font's source path is a label on a recipient; its bytes are read by the pin (Resolver).
text.title: TextFontCatalogDefinition

machines.description: The world's machines, projected (see WorldProjectedMachine), so a recipient knows what each machine screen shows.

items.description: One machine as a visitor's client sees it: what the device is and what it is cabled to, which is what a screen showing it and a client running it from its inputs both read. The projection document's own row type, not a WorldMachine with holes: it carries no member for the machine's memory bindings, which tie its hardware to state rows a projection does not carry, nor for its contentFolders and preferFolderDefault, which name places on the authority's disk and are read only by the authority that mounts from them. The content a machine runs is named by pin where the machine's state is delivered, never by a folder.

name.description: The instance identity a screen's machine source names.

configuration.description: The provider's versioned configuration. A path inside it is a label on a recipient: nothing a delivery names is opened.
configuration.$comment: Open payload: this member's shape is decided by an id named elsewhere in the document, never by this generator.

running.description: Whether the authority advances the instance.

cable.description: The standing cable endpoint, when the machine authors one: linked machines step as one unit, so a recipient reads which machines a unit holds.

name.description: The cable's stable kebab-case name, shared by every plugged port.

position.description: This machine's 0-based place in cable order — contiguous across the cable's ports (validated), and what decides the linking engine's deterministic player order.

cable.title: WorldMachineCable

items.title: WorldProjectedMachine

schema.description: Gets the document schema tag — SchemaVersion for a well-formed projection. A document that omits it is refused: the initializer names what the canonical writer emits, and does not stand in for a tag a peer left out.

anyOf.description: A state.<row>[.<key>] reference the containing document resolves from a cell.

ShadowTier.description: The engine-wide shadow tier: whether the shadow cascades render, and at what resolution. Each step down halves every cascade's texels along each side, a quarter of its memory and fill, so its shadows soften and lose their finest contacts over the same reach.
ShadowTier.title: ShadowTier

x-enumDescriptions.Off: No shadows: no cascade renders or is held, and every light goes unshadowed.
x-enumDescriptions.Low: Cascades at a quarter of the full resolution, 512 texels a side.
x-enumDescriptions.Medium: Cascades at half the full resolution, 1024 texels a side.
x-enumDescriptions.High: Cascades at the full resolution, 2048 texels a side.

WorldRenderScaleTier.description: The enumerated world render-scale tiers a player picks at the console and a view's floor names, over the continuous render-scale ceiling a view carries (SdfViewSnapshot.RenderScale). A view's output keeps its rect's extent; below native it traces and shades a grid of that extent times its render scale, rounded up on each axis to a step of the render graph's extent quantization (RenderGraphExtent.Quantize, sixteen steps per power-of-two octave), and its own resolve pass reconstructs the grid into the output at world.upscale-sharpness. A layout transition's dip moves that grid inside the ceiling (SdfViewSnapshot.ResolvedRenderScale); the enumerated set lives only at the user surface. WorldRenderScaleTiers is the one definition of the names and scales, which the quality presets' floors, the console world.render-scale verb and the per-view floors read; a ceiling is a scalar. Each extent below is a lone whole-display view at 1280x800.
WorldRenderScaleTier.title: WorldRenderScaleTier

x-enumDescriptions.Native: Native resolution (scale 1): the view renders at its rect's own extent, 1280x800, and a lone whole-display view is not placed at all, so the root shows the world's output itself.
x-enumDescriptions.ThreeQuarter: Scale 221/255 (about 0.867), which the extent quantization rounds up to 0.875: 1120x700, about three quarters of the native pixel work.
x-enumDescriptions.Half: Scale 181/255 (about 0.710), which the extent quantization rounds up to 0.75: 960x600, about 0.56 of the native pixel work.
x-enumDescriptions.Quarter: Scale 128/255 (about 0.502), which the extent quantization rounds up to 0.5625: 720x450, about 0.32 of the native pixel work.
x-enumDescriptions.Eighth: Scale 90/255 (about 0.353), which the extent quantization rounds up to 0.375: 480x300, about 0.14 of the native pixel work; the most aggressive tier.

x-enumDescriptions.Off: No indirect light: the coarse volume occludes, and none of its light is applied.

WorldDistantShadows.description: The key light's distant shadow map: one more shadow map past the far cascade, with texels of its own, so ridges shadow walls hundreds of metres off without costing the near cascades precision. It draws only what stands still and holds what it drew while the light turns within TurnDegrees and the eye stays within an eighth of the reach of where it was centred, so it costs a frame nothing between those changes. A device's quality row chooses it (DistantShadows); a view's shadow quality halves its texels as it does the cascades'.

reach.description: The distance, in metres from the eye in every direction, the map covers: past the far cascade's reach and up to the far distance, within [1, 8192].

texels.description: The texels along each side of the map at full shadow quality: a power of two from 256 through 4096. Its texel is about twice the reach over this.

turnDegrees.description: The light turn, in degrees, a held map tolerates before it is drawn again: the most its shadows lag a moving sun by, within [0, 10]. Zero, the default, takes the engine's: the turn that moves the shadow of a caster as tall as the reach by a quarter of the penumbra the surface pass draws for it and a texel besides.

frames.description: The fewest frames one redraw is spread over, from 1 through MaxFrames: each draws a share of the casters, and the map the receivers read changes only once the last share lands. The world's shadows spread a redraw over more frames where its measured work asks.

WorldDistantShadows.title: WorldDistantShadows

WorldFarShadows.description: How the key light's far shadow cascade keeps up with what moves: the casters that moved are drawn again Hertz times a second of presentation time, and the cascade is drawn whole again when the light turns past TurnDegrees, the eye crosses an eighth of its reach or a static caster changes, that redraw spread over at least the frames of one period. A dynamic caster's shadow lags it by up to one period, and every shadow lags a turning light by up to the turn. A device's quality row chooses it (FarShadows).

hertz.description: The refreshes a second, a whole number from 1 through MaxHertz, where MaxHertz draws moved casters every frame.

turnDegrees.description: The light turn, in degrees, a held cascade tolerates, within [0, MaxTurnDegrees]: past it the cascade is drawn again. Zero, the default, takes the engine's: the turn that moves the shadow of a caster as tall as the reach by a quarter of the penumbra the surface pass draws for it and a texel besides.

WorldFarShadows.title: WorldFarShadows

SdfViewsRate.description: The maximum square shading footprint and the tile classified together, in render pixels.

maxRate.description: Shading samples are at most this many pixels apart along each axis.

tileSize.description: Edge length of the region that must qualify together.

SdfViewsRate.title: SdfViewsRate

x-enumDescriptions.Off: No shadows: no cascade renders or is held, and every light goes unshadowed.
x-enumDescriptions.Low: Cascades at a quarter of the full resolution, 512 texels a side.
x-enumDescriptions.Medium: Cascades at half the full resolution, 1024 texels a side.
x-enumDescriptions.High: Cascades at the full resolution, 2048 texels a side.

WorldNestedViewQuality.description: One row of the nested-view table (render.nested): what a view shown inside another (through a window or portal, on a screen a camera films, or a session's screen) gives up while it is presented at or below a share of the display's height. A nested view takes the first row, in ascending Share, whose share it does not exceed, and gives up nothing past the last row; a world with no table gives up nothing at any size, so a portal that fills the screen is lit as the room behind it.

share.description: The largest share of the display's height, in (0, 1], at which the row applies; rows ascend strictly.

shadows.description: The finest shadow tier the view keeps: Off drops its cascades, so its lights take the probes' answer. Absent keeps the world's.

ambientOcclusion.description: Whether the view keeps ambient occlusion: false drops it. Absent keeps the world's.

indirectLevels.description: How many of the viewed world's irradiance-volume levels the view reads, counted from the coarsest, at least one: that world traces, relights and publishes those alone, so a world seen through a small glass measures only its coarse light. Absent, or at least the volume's level count, reads every level.

renderScale.description: The render-scale ceiling the view renders at, in [0.125, 1] of its presented extent, below the presentation's own (the world's or device's renderScale), which every nested view keeps as its ceiling in any case. A nested view never reconstructs over time, so a reduced one is upscaled spatially. Absent keeps the presentation's.

WorldNestedViewQuality.title: WorldNestedViewQuality

WorldRenderIndirectBudget.description: The irradiance volume's budget: a light change costs a relight of the probes' cached hits and a geometry change costs a trace, each granted a count for each presented frame (never a rate of wall time, so a slow frame owes no more probe work than a fast one), and overload lengthens the lighting's age rather than the frame. A device's quality row (IndirectBudget) chooses its own. Every member is optional; an absent one leaves that part unbounded.

relightPerFrame.description: The probes relit each presented frame, at least one.

tracePerFrame.description: The probes whose hits are traced each presented frame, at least one.

age.description: The lighting age, in seconds, past which the volume reports it is behind; positive.

WorldRenderIndirectBudget.title: WorldRenderIndirectBudget

shadows.description: The soft-shadow tier the preset selects.

ambientOcclusion.description: Whether the preset enables ambient occlusion.

renderScale.description: The scalar render-scale ceiling the preset selects.

temporal.description: Whether the preset reconstructs the world's views over time (world.temporal).

dynamicResolution.description: Whether the preset moves each view's render extent with the load (world.render-scale auto).

shadowLights.description: The number of held shadow slots, from 0 through 4.

shadowFadeSlots.description: The number of additional shadow handoff slots, from 0 through 2.

shadowFadeTicks.description: The length of a shadow handoff in delivered ticks; zero selects instant changes.

shadowOverflow.description: How a crossing proceeds when its handoff capacity is occupied.
shadowOverflow.title: WorldShadowOverflow

renderScaleFloor.description: The per-view floor tier the preset selects (Quarter by default).

sky.description: The sky's quality tier the preset selects (world.sky-quality).
sky.title: WorldSkyTier

indirect.description: The indirect tier override. Absent selects Off for Low, Medium for Medium and High for High.

skyFieldScale.description: The independent sky field grid fraction, one or one half.

rayQueries.description: Whether the preset lets the indirect volume's background rays take the device's ray hardware where it has it (world.rays); the software walk answers the same hits elsewhere.

distantShadows.description: The distant shadow map the device draws past the far cascade (its reach, texels and the light turn a held map tolerates): far shadows by rasterization, which need no ray hardware. Absent draws none.

farShadows.description: How often the device refreshes the far shadow cascade and the light turn a held cascade tolerates (WorldFarShadows). Absent refreshes it every frame.

viewsRate.description: The maximum shared shading footprint and classification tile size. Absent shades every pixel.

nested.description: The nested-view table the preset runs (WorldNestedViewQuality), in place of the world's render.nested, so each device chooses what its windows, portals and filmed screens give up at each size. Absent runs the world's table.

indirectBudget.description: The irradiance work each presented frame grants the volume on this device (WorldRenderIndirectBudget), in place of the world's render.indirect.budget, so each device chooses how much lighting work it affords a frame. Absent runs the world's budget.

WorldRenderLightDirectional.description: A Lambert directional light, such as the sun.

direction.description: The direction from a lit surface toward the light, any nonzero length (normalized host-side before upload). Absent is the pinned sun direction.

color.description: The light's colour, scaled to unit luminance so the light gives exactly its illuminance. Refused beside Temperature. Absent is white, or the temperature's.

illuminance.description: The illuminance on a surface facing the light, in lux: a clear midday sun gives about 100,000, an overcast day about 10,000, the full moon about 0.3. Absent is the pinned sun's.

angularRadius.description: The light's angular radius, in [0, atan 0.3] radians: the penumbra half-slope is its tangent, so 0 casts a hard shadow. Read only when the light shadows. Absent is 0, a point source: the engine chooses no softness, and the standard package authors the soft edge its own lights cast.

shadow.description: How this light competes for shadow slots. Absent is Never. A directional without a presented shadow slot is scaled by ambient occlusion instead.

name.description: The unique identity a section key and the shadow allocator address. Required when Shadow is Always or Auto.

temperature.description: The light's colour as a black body's at this temperature, in kelvin, in [1000, 40000]: noon sunlight about 5,500, a sunset about 3,000. Refused beside Color.

bounce.description: Gets the finite nonnegative gain of this light's diffuse contribution to indirect transport. Absent is one; zero excludes it from the traced indirect light while leaving direct shading unchanged. Rim and attenuation-only lights have no diffuse contribution. Literals, state bindings and keys use the same domain.

WorldRenderLightDirectional.title: WorldRenderLightDirectional

WorldRenderLightRim.description: A view-dependent silhouette brighten: luminance · color · pow(1 − saturate(dot(normal, −rayDirection)), power), added after the material shade.

luminance.description: The luminance the brighten adds at a silhouette, in nits. Absent is zero, which adds nothing.

power.description: The falloff exponent — larger confines the highlight nearer the silhouette. Absent is the engine default.

name.description: The name a section key addresses the light by, unique among the lights.

bounce.description: Gets the finite nonnegative gain of this light's diffuse contribution to indirect transport. Absent is one; zero excludes it from the traced indirect light while leaving direct shading unchanged. Rim and attenuation-only lights have no diffuse contribution. Literals, state bindings and keys use the same domain.

WorldRenderLightRim.title: WorldRenderLightRim

WorldAnchorEntity.description: Rides one population entity's ROOT pose — a walking avatar's whole-body position and orientation.

index.description: The 0-based entity index, bounded by the world's authored population capacity.

WorldAnchorEntity.title: WorldAnchorEntity

WorldAnchorEntityPart.description: Rides one entity look's authored part pose rather than its whole-body root. The active look publishes the mapping from PartId to its packed transform slot; the slot remains an engine detail.

partId.description: The ordinal, case-sensitive part identifier published by the entity's active look.

WorldAnchorEntityPart.title: WorldAnchorEntityPart

WorldAnchorPlacement.description: Rides a placement INSTANCE's stamped transform — a creation stamped into the world by reference (the same placement-reference shape CreationCameraDocument uses), optionally narrowed to one of its own authored shapes rather than the stamp's root.

shapeId.description: The referenced creation's ShapeDocument.Id to ride, or null for the placement's own stamped root transform.

WorldAnchorPlacement.title: WorldAnchorPlacement

WorldAnchorGroup.description: Rides the smoothed CENTROID of a set of population entities — the establishing-shot anchor. Also publishes the set's SPREAD (mean distance from the centroid), which a camera program's Offset consumes through its SpreadPullback. A group has no facing, so its orientation resolves to identity.

indices.description: The 0-based entity indices in the set, or null for the whole live population (every active entity). Each index is validated against the authored population capacity.

smoothRate.description: The exponential smoothing rate (per second) the centroid/spread ease at (validated positive and finite) — seeded un-smoothed on first resolve so a camera does not fly in from the origin.

WorldAnchorGroup.title: WorldAnchorGroup

WorldAnchorSeat.description: Rides a local seat's avatar — the body the seat perceives as its own, so possession follows — at its root or at a named part. Numbernull is the enclosing seat scope (the seat a HUD frame or view is being resolved for), an explicit number is 1-based. Presentation-only: a camera or speaker on this anchor is resolved per seat.
WorldAnchorSeat.title: WorldAnchorSeat

WorldAnchorRecentSpeaker.description: Rides the body that most recently spoke (see OverlayPredicate.Speaking), at its root or a named part; resolves nothing until something has spoken.
WorldAnchorRecentSpeaker.title: WorldAnchorRecentSpeaker

WorldAnchor.description: WHERE a placeable thing rides — the one shared pose-target vocabulary a placeable WorldCamera and a placeable WorldSpeaker both consume through the SAME resolver, distinct from HOW the thing looks at or emits from that pose (a WorldCameraProgram, a feed). The $type string is the JSON discriminator; a new anchor kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.
WorldAnchor.title: WorldAnchor

WorldRenderLightPoint.description: A point light, such as a bulb: its luminous intensity alike in every direction, falling off as the inverse square of the distance under a window that ends it smoothly and exactly at its range, the distance past which its light would show below SdfPhotometry.RangeThreshold of display white at the world's brightest exposure. An unanchored light is static, so the irradiance volume traces it: its light bounces off the static meshes, and each probe records whether it sees the light, so a surface the volume covers takes the light only where the probes about it see it, and a fixture lights nothing through the wall or slab between them. An anchored light moves with its anchor, lights through every wall and bounces nothing.

position.description: The world-space position for a static (unanchored) light. Absent is the world origin. An offset in the anchor frame when an anchor is authored.

anchor.description: An entity, entity part, or placement frame. A missing live target disables the light.

color.description: The light's colour, scaled to unit luminance. Refused beside Temperature.

intensity.description: The luminous intensity, in candela. Refused beside Power; absent with it is the engine default.

name.description: The name a section key addresses the light by, unique among the lights.

power.description: The luminous power, in lumens, emitted alike in every direction: a 60 W incandescent bulb gives about 800. Refused beside Intensity.

temperature.description: The light's colour as a black body's, in kelvin, in [1000, 40000]: a warm bulb about 2,700. Refused beside Color.

bounce.description: Gets the finite nonnegative gain of this light's diffuse contribution to indirect transport. Absent is one; zero excludes it from the traced indirect light while leaving direct shading unchanged. Rim and attenuation-only lights have no diffuse contribution. Literals, state bindings and keys use the same domain.

WorldRenderLightPoint.title: WorldRenderLightPoint

WorldRenderLightSpot.description: A spot light, such as a downlight: a point light whose light leaves in a cone about its aim, at full strength inside the inner angle and smoothly to none at the outer, with the point light's windowed falloff, range, and tracing and occlusion by the irradiance volume while unanchored.

position.description: The world-space position, or the offset in the anchor's frame.

direction.description: The direction the light shines along, any nonzero length; in the anchor's frame when an anchor is authored. Absent is straight down.

anchor.description: An entity, entity part, or placement frame. A missing live target disables the light.

angle.description: The cone's outer half angle, in (0, π/2] radians. Absent is 45 degrees.

innerAngle.description: The half angle inside which the light is at full strength, in [0, Angle] radians. Absent is three quarters of Angle.

color.description: The light's colour, scaled to unit luminance. Refused beside Temperature.

intensity.description: The luminous intensity along the aim, in candela. Refused beside Power; absent with it is the engine default.

power.description: The luminous power, in lumens, emitted alike across the outer cone. Refused beside Intensity.

temperature.description: The light's colour as a black body's, in kelvin, in [1000, 40000]. Refused beside Color.

name.description: The name a section key addresses the light by, unique among the lights.

bounce.description: Gets the finite nonnegative gain of this light's diffuse contribution to indirect transport. Absent is one; zero excludes it from the traced indirect light while leaving direct shading unchanged. Rim and attenuation-only lights have no diffuse contribution. Literals, state bindings and keys use the same domain.

WorldRenderLightSpot.title: WorldRenderLightSpot

WorldRenderLightOccluder.description: A smooth attenuation field. Position is world space, or an offset in an anchored entity/part/placement frame. Missing anchors disable it. Radius is positive; Weight is in [0, 1]. It shares the lights table's capacity.

position.description: The world-space position, or the offset in the anchor's frame.

anchor.description: An entity, entity part, or placement frame.

name.description: The name a section key addresses the light by, unique among the lights.

bounce.description: Gets the finite nonnegative gain of this light's diffuse contribution to indirect transport. Absent is one; zero excludes it from the traced indirect light while leaving direct shading unchanged. Rim and attenuation-only lights have no diffuse contribution. Literals, state bindings and keys use the same domain.

WorldRenderLightOccluder.title: WorldRenderLightOccluder

WorldRenderLight.description: One light. The $type string is the JSON discriminator; a new kind is a new derived record, its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line, and its kind in SdfLightKind.
WorldRenderLight.title: WorldRenderLight

WorldRenderCurvature.description: The stylized curvature enrichment, keyed on mean curvature estimated from the baked triangle's interpolated vertex normals in world units. Every field is optional individually — absent resolves to the engine's default. The three gains share one shading gate: while all are zero their enrichment is skipped. The surface pass supplies the same curvature for edge weathering without querying the field.

cavity.description: How far a concave crease darkens, in [0, 1] at a cavity whose curvature reaches InkLow. Zero darkens none.

rim.description: How far a convex ridge brightens, in [0, 1] at a ridge whose curvature reaches InkLow. Zero brightens none.

ink.description: The ink outline's strength where the curvature magnitude spikes. Zero draws none.

inkLow.description: The curvature magnitude (1 / fillet radius, in world units) at which the outline starts and the ridge and cavity terms saturate.

inkHigh.description: The curvature magnitude at which the outline saturates.

WorldRenderCurvature.title: WorldRenderCurvature

x-enumDescriptions.Linear: Time runs evenly from this key to the next.
x-enumDescriptions.Smooth: Time starts and ends slowly: t² (3 − 2t), so the value leaves and arrives at rest.
x-enumDescriptions.Step: The value holds this key's until the next key, where it changes at once.

elevation.description: The direction's Y component this stop sits at, in [−1, 1].

color.description: BindableColor's grammar: the colour at this elevation. Absent is white.

WorldRenderSkyCone.description: A cone mask: the directions within Spread of Toward, in the sky frame.

toward.description: The cone's axis in the sky frame, any nonzero length.

spread.description: The cone's angular radius in radians, in (0, π].

WorldRenderSkyCone.title: WorldRenderSkyCone

WorldRenderSkyMask.description: Where a sky layer draws: an elevation band of the sky frame, or a cone about a direction. Exactly one of Band and Cone.

band.description: The band's lowest and highest elevation in radians, two angles in [−π/2, π/2], ascending.

feather.description: The width of the mask's edge, an angle in radians. Absent is a hard edge.

WorldRenderSkyMask.title: WorldRenderSkyMask

WorldRenderSkyTransform.description: A sky layer's own transform about the sky frame: a turn about its up, then a tilt about its right axis. Each angle may bind or key on a clock, so a layer turns over a day.

turn.description: The turn about the sky frame's up. Absent is none.

tilt.description: The tilt about the sky frame's right axis. Absent is none.

WorldRenderSkyTransform.title: WorldRenderSkyTransform

WorldRenderSkyLayerGradient.description: The colour gradient over elevation: piecewise-linear between stops, clamped to the end stops.

stops.description: Two to SdfSky.MaxStops stops, strictly ascending in elevation.

name.description: The name a section key addresses the layer by, unique among the layers.

blend.description: Gets how the layer composes over the colour beneath it. Absent is its kind's: over for a gradient, clouds, noise, a pattern and a panorama, add for stars, a sun disc, an aurora and a panel.

opacity.description: Gets the layer's opacity, in [0, 1], which scales its alpha. Zero draws nothing and counts no work. Absent is one.

mask.description: Gets where the layer draws. Absent is everywhere.

luminance.description: Gets the luminance, in nits, a colour of one shows at in this layer: every colour and brightness the layer carries scales by it (a gradient's stops, a disc's, the stars', the clouds', an aurora's, a noise's, a pattern's, a panel's, a panorama's image, a view's fallback), so the sky is as bright beside its lights as the real one: a clear sky's horizon about 7,000, a night sky well under one. Absent is SdfSky.DefaultLuminance, a clear day's sky beside the pinned sun.

WorldRenderSkyLayerView.description: Another world in the sky: a second sdf.world instance (sky$<name>) rendering the destination's session from an anchor in it, turned with the viewer's camera. Without Follow the camera stays at the anchor, so the destination is a backdrop at infinity; with it the camera moves as the viewer does, so the destination is a place at a distance that grows as the viewer nears it, and the two worlds share one frame. It renders only while the viewer's previous frame showed it, and only the rectangle its mask covers (a cone, the cone its Bound subtends, or the whole frustum with neither). x-enumDescriptions.RoundCone: A tapered capsule — a fat base narrowing to a rounded tip along +Y (teeth, horns, spikes).
x-enumDescriptions.Plane: An infinite plane bounding a solid half-space; local +Y is the outward normal.
x-enumDescriptions.Cone: A sharp circular cone with a flat base, centered along local Y.
x-enumDescriptions.Prism: A bounded profile in local XY extruded along Z. The default trapezoid has unit bottom half-width, half-height and depth, with an authored top-to-bottom width ratio (default one half). SdfPrismProfile selects rounded rectangles, polygons, ellipses, or a convex vertex list instead.
x-enumDescriptions.Superellipsoid: A generalized ellipsoid: q = pow(abs(p)/r, e); d = (pow(q.x+q.y+q.z, 1/e) - 1) * min(r), unit radii (1,1,1) and an authored exponent e in [MinSuperellipsoidExponent, MaxSuperellipsoidExponent] (the document's exponent field carries it; unauthored is the minimum, the ellipsoid itself — an Ellipsoid emits the identical instruction, since every ellipsoid is this shape at that exponent). A squircle/rounded-cube family: the minimum exponent is a plain ellipsoid, larger values round toward a box.
x-enumDescriptions.Sweep: A quadratic Bezier curve swept with a tapering, optionally bulging radius, optionally as 1-4 helical strands — see Sweep. NOT a closed solid a body can stand on in the sense the rest of this enum's members are: its field is "exact enough", not exact, and carries no Reach unit-scale law — its control points and radii already carry creation-unit dimensions directly (see SweepReach). The authoring layer admits it only with a curve facet naming its control points and radii.

SdfPrismProfileKind.description: The cross-section of a prism, in its local XY plane.
SdfPrismProfileKind.title: SdfPrismProfileKind

x-enumDescriptions.Trapezoid: A trapezoid controlled by the shape's taper.
x-enumDescriptions.RoundedRectangle: A rectangle with independently controlled corner rounding.
x-enumDescriptions.Polygon: A regular polygon, stretched by the authored X/Y scale.
x-enumDescriptions.Ellipse: An exact elliptical profile, extruded with flat front and rear caps.
x-enumDescriptions.ChamferedRectangle: A rectangle with independently controlled 45-degree corner chamfers.
x-enumDescriptions.Convex: An arbitrary convex polygon authored by Vertices, with CornerRadius reused as a uniform corner-rounding radius. The exact convex-polygon SDF, not the study's smoothed half-plane intersection.
x-enumDescriptions.Path: Filled contours or variable-width strokes, flattened with an explicit tolerance and edge budget.

SdfPathStroke.description: Round-ended stroke radii. Smooth interpolates with smoothstep over [From, To]; otherwise interpolation is linear over that interval. Parameterization gives every authored segment an equal part of [0, 1].
SdfPathStroke.title: SdfPathStroke

SdfPathShear.description: Boundary deformation: target += Offset + Linear*d + Quadratic*d² + Cubic*d³, with the other coordinate clamped to [From, To] as d. Target is 0 (X) or 1 (Y). Filled paths only; included in the subdivision error bound, so clamped polynomial bends can shape an outline without a runtime warp.
SdfPathShear.title: SdfPathShear

SdfPathSegment.description: A line, quadratic/cubic Bezier, or circular arc ending at End. An arc uses ArcCenter and Clockwise; Beziers use Control and optionally Control2. Controls are in the profile's local XY frame.
SdfPathSegment.title: SdfPathSegment

SdfPathContour.description: A continuous contour. Filled contours close implicitly; stroked contours remain open unless Closed.

segments.description: Gets the contour's segments in order, each ending where the next begins. The list is owned.

SdfPathContour.title: SdfPathContour

SdfPathProfile.description: A bounded presentation profile. Filled contours use even/odd fill, including holes. Curves are flattened once at composition, with a local-space geometric error at most Tolerance (apart from floating-point rounding). Strokes approximate the union of disks along the curve, including their varying radius, to the same tolerance. The emitted polygon/rounded-segment field is 1-Lipschitz; no margin moves its zero surface. At most 128 edges are emitted; exceeding that budget refuses instead of silently relaxing the requested tolerance.

contours.description: Gets the profile's contours, filled with even/odd fill. The list is owned, since Compile caches its edges by the profile.

SdfPathProfile.title: SdfPathProfile

SdfPrismProfile.description: Authored profile controls for a solid prism. The profile is extruded along local Z.

cornerRadius.description: A fraction in [0, 1]: the profile's smaller half-extent for RoundedRectangle's corner radius or ChamferedRectangle's chamfer radius; the scaled polygon's conservative inradius (ConvexPolygonInradius) for Convex's uniform corner rounding, also clamped to the extrusion half-depth when extruded.

path.description: Required only for Path; its points are normalized profile coordinates.

vertices.description: Gets, for Convex only, 3 to MaxConvexVertices local XY points, clockwise (X right, Y up — each turn's 2D cross product of consecutive edges strictly negative), no coincident or collinear vertices, and convex. Ignored by every other kind. The list is owned.

SdfPrismProfile.title: SdfPrismProfile

SdfLift.description: How a 2D-primitive family shape (RoundedRectangle, RegularPolygon, Star, Trapezoid, Ellipse, ChamferedRectangle) is lifted from its 2D signed-distance field into a 3D solid. The kernels read each member as SDF_LIFT_* from the generated sdf-isa.hlsli; the mode is packed into the shape instruction's Data1.y and decoded as > 0.5.
SdfLift.title: SdfLift

x-enumDescriptions.Revolve: Revolve the 2D profile around the local Y axis (the revolve lift operator): the profile sits in the (radial, Y) half-plane at a radial offset (the shape's liftAmount). Exact when the offset clears the profile's radial extent (a torus-like solid); a harmless conservative underestimate near the axis when the profile crosses it (offset 0 = a solid of revolution centred on the axis, e.g. a spheroid from an ellipse). Always 1-Lipschitz.
x-enumDescriptions.Extrude: Extrude the 2D profile along the local Z axis (the extrude lift operator) to the given half-height (the shape's liftAmount): a prism/slab whose cross-section is the exact 2D shape. Exact for any exact 2D field, and 1-Lipschitz.

a.description: The curve's first control point, in creation units.

twist.description: The strand orbit rate, in turns along the curve.

strandOffset.description: The strand orbit radius, in creation units.

SdfShadeShape.description: A structural shape descriptor. Compilation uses the existing solid/paint emission and admission.
SdfShadeShape.title: SdfShadeShape

SdfShadeExpression.description: An expression supplied to shade admission, never executable words. The compiler validates every field.

name.description: A stamp member or runtime parameter name.

type.description: The type of a literal, validated against its bits.

bits.description: 32-bit literal components; integer components are never float converted.

shape.description: The structural descriptor of a shape operation.

SdfShadeExpression.title: SdfShadeExpression

SdfShadeExpressionNonNullable.description: An expression supplied to shade admission, never executable words. The compiler validates every field.

op.description: An op-table spelling, or constant, parameter, or input.

SdfShadeOutput.description: An output expression; omitted outputs retain the stage's default.
SdfShadeOutput.title: SdfShadeOutput

SdfShadeValue.description: A dependency-ordered value in the canonical document. Reads may name only earlier values of this phase.
SdfShadeValue.title: SdfShadeValue

SdfShadeDefinition.description: The source-level expression graph serialized in a material. Admission always compiles it afresh.

ShadeReference.description: A shade program a document uses (a palette row's, a look case's or the world's default): the program's identity, and the program once the document's table has supplied it. The identity is computed from the program's canonical bytes (KeyOf), never authored, so every use of one program names one row of the world's shades table and a program used by many creations is held, written and compiled once.
ShadeReference.title: ShadeReference

anyOf.description: The key of a row of the world's shades table.

WorldScreenSourceNone.description: No provider is bound — the engine shades the slot as dark glass, lit faintly by the sun.
WorldScreenSourceNone.title: WorldScreenSourceNone

WorldScreenSourceMachine.description: A named machine output. The source is a consumer reference only: the named machine is prepared, advanced, and retired by the world's machine host independently of every display that samples it.

output.description: The provider video output name exposed by that instance.

WorldScreenSourceMachine.title: WorldScreenSourceMachine

additionalProperties.$comment: Open payload: this member's shape is decided by an id named elsewhere in the document, never by this generator.

WorldScreenSourceProducer.description: An image a registered producer makes, such as the test pattern, a QR code, a camera or a desktop capture, named by the producer's id rather than by a document kind, so a new producer needs no change here. The producer binds Settings through its own settings shape and refuses a member it does not declare, by name; WorldImageProducerSettings holds the shapes of the producers the engine ships, and WorldImageProducerVocabulary holds every registered producer's shape. Two producer sources are equal when their ids and settings are, member for member.

settings.description: The producer's settings object, or null for its defaults. Omitted from the wire when null.

WorldScreenSourceProducer.title: WorldScreenSourceProducer

WorldScreenSourceView.description: A named view from the presentation view stack, such as a monitor showing another camera's output.

cameraName.description: The registered view name this slot samples.

WorldScreenSourceView.title: WorldScreenSourceView

WorldScreenProjection.description: How a Session face's destination render projects onto the face — an ordinary head-on camera image, or a WINDOW whose image shears with the viewer's own eye so the destination scene parallaxes against the aperture the way a real opening would.
WorldScreenProjection.title: WorldScreenProjection

x-enumDescriptions.Camera: The destination renders through its own declared (or default) camera, unaffected by the viewer's position — today's behavior, unchanged for every session facet authored before this member existed.
x-enumDescriptions.Window: The destination renders through an off-axis frustum fitted to THIS face's aperture, apexed at the viewer's eye mapped through the border pair's isometry (see Puck.World.Client.WorldWindowProjectionMath, downstream of this project — see docs/project-map.md's layering) — requires this same face's Portal to author Mapped with a Counterpart (refused by name otherwise — see WorldDefinitionValidator), since the aperture and the mapping both come from the SAME border pair. CameraName is ignored under this mode — the camera is derived every produced frame, never an authored row.

WorldScreenSourceSession.description: A live rendered view of another world, resolved through a destinations row (docs/architecture/worlds.md, "Observation and display"). The face/screen resolves the same resolver-owned identity a portal crossing at the same door would land in (WorldSessionResolver), attaches an observation lease to the resolved instance's server, and mirrors just enough of its delivered definition/snapshots to render its static authored geometry through CameraName (or the destination's default projection). It never re-derives durability/scope/generation itself — those are the destination row's own facts.

destination.description: The Name this face/screen observes. Must resolve to a declared destinations row — an undeclared name refuses at boot (validated, like a portal facet's own destination).

camera.description: The destination's own placeable-camera name to render through, or null for its default projection (its first declared camera, else a fixed overview derived from its spawn points). Wire name camera. Validated only as non-empty when present at author time — the destination's own definition is not joined at boot (references assert naming intent, not reachability), so an unknown camera name is refused loudly at bind time instead, once the destination is actually resolved, falling back to the default projection rather than refusing the whole bind. Ignored under Window (see Projection).

projection.description: How the destination render projects onto this face (see WorldScreenProjection). Default Camera — unauthored worlds and every session facet authored before this member existed render byte-identically. Optional and trailing (the same widen-without-moving-existing-members shape CameraName itself already follows). Window requires this same face's Portal to author Mapped with a Counterpart — refused by name otherwise (see WorldDefinitionValidator); a top-level screens row or magazine entry carries no face to pair with, so window is refused there unconditionally.

resolution.description: The offscreen target's [width, height] in pixels, or null for the default 160x144 panel (Puck.World.Client.WorldViewInstances.DefaultSessionWidth x DefaultSessionHeight). Each axis is validated within 1..WorldDefinitionValidator.MaxSurfaceDimension. Refused under Window, which renders at the extent its glass covers on screen. Omitted from the wire when null.
resolution.title: WorldScreenResolution

fallback.description: The colour the face shows, as #RRGGBB, when the screen is as many screens deep as the presentation nests (views.nestingDepth), so two portals facing each other end on it; or null for black. Omitted from the wire when null.

ripple.description: Whether the opening ripples: its image is refracted by slow interfering waves all the time, with a faint highlight riding them, and a body that touches or passes through sends rings across the whole glass that fade within about a second. Presentation only (the shading reads the contact and the clock; nothing in the simulation depends on it). Requires Window. Omitted from the wire when false.

WorldScreenSourceSession.title: WorldScreenSourceSession

WorldScreenSourceText.description: Authored reading text on the screen face, rendered through the engine's glyph-decal tier (Puck.SdfVm.SdfWorldTables.SetScreenDecal): a fixed monospace cell grid sampled from the world's packed font atlas at shade time — the dense-text sibling of a creation's textRuns, which stamp marched Glyph geometry. Signs, plaques, books, and monitors author this; short sculptural lettering stays a text run. Requires the world to declare a text font catalog (Text); the decal bypasses the screen image pipeline, so no image source competes with it on the slot.

lines.description: The text rows, top-down; each row maps onto one grid row of cells (row-major, one scalar per cell — no kerning or shaping on this tier). State placeholders follow {state.<row>[.<key>][.$target]}; {{ and }} escape literal braces. Rows must be declared Int, Fixed, Bool or Text; an absent cell displays empty. Expanded lines clip to the grid.

font.description: The text catalog font name; null selects the catalog's default font.

columns.description: The cell grid's column count, or null to fit the widest line. The grid (columns x rows) is capped by the engine's per-screen decal cell budget; inferred columns stop at that budget, including when a live placeholder grows (Puck.SignedDistance.SdfScreenDecalLayout.MaxScreenDecalCells).

rows.description: The cell grid's row count, or null to fit the line count.

foreground.description: The letter color as #RRGGBB, or null for white.

background.description: The cell background color as #RRGGBB, or null for black.

WorldScreenSourceText.title: WorldScreenSourceText

WorldScreenSourceProbe.description: A declared probe's texture output — the frame a kind that declares an output writes each cycle (a relit camera frame, a mask), published like a camera feed. The probe must be a probes row of this document; whether its kind writes a texture is checked at boot against the kind's manifest.

id.description: The probes[].id whose output this slot shows.

WorldScreenSourceProbe.title: WorldScreenSourceProbe

WorldScreenSource.description: The signal carried by a WorldScreen's lit face. A source declares which provider feeds a slot; the engine resolves and samples it. The $type string is the JSON discriminator; a new source kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.
WorldScreenSource.title: WorldScreenSource

WorldSolid.description: A row's solidity facet — it participates in contact resolution using its own declared shape. Presence is the whole switch; null means decoration — the row is drawn but bodies pass through it.

margin.description: The signed skin added to the shape for contact purposes. Positive fattens the collider past the drawn surface; negative lets a body sink in. Compensates the smooth-union blend.

WorldSolid.title: WorldSolid

WorldCameraSubjectReference.description: The program's externally supplied reference pose — a named camera's own WorldAnchor, or a seat rig's currently perceived body (the seat's own avatar, or a possessed camera body). Resolved outside the program and handed to it as the SdfAnchor the compiled rig receives every frame.
WorldCameraSubjectReference.title: WorldCameraSubjectReference

WorldCameraSubjectPlacement.description: Rides a placement's authored stamped transform (position only — a placement carries no live facing through this static resolve, the same limitation a placeable camera's own Placement arm and a speaker share).

shapeId.description: The referenced creation's own shape to ride, or null for the placement's stamped root transform.

WorldCameraSubjectPlacement.title: WorldCameraSubjectPlacement

WorldCameraSubject.description: The subject an Anchor/LookAt op resolves against — the closed "what a camera program can key off" vocabulary. Distinct from WorldAnchor (WHERE a whole placeable camera or speaker rides, resolved OUTSIDE the program and handed in as one reference pose): this is presentation math INSIDE the program, so it stays float and needs no live entity table — a placement's pose is its rest pose (Puck.World.Client.WorldAnchorPoses.TryRestPlacement), the document-only branch of the resolver a placeable camera's own anchor and a speaker read live.
WorldCameraSubject.title: WorldCameraSubject

WorldCameraProgramOpAnchor.description: Establishes the CURRENT subject — the pose Offset/Orbit place the eye relative to, and LookAt aims along the facing of when it names no subject of its own. Also re-seeds the eye at the resolved subject's own position (the "first person" default before any Offset/Orbit runs). At most one per program, and it must be the first operation when present; a program that omits it starts from Reference implicitly.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpAnchor.title: WorldCameraProgramOpAnchor

WorldCameraProgramOpOffset.description: Places the eye at an offset from the current subject's pose.

value.description: The offset.

worldAxes.description: Whether Value uses world axes rather than the subject's own.

spreadPullback.description: The group-spread multiplier applied to the offset — meaningful only when the program's OWN externally supplied reference is a Group establishing shot (zero, and thus inert, everywhere else).

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpOffset.title: WorldCameraProgramOpOffset

WorldCameraSubjectNullable.description: The subject an Anchor/LookAt op resolves against — the closed "what a camera program can key off" vocabulary. Distinct from WorldAnchor (WHERE a whole placeable camera or speaker rides, resolved OUTSIDE the program and handed in as one reference pose): this is presentation math INSIDE the program, so it stays float and needs no live entity table — a placement's pose is its rest pose (Puck.World.Client.WorldAnchorPoses.TryRestPlacement), the document-only branch of the resolver a placeable camera's own anchor and a speaker read live.
WorldCameraSubjectNullable.title: WorldCameraSubject

subject.description: The subject to look at, or null to look along the current subject's own forward axis from the eye, at FocusDistance.

targetOffset.description: An offset from the resolved Subject's pose; ignored when Subject is null.

worldAxes.description: Whether TargetOffset uses world axes rather than the subject's own.

focusDistance.description: The finite target distance along the current subject's forward axis, used only when Subject is null.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpOrbit.description: Orbits the eye about its pivot. Yaw and Pitch are live-bindable like FieldOfView's field of view: a seat rig whose yaw reads a state cell turns the CAMERA when that cell changes — look behind is state.look.behind flipping between 0 and π — while the seat's facing (what steering and movement resolve against) is untouched, because the facing never includes the rig's offsets.

yaw.description: The orbit heading in radians, as a literal, a numeric state binding, or keys on a clock that turn along the shorter arc.

pitch.description: The orbit tilt in radians, as a literal, a numeric state binding, or keys on a clock.

pivotOffset.description: The world-axis offset from the current subject's origin to the pivot.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpOrbit.title: WorldCameraProgramOpOrbit

WorldCameraProgramOpPath.description: Establishes the CURRENT subject at a point sampled from a named curves row by arc-length fraction, and re-seeds the eye there — the same subject-seeding role Anchor plays, so at most one of the two may appear in a program, and when present this must be the first operation. The sampled subject's orientation faces the curve's own tangent direction at that point. A following Offset with WorldAxes: false (the default) rotates its offset into that tangent frame, and a following LookAt with no subject of its own looks ahead along it; a following Orbit pivots at the traveling point but resolves its own yaw/pitch as literal world-frame angles regardless of the tangent — it never reads the subject's orientation. A dollied eye is path + LookAt + FieldOfView; a dollied pivot is path + Orbit with an authored yaw that already accounts for the curve's own heading. Composes with Dynamics's boom follower untouched. Carries no rate field: a constant-rate dolly binds Fraction to a state row carrying the advance trait (base + rate·ticks) rather than duplicating a rate spelling here.

curve.description: The referenced curves row name; must resolve.

fraction.description: The curve's arc-length fraction to sample, in [0, 1] for an open row (values outside clamp) or unrestricted for a closed row (values wrap) — a literal, or a state binding.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpPath.title: WorldCameraProgramOpPath

WorldCameraProgramOpDynamics.description: Sets the second-order response the resolved eye/target boom eases through. Read by the caller after resolving a frame — never affects the resolved pose itself. At most one per program.

row.description: The referenced dynamics row name; must resolve.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpDynamics.title: WorldCameraProgramOpDynamics

WorldCameraProgramOpClampPitch.description: Clamps the effective pitch the NEXT Orbit op resolves with (its authored Pitch plus any live seat delta) to [MinPitch, MaxPitch]. At most one per program; must precede the Orbit op it governs. A joined seat's own views.seatControl band already clamps its LIVE delta before this ever runs — this op exists for a program with no seat behind it (a named camera orbiting a state-bound pitch).

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpClampPitch.title: WorldCameraProgramOpClampPitch

WorldCameraProgramOpFieldOfView.description: Sets the rendered vertical field of view, radians — a literal, or a state.<row>[.<key>] binding so a world rule can pull focus or frame a moment (decisions in the sim, framing in presentation). At most one per program.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpFieldOfView.title: WorldCameraProgramOpFieldOfView

WorldCameraProgramOpBlend.description: Evaluates two other authored programs by name and linearly interpolates their resolved eye, target, and field of view — the whole document's camera-program table (every cameras[].rig plus views.seatRig/views.cameraRig/views.programs) is the namespace A/B resolve against. At most one per program; refused when it would create a reference cycle.

weight.description: The blend weight in [0, 1] — a literal, or a state binding.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpBlend.title: WorldCameraProgramOpBlend

WorldCameraSelectCase.description: One SelectProgram candidate: the program named by Program wins when the op's key rounds to Value.

value.description: The matching key value.

program.description: The candidate program's name — the same blend namespace Blend resolves against (every cameras[].rig, plus views.seatRig/views.cameraRig/views.programs).

WorldCameraSelectCase.title: WorldCameraSelectCase

WorldCameraProgramOpSelectProgram.description: Evaluates exactly one of several other named programs, chosen by a live key — the state-driven counterpart of Blend's two-way continuous mix: a rule-advanced integer row selects a whole framing outright rather than easing toward one, so a document can drive which of N stations a single camera program shows without a per-frame console override. The winning program's eye, target, field of view, and dynamics response pass through unchanged (no lerp). At most one per program; refused when it would create a reference cycle.

key.description: The selecting value — a literal, or (the intended use) a state.<row>[.<key>] binding — rounded to the nearest whole number and matched against Cases.

cases.description: The candidate programs, keyed by Value. At most one case per value.

default.description: The program resolved when no case's value matches Key.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpSelectProgram.title: WorldCameraProgramOpSelectProgram

WorldCameraProgramOpFirstPerson.description: Authors the seat's first-person destination and eased transition. The eye point is in the reference body's local axes at full size. Active may bind state: zero requests third person, one first person; an explicit player choice overrides it. The caller applies live body scale and view-local hiding.

eyePoint.description: The eye in the avatar's local frame.

active.description: The authored view request, a literal or state binding in [0, 1].

transitionSeconds.description: The duration of a complete eased move.

hideRadius.description: The head shell radius within which the own stamp is hidden.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpFirstPerson.title: WorldCameraProgramOpFirstPerson

WorldCameraProgramOpClearance.description: Keeps a seat's chase eye in the room: the seat probes the static geometry and the framed body along the boom each frame and places the eye on a spring arm eased on the program's Dynamics. It shortens the boom along its own heading, rises it toward the seat's up by at most MaxRise when no level boom stands far enough out, and migrates the look target toward CloseTargetOffset as the boom compresses. Two capabilities only the engine has are offered: cutting away the walls between an eye the body put beyond them and the body (Cutaway), and fading the framed body in this seat's own view (FadeStart to FadeEnd). How a world trades them is authored: a program per treatment, chosen by a SelectProgram. A program without this op passes the eye through. At most one per program; read only by a seat framing its own body. Every parameter is a literal or a state.<row>[.<key>] binding. Distances are full-size metres, scaled by the framed body's live scale; angles are radians.

cutaway.description: One keeps the body solid: the eye stays out of the body (its collider and drawn shapes), a boom that no rise clears goes up and over at MaxRise, a target inside geometry skips ObstructedTargetSkin, and the near plane cuts away the geometry between the eye and the body. Zero keeps the room: the eye stays level and short of every wall, at least MinimumBoom out where the room allows.

eyeRadius.description: The radius of the sphere the eye keeps clear of geometry and, under Cutaway, of the body.

surfaceSkin.description: The nearest the eased eye's centre comes to geometry along the boom: a sudden obstruction cuts the eye in to here at once and the ease carries it the rest of the way.

maxRise.description: The most the boom rises above the rig's own elevation, in [0, π/2].

minimumBoom.description: The shortest boom the eye keeps where the room allows it, rising if it must; a nearer wall takes precedence. Zero holds none.

fadeStart.description: The boom length at which the body starts to fade from this seat's view.

fadeEnd.description: The boom length at which the body is hidden; no less than FadeStart never fades it.

closeTargetStartFraction.description: The boom fraction below which the target migrates.

closeTargetFullFraction.description: The boom fraction at which the target reaches CloseTargetOffset.

nearMargin.description: How far short of the body's nearest surface a cutaway's near plane stops.

retractionSkin.description: How far short of a hit the probe reports the room.

obstructedTargetSkin.description: How far out along the boom the sweep starts when the target is inside geometry, past a shell such as a portal frame round the pivot; zero never skips.

closeTargetOffset.description: The target the look migrates to as the boom compresses, in the axes of the preceding LookAt's target offset, which must name a subject; absent keeps the rest target.

opcode.description: Gets this op's authored $type token — the one spelling a refusal, a read-back, and the document all use.

WorldCameraProgramOpClearance.title: WorldCameraProgramOpClearance

WorldCameraProgramOp.description: One instruction in an authored camera program's ordered op list — the presentation-side pose algebra bodyMotionPrograms established for sim-side movement, promoted to cameras: an authored rig is an ordered list of these trivial ops rather than a bespoke closed motion/aim union, so a new camera behavior is authored data, never new engine code. This is the AUTHORING vocabulary only: Puck.World.Client.WorldCameraRigCompiler translates it to Puck.SdfVm.Views.SdfCameraOp and resolves each frame's bindings and subject poses, and Puck.SdfVm.Views.SdfCameraProgramEvaluator — which parses no document — walks the result. Floats throughout; presentation carries no fixed-point burden.
WorldCameraProgramOp.title: WorldCameraProgramOp

WorldAnchorNonNullable.description: WHERE a placeable thing rides — the one shared pose-target vocabulary a placeable WorldCamera and a placeable WorldSpeaker both consume through the SAME resolver, distinct from HOW the thing looks at or emits from that pose (a WorldCameraProgram, a feed). The $type string is the JSON discriminator; a new anchor kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.
WorldAnchorNonNullable.title: WorldAnchor

OverlayFact.description: A presentation fact an overlay element's OverlayPredicate reads. Every fact is per local seat and never enters the simulation; a world-scope element (a hud.panels row) reads a fact as true when it holds for any joined local seat.
OverlayFact.title: OverlayFact

x-enumDescriptions.SeatInput: The seat sent any input (a routed signal) this tick.
x-enumDescriptions.PointerMotion: The seat's pointer moved this tick.
x-enumDescriptions.WheelOpen: The seat's binding wheel is open.
x-enumDescriptions.SeatCameraApplication: The seat's camera control application is active (see Target).
x-enumDescriptions.ScreenFramed: The seat is captured on a screen it engaged, and its view shows that screen's picture alone (not the held view of a carried screen, nor the room after player.frame).

OverlayPredicateRecently.description: The fact held within the last WindowSeconds.

fact.description: The fact whose recency is tested.

windowSeconds.description: How long after the fact last held the predicate still holds in full.

comparandState.description: Another declared state-section row name, or a reserved channel, read live and compared instead of Value. x-enumDescriptions.Int: A whole 64-bit signed integer cell (a score, a round counter, an inventory count, or — declaring min zero — a tick-count timer).
x-enumDescriptions.Fixed: A fixed-point cell holding raw FixedQ4816 bits — the deterministic replacement for a float in simulation state. Human-authored surfaces (document JSON, console verb arguments, validator refusal text, read-back echoes) use the decimal representation via FixedQ4816.TryParse/ToString; only the addon ABI channel wire and the per-cell mutation payload carry the raw bit pattern.
x-enumDescriptions.Bool: A boolean cell (a win flag, a toggle). Carries no range — a gauge cannot bind to it.
x-enumDescriptions.Text: A short-text cell (a status label, a player name slot), bounded to MaxTextValueLength UTF-16 code units. Carries no range — a gauge cannot bind to it. The only kind whose value is carried in Text rather than Value.
x-enumDescriptions.Vector: A vector cell holding an admitted, normalized signed 8-bit embedding vector, carried in Vector rather than Value or Text.
