anyOf.description: A state.<row>[.<key>] reference the containing document resolves from a cell.

WorldRowSelectorCase.description: One case of a WorldRowSelector: the row a body's register value selects.

value.description: The register value, a whole number; a counter holding a fraction matches no case.

row.description: The kit or look row name the value selects.

WorldRowSelectorCase.title: WorldRowSelectorCase

WorldRowSelector.description: A per-body row selector inside a WorldRowAssignment: each body's own value of a state.body counter picks the row the case for that value names. A body whose register holds a value no case names keeps the row the assignment's sequence gives it. The register is body state, so the choice is the body's and goes where the body goes: a kit action or a rule's setBodyState moves the row, a replay moves it at the same tick, a checkpoint restores it with the register, and a crossing to another world carries the register with the body (a destination declaring the same register under the same kind selects by the carried value). The look assignment's selector changes only what a body wears; the kit assignment's selector changes how it moves and what it collides as, so a collider change is its own authored mapping and a look never changes a kit.

bodyState.description: The state.body counter whose value selects.

cases.description: The value-to-row mapping, each value at most once.

WorldRowSelector.title: WorldRowSelector

WorldRowAssignment.description: The row-to-entity assignment declaration — nothing about Sequence/Rows is kit-specific, so the same primitive distributes the kit table (a way of moving) and the look table (a way of looking) across the population. Resolved once at construction into each entry's fixed row index (precompute; zero steady-state cost). The kit assignment affects the simulation (it selects the compiled tuning/action bindings); the look assignment is presentation-only (it selects the appearance row). A Select overrides the sequence for each body whose own state.body register maps to a row, and follows that register as the simulation writes it.

sequence.description: The sequence that selects a row.

select.description: The per-body selector, or null for the sequence alone.

rows.description: Gets the authored row-name view. The absence-coalesce lives in the accessor for the same reason Elements's does.

WorldRowAssignment.title: WorldRowAssignment

WorldBindingBarAnchor.description: Where a bar hangs: a viewport edge and how far in from it. Every bank anchored to the same edge and inset shares one frame — their plates are laid out together on one pitch grid and the nearest plate of the whole group sits at the inset — so a nested crossbar is five banks on one anchor, and a strip with side columns is three groups on three.

inset.description: The gap between that edge and the nearest plate edge of everything anchored here, in button pitches — the same ruler every plate position uses. Along the other axis the group is centered.

WorldBindingBarAnchor.title: WorldBindingBarAnchor

WorldPlacementTranslation.description: An opaque stored placement translation: a dealt child's displacement from its slot, otherwise an authored local offset. Geometry reads a resolved frame through WorldPlacementFrameCompilation, never this value as a position. Fixed-point writes and their JSON round trips retain every Q48.16 bit.
WorldPlacementTranslation.title: WorldPlacementTranslation

anyOf.description: A state.<row>[.<key>] reference the containing document resolves from a cell.

WorldPlacementMirror.description: A reflection plane in a placement's local frame.

offset.description: The signed plane offset along the normalized Normal.

WorldPlacementMirror.title: WorldPlacementMirror

WorldEmission.description: An emission facet — a synth voice a world row itself makes (phenomena sound like themselves; a creek is not a speaker). Nullable on WorldPlacement — a facet edit is the row's existing whole-row upsert. Under a repeat facet the emission binds to the placement root only (an 8×8 lattice must not become 64 voices; a per-copy flag is a future facet field, not a schema fork).

level.description: The emitter level (1 = unity), bounded by MaxLevel.

radius.description: The audible support radius in world units, or null for the audio defaults' DefaultSpeakerRadius.

WorldEmission.title: WorldEmission

WorldPlacementInhabit.description: A placement's inhabit facet — the row's binding to live population bodies. An inhabited placement is a normal entry in the entity table: it holds a Puck.World.Server.WorldBody, integrates under the named kit, and is addressable as Entity like any avatar. Its stamp rides the body's pose instead of the row's static transform; the row's position/yaw become its spawn pose. Absent (null) = decoration, the unchanged furniture behaviour.

kit.description: The Name the bodies move under. Null resolves the creation's own Locomotion token AS a kit name — a creation declaring "swim" inhabits the world's kit row named "swim". Neither resolving is a loud rejection naming every kit the world declares.

look.description: The Name the bodies wear, or null to wear an implicit creation look on this placement's own PrototypeId.

source.description: The live, idle, or named producer source the bodies wake on.

count.description: How many bodies: an authored literal, or a live cell reference naming an Int state.world row whose value the population admits and retires bodies to track (WorldPopulation.ReconcileInhabitCounts) — the spawner primitive a crawl's mob generator rides. Either way, bounded by the world's authored peer capacity; a cell reference is additionally bounded by Distribution's own sample count, the tighter of the two winning. Absent is an authored literal of 1 — see ResolvedCount.
count.title: WorldPlacementInhabitCount

distribution.description: The region and deterministic fill sequence that place the bodies relative to the placement root.

role.description: The name of the companion role (WorldRole) the body holds: it goes where the player it follows goes, under the role declaration of each world it enters. Absent: the body holds no role.

follows.description: The 0-based local seat whose player the role's body follows. Required with Role and refused without it.

WorldPlacementInhabit.title: WorldPlacementInhabit

WorldPortalArrival.description: Where a traveler lands at a WorldPlacementPortal's destination — the positional-continuity decision a portal facet authors on top of which destination it names.
WorldPortalArrival.title: WorldPortalArrival

WorldPlacementPortal.description: A WorldPlacementFace's portal facet — the authored decision that a face is a door: which WorldDestination row it leads to, and under what travel scope. Absent (the default) means the face is not a door — nothing here fires anything by itself; turning the decision into a diegetic step-into trigger is WorldInstanceHost's job (its per-tick portal scan, ScanInstancePortals, then ResolveAndEnqueueCoalescedTransfers), never this facet's. Durability, scope, and process-local instance selection live on the named WorldDestination row this facet points at, not here — a facet composes one destination selection with a travel scope, never re-authors how that destination is minted. Extensible deliberately (an optional-member record, the same widen-without-moving-existing-members shape WorldLatticeMedium's own remarks describe): a future fact-gate field (an authored predicate a traveler must satisfy to pass) adds cleanly as a new trailing member.

destination.description: The Name of the destinations row naming the selected destination. Must resolve to an existing row — an undeclared name refuses by name (see WorldDefinitionValidator). No boot-time file-existence check on the destination's own referenced document — resolving the document is a future consumer's job; resolving the name, against this document's own destinations section, is this facet's own.

travel.description: Who travels through (see WorldPortalTravel). Absent resolves against the world's own portals.portalDefaults.travel (see WorldPortalsSection), or Body when the world declares no portals section at all — see WorldDefinitionValidator's resolution order, echoed by world.portals. Omitted from the wire when null.

arrival.description: Where a traveler lands at the destination (see WorldPortalArrival). Default Spawn — unauthored worlds and every facet authored before this member existed are unchanged. Optional and trailing (the same widen-without-moving-existing-members shape Travel itself already follows).

counterpart.description: The destination document's border face this facet's frame maps onto under Mapped — "<placementId>/<face>", the placement id and declared face name whose own placement transform (position + yaw) is the arrival anchor. Required exactly when Arrival is Mapped (refused by name otherwise, in either direction — see WorldDefinitionValidator). No boot-time cross-document existence check: the named document is not resolved at boot (same reason Destination is not), so an absent placement/face refuses at transfer time instead, against the destination's own delivered definition (see WorldPortalCounterpart). Omitted from the wire when null.

capacity.description: The maximum number of live bodies and outstanding reservations admitted through this border at once, or null to use the destination population's remaining capacity. A full border refuses the current attempt immediately; it never queues.

WorldPlacementPortal.title: WorldPlacementPortal

WorldPlacementFace.description: A per-instance override of one declared creation face's feed — the face twin of the emission facet's per-instance override channel.

source.description: The screen source the face shows, in the existing WorldScreenSource vocabulary.

portal.description: The face's portal facet (see WorldPlacementPortal) — absent (the default) means this face is not a door. Optional and trailing deliberately: a face authored before this facet existed round-trips unchanged, and it composes freely with Source — the door and the screen it shows are independent facts about the same face.

filter.description: How the face's screen samples its source's image, as a screen row's Filter does: Nearest, the default, keeps each source pixel crisp; Linear blends between source pixels. Omitted from the wire when Nearest.
filter.title: GpuSamplerFilter

material.description: The id of the screen material the face's screen draws its picture through, as a screen row's Material does, or null for none. Refused on a window. Omitted from the wire when null.

WorldPlacementFace.title: WorldPlacementFace

WorldPlacementRegion.description: A placement's region facet — a named volume row, not a trigger system: any placement may carry one, turning its stamp into a sensing volume the world-events feed watches for body enter/exit edges (see Server.WorldEventFeed and the observe region:<name> grant subject). The region's name is the carrying placement's Id — one identity, never a second string kept in sync by hand. The volume is a sphere of Radius or an oriented box of HalfExtents (exactly one is authored), so a room or a corridor is one region. Its center is Center in the placement's resolved frame and a box turns with the placement's resolved yaw plus its own YawDegrees; the placement's Scale never sizes it, since a region's size is its own authored extent, never derived from the creation's visual bounds. Presentation-only in itself (drawing no geometry); sensing reads the fixed-point shape ShapeAt compiles from the placement's resolved frame — unless the row also carries Attach, in which case the frame is the resolved live body pose instead (Server.WorldEventFeed.CollectRegions, the same resolve world.attachments answers): the sensing volume follows the carrier, and an inactive carrier senses nobody rather than sensing at a stale point. A body is inside when its foot point lies within the closed volume, the test Contains owns.

radius.description: The sensing sphere's radius in world units, or zero for a box. A sphere's radius must be finite and positive (validated).

halfExtents.description: The sensing box's half-extents in world units along its own axes, or absent for a sphere. Each must be finite and positive (validated).

center.description: The volume's center in the placement's frame, world units (yawed with it, never scaled).

yawDegrees.description: A box's yaw about +Y in degrees, added to the placement's resolved yaw. Ignored by a sphere.

capacity.description: How many occupants the work sheet prices a rule's forEach: region(...) sweep at: the bodies the author expects the place to hold at once. Absent for the most bodies that fit the volume (RegionSweepCapacity). It prices and nothing else: the region senses and counts every body inside it, and a sweep binds every one.

WorldPlacementRegion.title: WorldPlacementRegion

WorldPlacementAttach.description: A placement's attach facet — binds the row's stamp to a live population body's transform, so the resolved world pose follows that body every tick (an avatar's hat, held item, nameplate, or aura) instead of sitting at the row's own authored Position/YawDegrees. The offset rides the body's own local frame — rotated by the body's orientation before adding, the Puck.SdfVm.Views.OrientedFollowRig/FirstPersonRig convention for a moving anchor, never the world-axis FollowRig shape a fixed subject would use. The resolved pose is never written back into the document, and it is derived twice, at two clocks, from the one authored facet: the authoritative answer is fixed point — the body's fixed-point pose composed with this facet's authored (float, quantized at resolution like every other placement field) offset, by Puck.World.Server.WorldPlacementAttachment.TryResolve, on demand by world.attachments and once per tick by attached local gravity areas;the rendered pose is presentation float — the same composition over the client's interpolated body pose, packed every frame by Client.WorldCreationInstances, which is what makes an attached row visibly ride its body as smoothly as the body itself. An attached row draws through that reserved stamp pool and not as a static stamp (Client.WorldPlacementStamper.IsStaticStamp), and it charges the live creation instance storage like an animated row does. Region, solid (under the analytic contact provider), and emission were once refused on the same row as this one because each read the row's own static transform — all three now read the same resolved dynamic pose instead (Server.WorldEventFeed.CollectRegions, Server.WorldColliderSet.RefreshAttached, Server.WorldGravityField.RefreshAttachedAreas, Client.WorldAnchorPoses), so a region's aura, an analytic collider's hitbox, and an emission's voice all track the carrier: an equipped item's sensing sphere, hitbox, or source point rides the body it is attached to. What stays refused: distribution/mirror (static-stamp-only, the same rule an animated or inhabited row already enforces), inhabit (a row cannot both spawn its own driven bodies and ride another's), and solid specifically under the field contact provider (it compiles every solid row's geometry once into one SDF program and never rebuilds it per tick) — refused by name rather than defining a blend (see WorldDefinitionValidator).

bodyIndex.description: The 0-based population entity index the placement rides — the same indexing Entity and the console's body:<n> grant subject use, not the 1-based player.* seat number (body:1 is "player 2"). Validated within 0..the world's authored population capacity; the target need not be active at author time (see remarks — an inactive body at runtime makes the row contribute nothing, it does not refuse).

localOffset.description: The stamp's position offset in the body's own local frame, world units.

localYawDegrees.description: The stamp's yaw offset from the body's own heading, degrees. Zero rides the body's exact facing.

WorldPlacementAttach.title: WorldPlacementAttach

WorldContributionTenure.description: How long a filled WorldPlacementContribution slot keeps the piece a federation partner put in it.
WorldContributionTenure.title: WorldContributionTenure

x-enumDescriptions.Presence: The piece stands while Link is reachable. The per-tick sweep stamps RetractDeadlineTick at GraceSeconds out when the link first reads unreachable, clears the stamp when it comes back, and retracts once the deadline passes.
x-enumDescriptions.Endowed: The piece persists; the sweep never touches the row. Link and a positive GraceSeconds are refused beside this tenure — the disjoint-field-set rule StateGenerator's source arms follow.

WorldPlacementContribution.description: A placement's contribution facet: the row is a slot whose frame (id, pose, scale, and these lifecycle terms) is host-authored and whose creation a federation partner supplies through ordinary mutations. Null is an ordinary placement.

slotCreationId.description: The host-owned Id the slot shows while unfilled and returns to on retraction. Must resolve to a declared creation row.

link.description: The authored adjacencies row name the presence check watches — the same key the $link:<adjacencyName> reserved rule channel reads. Required for Presence, refused beside Endowed.
link.title: SafeName

graceSeconds.description: Seconds the watched link may stay unreachable before the piece retracts, compiled to simulation ticks through CompiledGrace at each sweep observation and stamped once into RetractDeadlineTick. Zero disables the grace (retract on the first observed outage); a rate-0 world compiles to Never, so nothing retracts. Refused beside Endowed unless zero.

contributor.description: Server-stamped. The acting principal that filled the slot; null while unfilled. Never accepted from a submitted payload or an authored document.
contributor.title: Principal

retractDeadlineTick.description: Server-stamped. The simulation tick at or after which the presence sweep retracts this slot; null while the link is reachable.

WorldPlacementContribution.title: WorldPlacementContribution

WorldPlacementResponseConditionFieldCond.description: The original lattice-field condition, unchanged from before this union existed: the named field read at the placement's own coupled cell, compared against a literal or another row's slot cell.

field.description: The field read at the cell.

value.description: The scalar compared against (literal or state-row reference) — the same WorldLatticeScalar grammar a fields.reactions Transform/Expose condition already uses.
value.title: WorldLatticeScalar

WorldPlacementResponseConditionFieldCond.title: WorldPlacementResponseConditionFieldCondition

WorldPlacementResponseConditionStateCond.description: A state-cell condition: compares State's cell (its slot cell when Key is absent, else the cell at Key) against Value, or — when ComparandState is authored instead — against another declared row's cell, read live at the same evaluation. Exactly one of Value and ComparandState may be present, the same one-comparand rule CompareState already enforces for a rule's own gate — this facet reuses that field convention rather than inventing a second reading of "compare a state cell." Independent of the placement's position, and of whether the document declares a fields section at all.

state.description: The state row compared — any declared state.world row of a numeric kind (never Text).

value.description: The literal comparand, or null when ComparandState spells the comparand instead.

key.description: The cell inside State, or null for its slot cell. Refused when State is keyed and this is absent, or unkeyed and this is present.

comparandState.description: Another declared state.world row, read live and compared instead of Value. Must share State's cell kind (refused by name otherwise).

comparandKey.description: The cell inside ComparandState, on the same terms as Key. Refused when ComparandState is absent.

WorldPlacementResponseConditionStateCond.title: WorldPlacementResponseConditionStateCondition

WorldPlacementResponseCondition.description: The closed union a response entry's When speaks. Both arms evaluate against the SAME per-tick document the rule frame folds a rule's writes into before this sweep runs (Server.WorldTick.SweepPlacementResponses runs after EvaluateWorldRules' own end-of-tick fold), so a cell a rule wrote this tick already reads through StateCondition on the same tick's sweep.
WorldPlacementResponseCondition.title: WorldPlacementResponseCondition

WorldPlacementResponse.description: One entry of a placement's response trait: while When holds, the row draws and collides as PrototypeId instead of its authored PrototypeId — the bridge that lets a placement react to live simulation state (a burning tree shows a charred stump; a filled account swaps a granary's face). Absent Respond, the placement always shows its authored prototype.

when.description: The condition tested every sweep — a lattice-field read or a state-cell read.

prototypeId.description: The creation the placement shows/collides as while When holds and no earlier entry does. Must resolve to a declared, non-animated creation row.

WorldPlacementResponse.title: WorldPlacementResponse

WorldPlacementGrip.description: A placement's grip facet — overrides the world's DefaultHold hold policy for every collider this row compiles, composing as the tighter authoring layer: present, it decides; absent, the row's colliders fall back to the world default. Requires Solid (nothing else compiles a collider a grip trait could apply to). Every collider a distribution/mirror expands from one row shares the row's single grip decision — a lattice of holdable handholds is authored as one placement, not one per copy.

holdable.description: Whether a body's surface hold may take this row's compiled surface(s), overriding the world default.

WorldPlacementGrip.title: WorldPlacementGrip

WorldBoardEnforcement.description: How a tabletop board binding treats an illegal move — the author's choice per table, engine-side and game-agnostic: the judge that computes Verdict is authored per world, and this field only decides what the engine itself does once that verdict refuses.
WorldBoardEnforcement.title: WorldBoardEnforcement

x-enumDescriptions.Record: An illegal move is recorded; the body that moved stays where it settled.
x-enumDescriptions.Return: An illegal move is recorded and the body that moved is posed back onto the move's origin cell.

WorldTabletopSeat.description: One chair at a tabletop: the edge of the board a seat sits at, given as the way it faces.

yawDegrees.description: The chair's facing, in the convention of a spawn point's and a body's yaw: 0 faces -Z (the chair stands at the board's +Z edge), 90 faces -X, 180 faces +Z and 270 faces +X. A board's topology is world-axis-aligned, so a chair faces across one of its four edges: a whole number of quarter turns.

WorldTabletopSeat.title: WorldTabletopSeat

WorldTabletopEngage.description: A tabletop's engagement: a seat standing within Radius of the board's centre presses Channel (its context button) and sits down at the table, in the authored chair nearest it (Seats). The seat is captured (its avatar stands still) on a control placement:<id> application, its camera eases to a view of the whole board from that chair's side, and the same button leaves. While engaged, the world's rules read the seat's channels as play (channel(...)), and the board reads where the seat points (board(pointer, <row>, <seat>)), whether the seat sits at it (board(engaged, …)) and which chair's side it plays from (board(side, …)), so the game itself stays document rules.

channel.description: The declared channel whose press engages and leaves the table.

radius.description: How near the board's centre, on the ground plane in world units, a seat must stand to engage. Positive.

pitch.description: The board view's elevation above the horizontal, in degrees: 90 looks straight down, smaller leans toward the seat's side. In (0, 90].

margin.description: World units of room the board view leaves around the board's footprint. Non-negative.

surface.description: The height above the topology's origin, in world units, of the plane a pointer ray meets when it picks a cell: the playing surface, so a cell under the pointer is the cell the eye sees. Non-negative.

seats.description: The chairs a seat sits in, each at one edge of the board facing across it; a seat sits in the one nearest where it stands (SeatSide). Absent, the table has a chair at each of its four edges. A board laid out for one player's view (a solitaire tableau, a lectern behind the board) names the chair it is laid out for, so its layout and controls read the right way round wherever the player walks up.

WorldTabletopEngage.title: WorldTabletopEngage

WorldPlacementBoard.description: A placement's board facet — the tabletop primitive. Anchors a state.lattices Grid topology (which already carries its own world-space origin/cellSize frame) to this placement, so a chess set, a checkers board, or a card table is one placement/body carrying one topology — carriable as a unit once an attachment primitive picks it up. A topology is carried by at most one placement (validated). Occupancy is the only row the engine reads; Turn/Verdict/ Move/Plan are author-named convenience bindings world.tabletop echoes together — ordinary declared rows, never engine-interpreted, so this facet stays a reusable primitive rather than a chess-specific feature.

topology.description: The state.lattices Grid topology this placement anchors.

occupancy.description: The board-typed row over Topology holding current occupant codes.

turn.description: An optional phase row read back beside the frame.

verdict.description: An optional row read back beside the frame (a ruling on the last recorded change). Required when Enforcement is Return (validated).

move.description: An optional keyed row (conventionally cells "from"/"to") read back beside the frame. Required when Enforcement is Return (validated).

plan.description: An optional board-typed row over Topology a future addon paints candidate cells into for highlight rendering — the seam, not the addon.

enforcement.description: What the engine itself does once Verdict refuses a move.

accept.description: The Verdict value the judge writes to accept a move — any other value is a refusal.

engage.description: How a seat sits down at the table, or null for a table no seat engages: the context button that engages and leaves it, how near a seat must stand, the board view its camera eases to, and the surface the seat's pointer meets.

WorldPlacementBoard.title: WorldPlacementBoard

WorldPlacementDealVariants.description: A deal facet's variant selection: a keyed row read at the dealt cell's key, and the map from that cell's text to the prototype the child is dealt with.

row.description: The keyed state.world row read at the dealt cell's key. May be the dealt row itself.

map.description: Cell text (an integer cell's value spelled as text) to the Id the child shows. Every value must resolve to a declared, non-animated creation.

WorldPlacementDealVariants.title: WorldPlacementDealVariants

WorldPlacementDealPreserve.description: Instance-owned properties which reconciliation seeds at creation and subsequently preserves. Membership and the allocated deal slot remain owned by the source row.

transform.description: Preserve an existing child's displacement from its slot, yaw, and scale.

prototype.description: Preserve its prototype, including changes made by responses.

facets.description: Preserve its other facets, including responses and face sources.

WorldPlacementDealPreserve.title: WorldPlacementDealPreserve

WorldPlacementReflow.description: Author-selected work and payment policy for rearranging a deal template's children.

candidateBudget.description: Maximum preparation, candidate, and overlap work units in one preview; preparation includes a conservative charge for sorting offsets. Exhaustion refuses without edits.

costPerMove.description: Nonnegative Int units charged for each changed placement, including a spatial seed edit.

costRow.description: An Int state row paying the price. Required for a nonzero price.

costKey.description: The payer cell; absent selects an unkeyed row's slot.

WorldPlacementReflow.title: WorldPlacementReflow

WorldPlacementDeal.description: A placement's deal facet: the row is a template whose instances are dealt from a keyed state row, one child placement per cell, laid out over the template's own Distribution region in cell order. The template itself renders nothing and collides with nothing; its prototype, its Scale and its Solid/Grip/Region/ Emission facets are what every child is stamped with. The region's offsets are metres in the template's frame, never scaled by it. A child is an ordinary placement row named <template>/<cellKey> (ChildId) with Parent naming the template and DealSlot its slot. Its Position is its displacement from that slot, so its local frame is the slot's fixed-point offset (SlotOffset) plus that displacement, composed by WorldPlacementFrameCompilation, and moving a child to another slot moves it with its displacement. It is installed by the per-tick sweep (Server.WorldTick.SweepPlacementDeals) through the shared placement projection install, which refreshes colliders and delivery. The source cells journal, undo and replay; their derived children are reprojected without adding declaration edits to the journal.

row.description: The keyed state.world row whose cells are dealt, of any cell kind. One child per cell, keyed by the cell's key.

variants.description: The optional variant selection: a second keyed row read at the same key, whose cell text (an integer cell spelled as text) selects a prototype from Map; a cell with no entry, or no cell at all, deals the template's own prototype.

preserve.description: Which properties of existing instances are owned by gameplay. Absent synchronizes copied properties with the template. New instances receive the template's supported copied facets.

reflow.description: Optional bounded rearrangement policy. Requires instance-owned transforms and a footprint.

WorldPlacementDeal.title: WorldPlacementDeal

WorldPlacementSpatialRole.description: The contract a named placement-local spatial volume contributes to queries.
WorldPlacementSpatialRole.title: WorldPlacementSpatialRole

x-enumDescriptions.Occupation: Blocks occupation by another occupation volume.
x-enumDescriptions.Clearance: Reserves passage around an occupation volume.
x-enumDescriptions.Influence: Reports presence to a named, author-defined channel without blocking.

WorldSpatialShapeKind.description: The shared shape vocabulary used by occupation, clearance, and influence volumes.
WorldSpatialShapeKind.title: WorldSpatialShapeKind

WorldSpatialShape.description: A placement-local bounded shape. Box yaw is measured about +Y; Y extents are part of the contract.

halfExtents.description: Positive local half extents for a box; zero for a sphere.

radius.description: Positive radius for a sphere; zero for a box.

yawDegrees.description: The local box yaw, in degrees. Sphere yaw is ignored.

WorldSpatialShape.title: WorldSpatialShape

WorldPlacementSpatialVolume.description: A named spatial volume authored on one placement. The name is placement-local metadata; an influence channel is opaque to the engine and is never interpreted as water, power, or another game noun.

name.description: The stable name returned by spatial queries.

role.description: Whether the volume occupies, reserves clearance, or reports influence.

channel.description: An author-defined influence label. Required only for influence volumes.

pinned.description: Whether layout policy must preserve this volume's placement transform.

WorldPlacementSpatialVolume.title: WorldPlacementSpatialVolume

WorldPlacementSurface.description: One-time directed projection of static occurrence roots onto named static contact geometry. The occurrence keeps its authored rotation and scale; its resolved origin is shared by presentation and collision.

targets.description: Placement IDs whose static contact fields may receive a root. Surface and parent dependencies must be acyclic.

fromOffset.description: World-space offset from each candidate root to the ray origin.

direction.description: World-space ray direction, normalized in fixed point.

reach.description: Maximum ray length in world units.

offset.description: Signed world-space displacement along the hit normal (negative embeds a root).

minFacing.description: Minimum cosine of hit normal with the opposite cast direction, in [0,1].

requireHit.description: Refuse derivation instead of dropping an occurrence when no proven eligible surface is found.

WorldPlacementSurface.title: WorldPlacementSurface

WorldSpeakerSourceNone.description: No signal is bound — honest silence (the emitter holds its place; audio.emitters reads the state).
WorldSpeakerSourceNone.title: WorldSpeakerSourceNone

WorldSpeakerSourceMachine.description: A named machine audio output. The source is a consumer reference only: the named machine host owns preparation, advancement, and the single drain shared by every speaker feed that names this output.

output.description: The provider audio output name exposed by that instance.

WorldSpeakerSourceMachine.title: WorldSpeakerSourceMachine

WorldSpeakerSourceTune.description: A tune asset (WorldTune) played through a headless machine host — acquired while any speaker references it, released when orphaned (a runtime derivation, never a data concept).
WorldSpeakerSourceTune.title: WorldSpeakerSourceTune

WorldSpeakerSourceSynth.description: The world voice synth playing a patch asset (WorldPatch). Patches are mono by construction: the feed's channel selectors degenerate to mix — documented, never rejected.
WorldSpeakerSourceSynth.title: WorldSpeakerSourceSynth

WorldSpeakerSource.description: The signal a WorldSpeaker's feed taps — a shared source identity, never an inline payload: the runtime drains each distinct source once per mix block and every feed tapping it shares that one pull, so "stereo = two rows sharing a source" costs one drain. The $type string is the JSON discriminator, matching WorldScreenSource's convention; a new source kind is a new derived record plus its JsonDerivedTypeAttribute line.
WorldSpeakerSource.title: WorldSpeakerSource

WorldSpeakerFeed.description: A speaker's feed — what it plays: a shared source identity, a stereo channel selector, and a gain. Stereo separation is two independent speaker rows sharing one source with left/right selectors and different geometry — no group/attachment construct. Mono sources (the synth) degenerate every selector to ChannelMix.

source.description: The shared source identity this feed taps.

channel.description: The stereo channel selector — ChannelMix, ChannelLeft, or ChannelRight.

gain.description: The feed gain (1 = unity), as a literal, state binding or keys on a clock, bounded by MaxLevel. Publication resolves the live value without restarting the emitter.

WorldSpeakerFeed.title: WorldSpeakerFeed

WorldSpeakerAttenuation.description: A point speaker's distance-attenuation policy, or null on the row to coalesce to the WorldAudioDefaults section (DefaultSpeakerRadius/DefaultCurve).

radius.description: The finite audible support radius in world units — at or beyond it the emitter is culled (finite support is the cull).

curve.description: The falloff curve token (CurveSmoothstep or CurveLinear), or null for the audio-defaults curve.

WorldSpeakerAttenuation.title: WorldSpeakerAttenuation

WorldCameraProgram.description: An authored camera program — the ordered op list a rig resolves through every frame.

name.description: The stable name a Blend op selects this program by.

operations.description: The selected ops, in authored evaluation order.

bloom.description: The camera's optical scatter override; absent inherits the world.

WorldCameraProgram.title: WorldCameraProgram

WorldViewTransition.description: The transition envelope of a composition change: how long the ease takes and how far the render scale dips while it runs. A layout carries one as Transition and the built-in seat ladder as BuiltinTransition; the defaults are neutral, a cut with no dip.

seconds.description: How long the ease takes, in seconds; 0 is a cut. Default 0.

renderScale.description: The render scale (0, 1] applied to every slot mid-transition; 1 is no dip. Default 1.

WorldViewTransition.title: WorldViewTransition

WorldHudRect.description: A normalized rect (origin top-left, Y down) — a WorldHudPanel's rect is in screen space [0, 1] × [0, 1]; a WorldHudElement's rect is in its owning panel's local [0, 1] × [0, 1] space.

width.description: The rect's width, normalized — must be positive.

height.description: The rect's height, normalized — must be positive.

WorldHudRect.title: WorldHudRect

WorldHudLayer.description: Where a WorldHudPanel draws relative to the five first-party overlay writers (the console panel, binding bars, gizmos, editor HUD, and toast) — the banded pipeline's ordering key.
WorldHudLayer.title: WorldHudLayer

x-enumDescriptions.Under: Draws before the first-party writers (document order among Under panels).
x-enumDescriptions.Over: Draws after the first-party writers, or after the replace panels when any are live (document order among Over panels) — always the topmost band.
x-enumDescriptions.Replace: Takes the base slot the five first-party writers would otherwise occupy: while at least one live panel declares Replace, every replace panel renders itself there (document order) and the five first-party writers do not run. Removing the last replace panel restores them.

WorldHudPanelStyle.description: A WorldHudPanel's chrome recipe — the authored twin of Puck.Overlays.OverlayPanelStyle (Puck.World.Schema must not reference Puck.Overlays; the renderer maps this token to the concrete style).
WorldHudPanelStyle.title: WorldHudPanelStyle

x-enumDescriptions.Strip: The strip scrim (a thinner readout band).
x-enumDescriptions.Chip: The chip scrim (a small badge-sized panel).

WorldHudElementKind.description: A WorldHudElement's rendered kind — the schema→render expansion cost differs per kind (see WorldHudCapacity).
WorldHudElementKind.title: WorldHudElementKind

x-enumDescriptions.Rect: A filled rect — 1 render element, no binding.
x-enumDescriptions.Text: A fixed-cell text run — the authored Text string, or (when Binding names one) the live-resolved binding's text form.
x-enumDescriptions.Gauge: A fill-bar readout of a bound binding's normalized 0..1 value (0 when unbound).
x-enumDescriptions.Plot: A scrolling recent series in an authored range, with an optional reference line.
x-enumDescriptions.Frame: A sampled frame: the element rect shows the frame a WorldFrameSource produces (camera/view/probe/capture) — the picture-in-picture element kind (e.g. a face-cam overlay).

WorldHudStyleToken.description: A WorldHudElement's color role — a curated authored subset of Puck.Overlays.OverlayColorRole (Puck.World.Schema must not reference Puck.Overlays; the renderer maps this token to the concrete role).
WorldHudStyleToken.title: WorldHudStyleToken

WorldFrameSource.description: The WorldScreenSource arms that produce a sampled frame — Producer, View and Probe — carrying its own JsonPolymorphicAttribute over the same three discriminators (producer/view/probe) their parent union uses, so a member declared as this narrower type round-trips the identical JSON a full WorldScreenSource screen row does. A WorldProbe socket is the driving consumer: it plugs one of these into each named input rather than the wider union, which would legally admit a decal, machine, text or none source no probe kernel can sample.
WorldFrameSource.title: WorldFrameSource

WorldFrameSourceNonNullable.description: The WorldScreenSource arms that produce a sampled frame — Producer, View and Probe — carrying its own JsonPolymorphicAttribute over the same three discriminators (producer/view/probe) their parent union uses, so a member declared as this narrower type round-trips the identical JSON a full WorldScreenSource screen row does. A WorldProbe socket is the driving consumer: it plugs one of these into each named input rather than the wider union, which would legally admit a decal, machine, text or none source no probe kernel can sample.
WorldFrameSourceNonNullable.title: WorldFrameSource

WorldHudFrameCandidate.description: One ranked source candidate of a Frame element: the frame shown while When holds. Candidates are walked in authored order every frame and the first holding one wins; a null predicate always holds, so the last row is the default.

source.description: The sampled frame while this candidate wins.

when.description: The condition, evaluated for the panel's seat.

WorldHudFrameCandidate.title: WorldHudFrameCandidate

WorldVoiceProfile.description: A character voice over an existing synth patch or an authored syllable sample set. HUD Text elements speak their resolved text on visible arrival or change. Pitch and formant scales distinguish speakers; cadence and pace determine the integer audio-frame schedule. Identity babble also uses the patch and cadence selectors; absent selectors mean no identity babble.

patchId.description: The referenced Name (must resolve when declared).

cadenceTicks.description: The base spacing in 240 Hz audio ticks: 1..240 for HUD text, any positive value for count-based identity babble.

pitchThousandths.description: Pitch relative to the patch, 250..4000; 1000 leaves it unchanged.

paceThousandths.description: Speech speed, 250..4000; 2000 halves each character's interval.

sampleSet.description: Optional syllable-bank document path, replacing synthesis for HUD text.

hash.description: Optional SHA-256 content pin of the canonical SampleSet manifest so a delivered world with no document directory resolves its voice samples through Resolver.

WorldVoiceProfile.title: WorldVoiceProfile

WorldHudElement.description: One HUD element row inside a WorldHudPanel — a stable id (unique within the owning panel), its kind, its local rect, its color role, an authored literal string (meaningful for Text), and an optional binding into the closed HudBindingVocabulary (meaningful for Text and Gauge — a bound text element's live value replaces the authored literal; a bound gauge element's live value drives its fill; an unbound gauge draws empty).

id.description: The element's stable id (unique within the owning panel — the world.row.set hud.panels/ .remove mutation address).

rect.description: The element's rect, normalized to the owning panel's local space.

text.description: The authored literal string a Text element draws when neither Binding nor Template is set; ignored for Rect and Gauge. Omitted from the wire when null.

binding.description: A closed HudBindingVocabulary token, or null for an unbound element. Refused alongside Template — exactly one live-value source, never both. Omitted from the wire when null.

template.description: A Text element's template string — authored literal text interleaved with {token} placeholders, each a closed HudBindingVocabulary token resolved through the same operand path Binding uses (see HudTemplate for the brace/escape grammar). A richer binding source than Binding — many live facts composed into one string instead of one — never both on the same element. Ignored for Rect and Gauge (a gauge's fill is one fraction; it has no composed string to show). Omitted from the wire when null.

source.description: A Frame element's sampled frame — the same WorldFrameSource vocabulary a screen row or probe socket plugs into (camera/view/probe/capture). Required for Frame; refused on every other kind. Omitted from the wire when null.

fit.description: A Frame element's aspect-fit policy. Ignored for every other kind. Omitted from the wire at its default (Cover).
fit.title: SourceFit

mirror.description: Whether a Frame element flips its sampled frame horizontally — a face cam is conventionally mirrored. Ignored for every other kind. Omitted from the wire at its default (false).

radius.description: A Frame element's corner-rounding radius, in pixels. Must be finite and non-negative. Ignored for every other kind. Omitted from the wire at its default (0).

opacity.description: A Frame element's sampled-frame alpha, in [0, 1]. Ignored for every other kind.

sources.description: A Frame element's ranked source candidates — a portrait that shows the speaking character, else the webcam when the player chose it, else the seat's own avatar. Refused beside Source: a bare Source is exactly a one-entry list with no condition. At most MaxFrameCandidatesPerElement entries, every one counted toward MaxFrameSources.

fadeSeconds.description: How long a Frame element cross-fades when its winning candidate changes; 0 cuts. Finite and non-negative.

voice.description: Optional Text voice. Speaks the resolved literal, binding or template once on visible arrival or change, and stops when hidden. Both patchId and cadenceTicks are required here.

plotSamples.description: The recent samples a Plot requests; counted against the panel's bar reservation.

plotMin.description: The plot's lower bound, in the reading's units.

plotMax.description: The plot's upper bound, strictly above PlotMin.

plotReference.description: An optional constant reference line in the reading's units.

plotReferenceBinding.description: An optional reading binding for a live reference line, instead of PlotReference.

markup.description: Whether a text element's resolved text is read as markup: [wave], [shake], [caret at=3] and the other effect tags of Puck.Text style each glyph, and a placeholder may supply a tag's name or a parameter's value. Absent, brackets are ordinary text.

WorldHudElement.title: WorldHudElement

PaletteSurfaceDocument.description: An authored surface tint and reflectance.
PaletteSurfaceDocument.title: PaletteSurfaceDocument

SdfPathSegmentNullable.description: A line, quadratic/cubic Bezier, or circular arc ending at End. An arc uses ArcCenter and Clockwise; Beziers use Control and optionally Control2. Controls are in the profile's local XY frame.
SdfPathSegmentNullable.title: SdfPathSegment

SdfPathContourNullable.description: A continuous contour. Filled contours close implicitly; stroked contours remain open unless Closed.

segments.description: Gets the contour's segments in order, each ending where the next begins. The list is owned.

SdfPathContourNullable.title: SdfPathContour

SdfPathProfileNullable.description: A bounded presentation profile. Filled contours use even/odd fill, including holes. Curves are flattened once at composition, with a local-space geometric error at most Tolerance (apart from floating-point rounding). Strokes approximate the union of disks along the curve, including their varying radius, to the same tolerance. The emitted polygon/rounded-segment field is 1-Lipschitz; no margin moves its zero surface. At most 128 edges are emitted; exceeding that budget refuses instead of silently relaxing the requested tolerance.

contours.description: Gets the profile's contours, filled with even/odd fill. The list is owned, since Compile caches its edges by the profile.

SdfPathProfileNullable.title: SdfPathProfile

SdfPrismProfileNullable.description: Authored profile controls for a solid prism. The profile is extruded along local Z.

cornerRadius.description: A fraction in [0, 1]: the profile's smaller half-extent for RoundedRectangle's corner radius or ChamferedRectangle's chamfer radius; the scaled polygon's conservative inradius (ConvexPolygonInradius) for Convex's uniform corner rounding, also clamped to the extrusion half-depth when extruded.

path.description: Required only for Path; its points are normalized profile coordinates.

vertices.description: Gets, for Convex only, 3 to MaxConvexVertices local XY points, clockwise (X right, Y up — each turn's 2D cross product of consecutive edges strictly negative), no coincident or collinear vertices, and convex. Ignored by every other kind. The list is owned.

SdfPrismProfileNullable.title: SdfPrismProfile

WorldFieldWriteOp.description: How a transform writes a field cell.
WorldFieldWriteOp.title: WorldFieldWriteOp

ActionTarget.description: The participant an action effect addresses. A document-scope rule has no participant to select, so only Self is admitted there; the other members belong to a host's per-participant action programs, which share the SetState/AddState shapes with the rule compiler and therefore carry the member on the wire.
ActionTarget.title: ActionTarget

x-enumDescriptions.ProducerTarget: The target selected by the participant's active producer.
x-enumDescriptions.AffectingSubject: The participant that applied the recipient's most recent targeted effect.

ActionEffectSetState.description: Writes a named state cell — a state-section row's cell at rule scope, a counter slot inside a host's per-participant action program.

state.description: The state row name (or the host's counter slot).

value.description: The literal value to write, or null when FromState spells a live operand to copy instead — exactly one of the source spellings is authored (refused by name when both or neither are present, the same duality CompareState's own comparand carries).

target.description: The addressed participant — meaningful only inside a host's per-participant program; a non-Self target is refused at rule scope, where there is no participant to select.

key.description: The cell inside State — null writes the row's slot cell, which a keyed row does not have (refused by name).

fromState.description: Another declared state-section row name, or a reserved channel, read live at fire time and copied in place of an authored Value — the row that resets to another row's own current value (a shadow row mirroring a counter someone else advances), never only a standing literal. Resolved through the same operand walk CompareState's own ComparandState uses; mixing a fixed row into an int destination (or the reverse) is refused by name rather than coerced.

fromKey.description: The cell inside FromState, on the same (row, key) terms as Key. Refused when FromState names a reserved channel or is absent.

valueSeconds.description: An alternative to Value for a kind=Int state row: writes the row's raw engine-tick representation of a duration rather than the duration's own numeric value. Authored in seconds — a physical unit, not a tick count, so a document's rate can change without silently retuning the written duration — and converted once at rule compile time to an exact whole engine-tick count via TryDurationEngineTicksExact, never re-derived at runtime and never rounded: a duration that is not an exact whole engine-tick count is refused rather than silently rounded away (DurationNotExactEngineTicks). Typed Decimal rather than float because JSON deserializes a number token to Decimal exactly (base-10, no binary-float intermediate), and most terminating decimals — the only ones an author can spell — have no exact binary float or fixed-point spelling either.

text.description: The literal a kind=Text state row's cell takes — the fourth spelling beside Value/FromState/ValueSeconds, exactly one authored. Every state-bound document value re-resolves on the write, so this is how a rule restyles what a state-bound document row names.

expression.description: A bounded numeric expression evaluated in the destination row's integer or fixed-point domain. Exactly one source spelling is authored.

vector.description: The base64url-encoded vector literal a vector state row's cell takes.

ActionEffectSetState.title: ActionEffectSetState

ActionEffectAddState.description: Adds to a named state cell — the same shape as SetState, here the source is the addend rather than the replacement.

state.description: The state row name (or the host's counter slot).

value.description: The literal addend, or null when FromState spells a live addend instead — see Value's remarks.

key.description: The cell inside State — see Key.

fromState.description: See FromState's remarks; here the addend is read live rather than the replacement.

fromKey.description: The cell inside FromState — see FromKey.

valueSeconds.description: See ValueSeconds's remarks; here the converted tick count is the addend rather than the replacement.

ActionEffectAddState.title: ActionEffectAddState

ActionEffectPushState.description: Pushes one numeric value into a history row's ring (see Ring), the same source spellings as SetState minus text: exactly one of Value, FromState, or Expression.

value.description: An exact decimal literal in the row's kind.

fromState.description: A state row or reserved channel read live at every firing.

fromKey.description: The cell of FromState, or null for its slot.

expression.description: A bounded numeric expression evaluated in the row's kind.

ActionEffectPushState.title: ActionEffectPushState

ZoneSelector.description: Selection of a single token from a zone.
ZoneSelector.title: ZoneSelector

x-enumDescriptions.First: Select the first cell of an ordered zone.
x-enumDescriptions.Last: Select the last cell of an ordered zone.
x-enumDescriptions.Random: Select by one draw from an explicitly named stream-draw state row.
x-enumDescriptions.Slice: Select the keyed token and every token after it in the zone — a cascade's tail, moved in order as one run (a solitaire column's run from a card to its top).

StateTransformTransfer.description: Moves selected tokens, preserving identity. A random draw advances only when the whole transfer commits.

from.description: The source zone — a zone name, or in an authored rule a live zone ($zones[<index>], an entry of the rule's Zones table selected before each firing; an index selecting none refuses the transfer by name).

to.description: The destination zone, on the same terms as From.

key.description: The token key for key or slice selection. In an authored rule this may be a dynamic key, resolved from the active store before each transfer; direct mutations carry the resolved literal.

insertFirst.description: Insert at the first position rather than the last.

draw.description: A streamDraw site for random selection; absent for other selectors.

count.description: How many tokens move in this one transfer, 1..MaxTransferCount, each selected afresh from what remains (a five-card deal is one mutation); a key selection moves exactly one, and a slice selection moves the keyed token's whole tail (its count is 1).

StateTransformTransfer.title: StateTransformTransfer

StateTransformSetRay.description: Writes the longest run a patterns row accepts, walked from the origin outward: the same prefix semantics as the $match operand's prefix facet, landed back on the board instead of read as a fact. Refuses when the accepted prefix is empty, so an author closes a run with the required symbol (a bracket capture is plus(through) . symbol(until)) rather than an unbounded one running off the board.

from.description: The origin key, excluded from the read word and the write.

direction.description: A direction in the board's topology.
direction.title: CellName

pattern.description: A patterns row over the board's own raw values (kind Int).

value.description: The replacement value written to every cell of the accepted prefix.

StateTransformSetRay.title: StateTransformSetRay

StateTransformPushRay.description: Moves one live origin token and the outward tokens selected by PushPattern one topology cell. A token selected by StopPattern blocks the whole move, including when it is also selected by PushPattern. Other occupants remain in place. The mover is the first run symbol; pushed tokens follow in ascending pool-slot order within each cell, and the first cell without a pushed token contributes its passable occupants, or Empty when physically empty, as the terminator. The whole word must match Pattern, otherwise no token moves.

pool.description: The sole pool whose live instances participate.
pool.title: CellName

cell.description: The integer field holding each token's topology cell ordinal.
cell.title: CellName

value.description: The scalar field supplying each token's pattern symbol.
value.title: CellName

from.description: The selected pool's live Cell field, which identifies the one mover; other tokens sharing its origin remain in place.

topology.description: The lattice the cell ordinals address.
topology.title: CellName

pattern.description: The pattern matched against the movable run followed by the passable or empty terminator.

pushPattern.description: The integer pattern selecting occupants that join the moving run.

stopPattern.description: The integer pattern selecting occupants that block the move.

empty.description: The explicit symbol contributed by the first unoccupied cell.

StateTransformPushRay.title: StateTransformPushRay

StateTransformShuffle.description: Reorders a row's cells by value in place by one Fisher-Yates pass over the named redrawable integer streamDraw site: n cells make n - 1 unbiased bounded selections. The cursor counts every raw word, including rejections, so reopening it reproduces the permutation.

row.description: Any ordered zone or keyed row.

draw.description: The integer streamDraw site supplying the samples.

StateTransformShuffle.title: StateTransformShuffle

SortKey.description: One numeric key of a Sort, in its declared precedence order.

row.description: The target itself for own-value sorting, or an attribute row over the zone's token domain.

descending.description: Whether the greatest value comes first under this key.

SortKey.title: SortKey

StateTransformSort.description: Stably reorders a row by numeric keys in precedence order. Naming the target row as the sole key orders its own values; otherwise the target is an ordered zone and the keys are token attributes.

row.description: A keyed or ordered numeric row for own-value sorting, or an ordered zone for attributes.

by.description: One or more distinct numeric key rows, each carrying its own direction. Attribute rows must share the zone's token domain. A sole key naming the target reads its own stored values.

StateTransformSort.title: StateTransformSort

StateTransformWriteSet.description: Writes one value into every cell of a board whose bit is set in a cell-set mask read from a state cell: the way a set built from $board:mask and the and/or/xor/not/shift/image expression ops lands back on the board. The one board-writing form for every topology of at most 64 cells; a wider topology has no transform of its own and composes through per-cell rules instead.

row.description: The board row, over a topology of at most 64 cells.

set.description: The integer row the cell-set mask is read from.

setKey.description: The cell of that row, or null for its slot cell: a literal cell key, or any dynamic key spelling a write accepts (a binding token, a registered key family, an expression key, or a $cell:<row>:<key> indirection).

value.description: The value written to every masked cell.

StateTransformWriteSet.title: StateTransformWriteSet

BoardCombineOp.description: What BoardCombine writes into its board, cell by cell. A cell is a member of a board when its value is not the board's declared empty.
BoardCombineOp.title: BoardCombineOp

x-enumDescriptions.Copy: Every cell of left, value for value, including its empty value even when the target's differs.
x-enumDescriptions.And: Members of both left and right.
x-enumDescriptions.AndNot: Members of left that are not members of right.
x-enumDescriptions.Not: Every cell that is not a member of left.
x-enumDescriptions.Shift: Each member of left moved one step along direction; a member with no neighbour that way drops — the same move boardShift makes on a 64-bit mask.
x-enumDescriptions.Image: Each member of left carried through the point-group element — the same move boardImage makes.

StateTransformBoardCombine.description: Rewrites a board from one or two boards over the same topology, cell by cell, in one journaled mutation: the set algebra $board:mask and the bit operators give a board of at most 64 cells, for a board of any size. A cell is a member when its value is not its board's empty; every member of the result is written as Value and every other cell as the board's empty.

left.description: The first source board, over the same topology; absent for Fill and Clear.

right.description: The second source board for the two-board operations.

direction.description: The direction a Shift steps along.

element.description: The point-group element an Image carries through.

value.description: The value written to every member; never the board's own empty.

StateTransformBoardCombine.title: StateTransformBoardCombine

StateTransformArrange.description: Reorders an ordered zone of at most 20 tokens into the arrangement at a Lehmer rank read from an integer cell — the inverse of $reduce:arrangementRank: rank 0 is the token domain's own order, and a rank at or past k! refuses.

from.description: The integer row the rank is read from.

fromKey.description: The cell of that row, or null for its slot cell.

StateTransformArrange.title: StateTransformArrange

StateTransformClearEnclosed.description: Clears every group of cells valued Lower..Upper beside the cell From names that has no liberty in the boundary range, writing the board's empty value over its members. The write-path twin of $board:enclosedAt, applied after the value lands.

from.description: The placed value's cell: a literal cell key, or any dynamic key spelling a write accepts.

lower.description: The enclosed range's inclusive low end; the board's empty value lies outside it.

upper.description: The enclosed range's inclusive high end.

boundaryLower.description: The liberty range's inclusive low end. Defaults to the board's empty value.

boundaryUpper.description: The liberty range's inclusive high end. Defaults to the board's empty value.

StateTransformClearEnclosed.title: StateTransformClearEnclosed

StateTransformObserve.description: Refreshes a knowledge board from its declared source and visibility mask; authority only.

row.description: A row name or literal key as plain text, or an object identifying a reserved channel, lexical pool field, or static pool field.

StateTransformObserve.title: StateTransformObserve

VectorTerm.description: One term of a Mix: a vector operand with an integer weight.

weight.description: The integer weight in [-1000, 1000] and non-zero.

StateTransformMix.description: Writes the normalized sum of 1 to MaxMixTerms weighted vector terms.

into.description: The target vector cell or slot.

StateTransformMean.description: Writes the normalized sum of every candidate cell of a table.

into.description: The target vector cell or slot.

StateTransformMean.title: StateTransformMean

StateTransformNearest.description: Writes the closest cells of a table.

query.description: The query vector cell, slot, or literal.

k.description: How many nearest results to recall.

exclude.description: Optional key to exclude from candidates.

farthest.description: Whether to rank lower scores first.

StateTransformNearest.title: StateTransformNearest

StateTransformRemember.description: Stores a vector unless the table already holds a near-duplicate.

key.description: The key to write.
