StateTransform.description: The closed set of atomic state transforms. Each folds one candidate document and journals once.
StateTransform.title: StateTransform

ActionEffectTransformState.description: Applies a bounded state transform through the ordinary mutation pipeline.
ActionEffectTransformState.title: ActionEffectTransformState

ActionEffectGenerate.description: Redraws a draw site (a state row declaring a Draw). A draw's moment is authored through the rule that fires this: a TickPeriod site redraws on an ordinary $tick-scheduled rule and a Event site on an event-gated one, so timing costs no mutation ordinal.

row.description: The draw site's row name. One name, not a (source, destination) pair: a site's source is its own facet and a site is a scalar slot, so there is nothing else to address.

ActionEffectGenerate.title: ActionEffectGenerate

ActionEffectRemoveStateCell.description: Removes one addressed cell from a declared state row.

key.description: The optional cell key.

ActionEffectRemoveStateCell.title: ActionEffectRemoveStateCell

ActionEffectScheduleState.description: Writes an absolute simulation due tick into an integer state cell. The delay is converted against the document's authored simulation rate and rounded up, so it never fires early. A companion rule compares $tick against the cell and removes it after handling, forming a bounded, document-backed scheduler.

delaySeconds.description: The non-negative delay, rounded up to simulation ticks.

key.description: The optional cell key.

ActionEffectScheduleState.title: ActionEffectScheduleState

ActionEffectTransaction.description: Applies a bounded list of effects atomically, as a savepoint inside the firing: each effect fires once, and when any refuses, the savepoint rewinds so none apply and OnFailure runs instead. The compiler refuses an empty main branch, a branch of more than MaxTransactionEffects effects, and a transaction anywhere inside another, including inside an If branch.

onFailure.description: The optional branch run after a main-branch refusal.

ActionEffectTransaction.title: ActionEffectTransaction

ActionPredicateNonNullable.description: A data-composable gate over named state. A rule fires only while its gate holds. The $type string is the JSON discriminator, the same convention every polymorphic row family uses; the arms declared here are the ones this library owns, and a document project appends its own derived arms through its own rule vocabulary (RuleVocabulary.ExtendJson) rather than by editing this list.
ActionPredicateNonNullable.title: ActionPredicate

ActionEffectIf.description: Branches on a predicate: fires Then when it holds, else Else when present. Both branches read the frame at the effect's own position, so an earlier effect's same-firing write is visible to the condition exactly as it is to a later effect's own operand. A condition that fails to evaluate (an arithmetic fault, a missing table key) runs neither branch and is reported the same way a failing top-level effect is; a false condition with no branch that fires is not a failure. An effect inside a branch that itself refuses is refused on the same terms as a top-level effect — a branch is not a transaction, though a Transaction may appear inside one when this if is not itself inside a transaction.

then.description: The branch fired when Condition holds.

else.description: The branch fired when it does not, or null to fire nothing.

ActionEffectIf.title: ActionEffectIf

ActionEffectClaim.description: Claims one lowest-free instance from a declared pool and fires Effects with Binding bound to that fresh, generation-checked instance. A full pool, an initializer refusal, or any nested effect refusal rejects this effect and rewinds the enclosing firing.

pool.description: The declared pool to claim from.

binding.description: The lexical instance name available only inside Effects.
binding.title: CellName

effects.description: The ordered initializer and body effects run under the fresh binding.

ActionEffectClaim.title: ActionEffectClaim

ActionEffectRelease.description: Releases the currently bound pool instance named by Binding. A stale or already released binding refuses the enclosing firing instead of selecting a later reclaim of the same slot.

binding.description: The lexical instance binding to release.
binding.title: CellName

ActionEffectRelease.title: ActionEffectRelease

ActionEffectForEachPool.description: Snapshots one pool's live generation-checked instances and fires Effects for each under Binding. A release or reclaim inside the body cannot make a replacement slot appear in the same sweep.

binding.description: The lexical binding available only inside Effects.
binding.title: CellName

effects.description: The ordered effects run for each snapshot instance.

ActionEffectForEachPool.title: ActionEffectForEachPool

ActionEffectClaimPair.description: Claims one pair-pool instance for two currently bound endpoint instances, then runs its body under the fresh pair binding. Endpoint handles remain generation-checked, so a released/reclaimed endpoint cannot be paired through a stale alias.

left.description: The lexical binding for the left endpoint.
left.title: CellName

right.description: The lexical binding for the right endpoint.
right.title: CellName

binding.description: The lexical binding for the fresh pair instance.
binding.title: CellName

ActionEffectClaimPair.title: ActionEffectClaimPair

ActionEffectRewindGroup.description: Restores and removes the newest retained turn of a named undo group.
ActionEffectRewindGroup.title: ActionEffectRewindGroup

WorldEffectConsumeInput.description: Consumes the named matched event range only when the enclosing rule commits.
WorldEffectConsumeInput.title: WorldEffectConsumeInput

WorldEffectSetVerticalVelocity.description: Writes a body's vertical-velocity channel (the jump launch / the surge).

velocity.description: The vertical velocity, in world units per second at the body's authored size; a body whose live scale (bodies.scale) is not one launches at this times its scale, so under the gravity that scales with it the jump rises the same number of its own heights.

key.description: The body a world rule names — an index, a $cell: indirection, or a bound key. A kit's action names none: it acts on its own body, or on Target.

target.description: The participant a kit's action addresses; a world rule refuses any but the default.

WorldEffectSetVerticalVelocity.title: WorldEffectSetVerticalVelocity

WorldEffectScaleVerticalVelocity.description: Multiplies a body's vertical velocity (the jump cut; gate on Rising).

key.description: The body a world rule names — see Key.

target.description: The participant a kit's action addresses — see Target.

WorldEffectScaleVerticalVelocity.title: WorldEffectScaleVerticalVelocity

WorldEffectPlanarImpulse.description: A timed planar velocity overlay (the dash): BodyDirection is rotated by the body's attitude at fire time and ridden as authored, never normalized, so it must be unit length, at Speed for DurationSeconds, an exact whole number of engine ticks.

bodyDirection.description: The unit direction in the body's own frame.

speed.description: The overlay's speed, in world units per second at the body's authored size, times the body's live scale.

key.description: The body a world rule names — see Key.

target.description: The participant a kit's action addresses — see Target.

useMoveDirection.description: Uses the normalized current movement command when nonzero, falling back to the authored body direction.

WorldEffectPlanarImpulse.title: WorldEffectPlanarImpulse

WorldEffectTimedMove.description: Moves a body along its launch plane and turns it through a signed relative yaw over time.

right.description: Travel to the right in body-sized world units.

forward.description: Travel forward in body-sized world units.

yawDegrees.description: Signed relative turn in degrees, in Puck's yaw convention.

durationSeconds.description: Positive duration in exact engine ticks, expressed in seconds.

curve.description: How both travel and yaw are distributed over the duration.
curve.title: BodyMotionCurve

key.description: The recipient of a world rule. A kit action supplies its own body.

WorldEffectTimedMove.title: WorldEffectTimedMove

WorldEffectStartTimer.description: Starts a named timer slot with an authored duration.
WorldEffectStartTimer.title: WorldEffectStartTimer

WorldBodyDesignationKind.description: How a rule-triggered body designation chooses its target.
WorldBodyDesignationKind.title: WorldBodyDesignationKind

WorldEffectDesignate.description: Designates a subject into a body's named target register, or clears the register. A kit's action designates into its own body the participant that last affected it; a world rule names the body with Key and the subject with TargetKey, or a world point with Placement, Position and the pointX/pointY/pointZ expressions: the same point designation body.designate <register> at:x,y,z makes, which a body program's designated or navigated target walks to.

kind.description: Whether the register is filled with a body or a point, or cleared; only a world rule clears or designates a point.

key.description: The body a world rule names — see Key.

targetKey.description: The body a world rule designates, required when Kind is Body and refused otherwise. A kit's action names none.

placement.description: For Point, the placement whose document position is the point's base (its frame composed over its parent, as every consumer reads it), read when the effect fires, so a moved placement is followed; the point is the origin when none is named.

position.description: For Point, the literal point, or its offset from Placement when one is named. Exclusive with the point expressions.

pointX.description: For Point, a fixed-point expression for the point's x axis, evaluated when the effect fires; PointY and PointZ accompany it, and together they are the point, or its offset from Placement.

pointY.description: The y axis of the computed point.

pointZ.description: The z axis of the computed point.

WorldEffectDesignate.title: WorldEffectDesignate

name.description: The cue name; see IsValidName.

key.description: The body the cue is about — a body index, a $cell: indirection, or a bound key.

argument.description: An optional integer expression, interpreted by the cue's consumer.

WorldEffectApplyRigidImpulse.description: Applies the same instantaneous world-space rigid impulse body.impulse fires (Δv = impulse / mass, through the server's rigid-body solver — never a second impulse mechanism) to a Key-addressed body, along HeadingKey's own body's forward facing, scaled by a live kind=Fixed state cell's magnitude. The cue gesture's one honest path: billiards charges MagnitudeState by hold duration and fires this on release. Refused by name when the struck body resolves to no active body or carries no 'rigid' kit facet, the heading body resolves to no active body, or the resulting impulse is not representable or exceeds the world's declared rigid speed ceiling.

key.description: The struck body reference — body:<n>, argmax:<row>/ argmin:<row>, or placement:<id> (see BodyRefVocabulary).

headingKey.description: The body reference whose forward facing supplies the impulse direction — the same reference grammar as Key.

magnitudeState.description: The declared kind=Fixed row naming the impulse's magnitude.

magnitudeKey.description: The row's cell key, or null for an unkeyed row.

WorldEffectApplyRigidImpulse.title: WorldEffectApplyRigidImpulse

WorldEffectPaintField.description: Paints one lattice field cell, or the cube of Radius around it.
WorldEffectPaintField.title: WorldEffectPaintField

WorldHudPanel.description: One HUD panel row — a stable id (unique within the section), a normalized viewport rect in screen space, which band it draws in, its chrome style, and its child elements. WorldMutation.UpsertHudPanel carries the whole row (elements included) as one cross-row transaction boundary; WorldMutation.UpsertHudElement/ WorldMutation.RemoveHudElement read-modify-write a single element within an already-declared panel.

id.description: The panel's stable id (unique within the section — the world.row.set hud.panels/world.row.remove hud.panels mutation address).

rect.description: The panel's viewport rect, normalized to screen space.

layer.description: Which band the panel draws in.

visible.description: The panel's visibility condition over presentation facts, or null for always.

elements.description: Gets the panel's child elements. Absent and empty read identically to every consumer, and the coalesce lives in the accessor so no caller grows its own; every other list-valued row member that reads absent as empty cites this one.

WorldHudPanel.title: WorldHudPanel

WorldEffectUpsertHudPanel.description: Upserts a HUD panel document row.
WorldEffectUpsertHudPanel.title: WorldEffectUpsertHudPanel

WorldEffectRemoveHudPanel.description: Removes a HUD panel document row by id.
WorldEffectRemoveHudPanel.title: WorldEffectRemoveHudPanel

WorldPlacement.description: One placement instance row — a creation asset stamped into the world by reference: transform + facets as data, addressed by its stable Id. A placement whose creation carries timeline frames is animated: it replays client-side on the render clock through the reserved dynamic-transform pool (distribution/mirror facets are static-stamp-only and reject on an animated row). A placement carrying an Inhabit facet is a live population body rather than furniture (see WorldPlacementInhabit); its declared creation eyes derive WorldCamera feeds and its declared faces derive screens (both at the delivery boundary, never written to the document).

id.description: The row's stable string id (its mutation address). It may not carry : or be exactly $each (TryValidateId).

prototypeId.description: The referenced Id (must resolve; removal of a referenced creation rejects loudly).

position.description: The opaque stored translation — a local offset when Parent is null, or relative to Parent's composed frame otherwise (see Parent). A dealt child's is its displacement from its DealSlot's offset in its template's region (LocalFrame). Exact runtime writes retain Q48.16 through serialization; geometric readers require a resolved frame. Inert (still validated and stored, but read by nothing — neither the resolve nor the renderer) when Attach is set: the row's live position is the resolved attachment, never this authored one.

yawDegrees.description: The stamp yaw about +Y, degrees — world-space when Parent is null, added to the parent's own composed yaw otherwise. Same attach caveat as Position.

scale.description: The uniform stamp scale (clamped to the placement policy envelope by validation).

distribution.description: The placement distribution, or null for a single copy. Static placements accept a Lattice, Noise, or Scatter region, each with a none fill — Lattice materializes a regular two-axis grid (PatternFor); Noise and Scatter materialize a deterministic hash-sampled instance set instead (SampledFixedOffsetsFor), the placement twin of the field lattice's own Noise/Scatter fills. Refused together with Attach.

mirror.description: The authored local reflection plane, or null for no reflected copy. Refused together with Attach.

emission.description: The placement's emission facet (a synth voice the stamp itself makes — see WorldEmission), or null for silent. Under Distribution the emission binds to the placement root only. Omitted from the wire when null. Composes with Attach: an attached row's source point rides the resolved live pose (Client.WorldAnchorPoses) instead of the row's static position, and an inactive carrier silences the emitter rather than leaving it at a stale point.

solid.description: The placement's solidity facet (see WorldSolid). Both contact providers compile the creation's emitted shapes; analytic collision uses per-primitive colliders, including exact half-spaces for planes. Omitted from the wire when null. Composes with Attach under the analytic provider only (WorldColliderSet.RefreshAttached recomputes an attached row's colliders every tick from the resolved live pose); still refused together under the field provider, which compiles every solid row's geometry once into one SDF program and never rebuilds it per tick.

inhabit.description: The inhabit facet (null = decoration), binding the row to live population bodies. Omitted from the wire when null. Refused together with Attach — a row cannot both spawn its own driven bodies and ride another body's pose.

faceSources.description: Per-instance overrides of the creation's declared faces (null = every face shows its declared default). Omitted from the wire when null. Orthogonal to Attach (a content selector, not a transform) — composes freely, like every other facet that now tracks the dynamic pose.

region.description: The placement's region facet (see WorldPlacementRegion) — a named volume the world-events feed watches for body enter/exit, or null for none. Omitted from the wire when null. Composes with Attach: an attached row's sensing sphere centers on the resolved live pose (Server.WorldEventFeed.CollectRegions) instead of the row's static position — see WorldPlacementRegion's own remarks.

attach.description: The placement's attach facet (see WorldPlacementAttach) — binds the row's resolved world pose to a live population body, or null for a static/authored transform (the default, unchanged behavior). Omitted from the wire when null.

contribution.description: The placement's contribution facet (see WorldPlacementContribution) — marks the row a host-authored slot a federation partner fills, or null for an ordinary placement. Omitted from the wire when null. Composes with every other facet: the facet governs which creation the row shows and for how long, never its transform.

respond.description: The placement's response facet (see WorldPlacementResponse) — the ordered prototype swaps a lattice-field or state-cell condition fires, or null for an ordinary placement that always shows PrototypeId. Omitted from the wire when null. Refused together with Attach, Inhabit, and FaceSources.

grip.description: The placement's grip facet (see WorldPlacementGrip) — overrides the world's default hold policy for this row's compiled surface(s), or null to inherit the world default. Omitted from the wire when null. Requires Solid (validated).

board.description: The placement's board facet (see WorldPlacementBoard) — the tabletop primitive, or null for no anchored topology. Omitted from the wire when null.

parent.description: Another placement's Id this row's frame composes over, or null for a world-space row (today's behavior, unchanged). Position/YawDegrees become this row's own LOCAL offset/heading in the parent's composed frame: the parent's resolved yaw rotates the offset before adding the parent's resolved position (the same local-offset-rotated-by-orientation convention WorldPlacementAttach already uses), and yaw adds. Resolved by WorldPlacementFrameCompilation into PlacementFrames, with cached frames only for immutable inputs and fresh frames for state-bound translations or lattice steps, which every consumer of a placement's WORLD transform reads instead of this row's own Position/YawDegrees. Validated: must name a declared placement other than itself, must not close a cycle, and that placement must carry neither a Distribution nor a Mirror (an expanded row has no single frame to compose against). Parent scale multiplies the child's local offset and resolved scale.

deal.description: The placement's deal facet (see WorldPlacementDeal) — the row is a template whose instances are dealt from a keyed state row as child placements over its own Distribution region, or null for an ordinary placement. A template renders nothing and collides with nothing itself. Omitted from the wire when null. Requires Distribution; refused together with Inhabit, Attach, Respond, Mirror, and FaceSources.

dealSlot.description: A dealt child's reserved distribution slot, independent of its editable transform. Absent on ordinary placements and templates.

spatial.description: Named occupation, clearance, and influence volumes in this placement's local frame. The compiled static-query eligibility is exposed by Unsupported; ordinary inhabit/attach/distribution facets remain legal and are reported there when they have no single static frame.

holding.description: Which of Respond's entries held at the last response sweep, one bit per entry in authored order (bit i for entry i); 0 while none holds, and always 0 on a row without Respond. The response sweep writes it, and a booting document's state entries are settled into it before admission (SettleResponses); the row shows the lowest set bit's entry, else its own authored PrototypeId (ShownPrototypeId). Refused on a row without Respond and with a bit at or past its entry count. A reader whose disclosure withholds a cell an entry reads is handed the mask without that entry's bit (Disclosed). Omitted from the wire when 0.

surface.description: Optional one-time projection of each static occurrence onto explicitly named contact surfaces.

WorldPlacement.title: WorldPlacement

WorldEffectUpsertPlacement.description: Upserts a placement document row; inside a transaction it must sit in the closing suffix.
WorldEffectUpsertPlacement.title: WorldEffectUpsertPlacement

WorldEffectRemovePlacement.description: Removes a placement document row by id; inside a transaction it must sit in the closing suffix.
WorldEffectRemovePlacement.title: WorldEffectRemovePlacement

WorldEffectSave.description: Saves the world through the host's save tap.
WorldEffectSave.title: WorldEffectSave

WorldEffectPoseCell.description: Places a body at a live cell of an anchored topology, plus an authored offset, upright or rolled.

key.description: A body reference, including placement:$each.

expression.description: The integer cell ordinal evaluated when the effect fires.

offset.description: The displacement from the cell centre, in world units.

glide.description: Whether the body moves there as continuous motion, which a client interpolates and which keeps the body's attitude, velocity and contact state, rather than a teleport that snaps it and drops them. For a rule that moves a body a short step every tick (a lift car); a long jump should teleport.

rollDegrees.description: The roll a teleport stands the body at, about its forward axis: 180 lays it upside down, as a rule turning a two-faced piece over does. A glide keeps the body's attitude and ignores it.

pitchDegrees.description: The pitch a teleport stands the body at, about its right axis: a creation authored standing on its edge (a playing card, whose face looks along its forward axis) is laid flat at 90 or -90. A glide keeps the body's attitude and ignores it.

Exactly one of Value and Expression is authored; a body driving under no identity refuses the write rather than minting one.

The register is the body's, so it crosses to another world with the body and survives a kit recompile; an anonymous seat holds one like any body. Exactly one of Value and Expression is authored. A kit writes its own registers with setState, so this arm refuses in a kit.

key.description: The body — an index, a $cell: indirection, or a bound key.
